knowledge_statements.statement_title: Submodular Set Functions and Ring-Family Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the normalized real and integer classes and states closure of the effective domain under union and intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function \(\rho:2^V\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is submodular if \(\rho(X)+\rho(Y)\geq\rho(X\cup Y)+\rho(X\cap Y)\) for all \(X,Y\subseteq V\). The class \(\mathcal S[\mathbb R]\) consists of such functions with \(\rho(\varnothing)=0\) and \(\rho(V)<+\infty\), while \(\mathcal S[\mathbb Z]\) consists of those taking values in \(\mathbb Z\cup\{+\infty\}\). If \(\rho\in\mathcal S[\mathbb R]\), then \(\operatorname{dom}\rho\) is a ring family: \(X,Y\in\operatorname{dom}\rho\Rightarrow X\cup Y,X\cap Y\in\operatorname{dom}\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Submodularity requires the values on two sets to dominate the values on their union and intersection. For a normalized extended-real submodular function, the finite-valued sets form a family closed under union and intersection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\forall X,Y\subseteq V\bigr)\ \rho(X)+\rho(Y)\geq\rho(X\cup Y)+\rho(X\cap Y);\qquad \rho\in\mathcal S[\mathbb R]\Rightarrow\bigl(X,Y\in\operatorname{dom}\rho\Rightarrow X\cup Y,X\cap Y\in\operatorname{dom}\rho\bigr)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Submodularity on a Lattice of Subsets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition using the join and meet operations of a subset lattice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal E\) be a collection of subsets of \(E\) forming a lattice under inclusion. A function \(t:\mathcal E\to\mathbb R\) is submodular on \(\mathcal E\) if, for all \(X,Y\in\mathcal E\),
\[
t(X)+t(Y)\ge t(X\vee Y)+t(X\wedge Y).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real-valued function on a lattice of subsets is submodular when its values at any two elements sum to at least its values at their lattice join and meet.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal E\subseteq 2^E\text{ is a lattice under inclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall X,Y\in\mathcal E,\quad t(X)+t(Y)\ge t(X\vee Y)+t(X\wedge Y)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Effective Domain of an Extended-Real Set Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the book's normalization and one-sided extended-value conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\rho:2^V\to\mathbb R\cup\{\pm\infty\}\), \(\operatorname{dom}\rho=\{X\subseteq V\mid -\infty<\rho(X)<+\infty\}\). The stated convention assumes \(\rho(\varnothing)=0\), \(\rho(V)\in\mathbb R\), and that \(\rho\) takes extended values of only one sign: either \(\rho:2^V\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) or \(\rho:2^V\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The effective domain is the family of subsets where the set function is finite. The book normalizes the empty-set value to zero, requires a finite ground-set value, and permits infinities of only one sign.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dom}\rho=\{X\subseteq V\mid -\infty<\rho(X)<+\infty\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Diminishing-Returns Characterization of Submodularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order discrete-difference characterization on nested subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set function \(F:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) is submodular if and only if, for all \(A,B\subseteq V\) and \(k\in V\) satisfying \(A\subseteq B\) and \(k\notin B\), \[F(A\cup\{k\})-F(A)\geq F(B\cup\{k\})-F(B).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set function is submodular exactly when adding an element outside a larger set gives no greater marginal gain than adding it to a nested smaller set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is submodular}\iff \forall A\subseteq B\subseteq V\;\forall k\in V\setminus B,\;F(A\cup\{k\})-F(A)\geq F(B\cup\{k\})-F(B).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parallel multiplication of an element
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the ground-set expansion and states preservation of submodularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let b be a set function on S, let t\in S, and let T\ne\varnothing replace t. On S'=(S\setminus\{t\})\cup T define b'(X)=b(X) when X\subseteq S'\setminus T, and b'(X)=b((X\setminus T)\cup\{t\}) when X\cap T\ne\varnothing. This operation is parallel multiplication of t. If b is submodular, then b' is submodular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel multiplication replaces one ground-set element by a nonempty set of copies. Sets avoiding the copies retain their old value, while any set meeting the copies is evaluated after replacing all encountered copies by the original element. Applied to a submodular function, the resulting function is submodular.
assumptions_latex: b\text{ is a set function on }S
b\text{ is submodular for the closure conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b'\text{ defined by the parallel-multiplication rule is submodular.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Set-function classes and paramodular pairs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions use normalized extended-real-valued set functions on a ground set, with only one infinity sign allowed for any one function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S be a ground set and normalize every set function by h(\varnothing)=0. A function h is nondecreasing when h(X)<+\infty and X\subseteq Y imply h(X)\le h(Y), nonincreasing when -h is nondecreasing, and symmetric when h(X)=h(S\setminus X) for every X\subseteq S. A singleton weight m extends modularly by \widetilde m(X)=\sum_{s\in X}m(s), satisfying \widetilde m(X)+\widetilde m(Y)=\widetilde m(X\cap Y)+\widetilde m(X\cup Y); conversely, every finite-valued normalized modular function has this form. A function b:2^S\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\} is submodular when b(X)+b(Y)\ge b(X\cap Y)+b(X\cup Y) for all X,Y\subseteq S; p is supermodular when -p is submodular, and a polymatroid function is finite-valued, nondecreasing, and submodular. A finite-valued normalized supermodular p is nonnegative on every set if and only if it is nondecreasing. If h(S) is finite, its complement is \bar h(X)=h(S)-h(S\setminus X); then \bar h(\varnothing)=0, \bar h(S)=h(S), \overline{\bar h}=h, complementation sends submodular functions to supermodular functions, and fixes modular functions. A pair (p,b) is paramodular precisely when p(\varnothing)=b(\varnothing)=0, p is supermodular, b is submodular, and b(X)-p(Y)\ge b(X\setminus Y)-p(Y\setminus X) for all X,Y\subseteq S. Finally, \{X:b(X)<+\infty\} is a ring family for every extended-valued submodular b, and extension by +\infty gives a one-to-one correspondence with finite-valued submodular functions defined on ring families.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized set functions are classified by monotonicity, symmetry, modularity, submodularity, and supermodularity. Modular functions are exactly additive singleton-weight sums in the finite-valued normalized case. A finite normalized supermodular function is nonnegative exactly when it is nondecreasing. Complementation is an involution that exchanges submodularity and supermodularity and fixes modular functions. A paramodular pair consists of a normalized supermodular lower function and normalized submodular upper function satisfying the cross-inequality for every two subsets. Extended-valued submodular functions correspond to finite-valued submodular functions on ring families by assigning positive infinity outside the family.
assumptions_latex: h(S)\in\mathbb R\text{ whenever }\bar h\text{ is used}
p,b\text{ do not simultaneously use both }+\infty\text{ and }-\infty
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (p,b)\text{ is paramodular}\iff p(\varnothing)=b(\varnothing)=0,\ p\text{ is supermodular},\ b\text{ is submodular},\ \forall X,Y\subseteq S:\ b(X)-p(Y)\ge b(X\setminus Y)-p(Y\setminus X).

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set function is submodular exactly when the marginal gain from adding k cannot increase after j has been added to the current set.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite and let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\). The function \(f\) is submodular if, for every \(A,B\subseteq V\), \[f(A)+f(B)\ge f(A\cup B)+f(A\cap B).\] Equivalently, it has diminishing marginal returns: whenever \(A\subseteq B\subseteq V\) and \(e\in V\setminus B\), \[f(A\cup\{e\})-f(A)\ge f(B\cup\{e\})-f(B).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set function is submodular when unions and intersections satisfy the submodular inequality, equivalently when each element's marginal gain decreases as the chosen set grows.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Submodular, supermodular, modular, and monotone set functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the modular representation and diminishing-marginal characterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f:\mathcal P(S)\to\mathbb R\), submodularity means \(f(T)+f(U)\ge f(T\cap U)+f(T\cup U)\) for all \(T,U\subseteq S\); supermodularity reverses this inequality, and modularity requires equality. The function is nondecreasing (respectively nonincreasing) when \(T\subseteq U\) implies \(f(T)\le f(U)\) (respectively \(f(T)\ge f(U)\)). For \(w:S\to\mathbb R\), writing \(w(U)=\sum_{s\in U}w(s)\) gives a modular set function. Conversely, every modular \(f\) has the unique representation \(f(U)=\sum_{s\in U}w(s)+\gamma\), with \(\gamma=f(\varnothing)\); thus normalized modular functions are precisely additive weight functions. Finally, with \(\delta f_x(T)=f(T\cup\{x\})-f(T)\), \(f\) is submodular if and only if \(\delta f_x\) is nonincreasing for every \(x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set function is submodular when its values satisfy the union-intersection inequality, supermodular when the inequality is reversed, and modular when equality always holds. Monotonicity is defined by inclusion. Modular functions are exactly an additive element-weight function plus a constant, uniquely so. Submodularity is equivalently diminishing marginal returns for every element.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is submodular}\iff \forall x\in S,\ \delta f_x\text{ is nonincreasing},\qquad f\text{ modular}\iff \exists!\,(w,\gamma): f(U)=\sum_{s\in U}w(s)+\gamma.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Discrete separation theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of a supermodular lower set function and a submodular upper set function by a modular function, including the integral case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $S$ be a ground set, let $p^*:2^S\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}$ be supermodular, and let $b^*:2^S\to\mathbb R\cup\{\infty\}$ be submodular, with $p^*(\varnothing)=b^*(\varnothing)=0$. Writing $\widetilde m(X)=\sum_{s\in X}m(s)$, there exists $m:S\to\mathbb R$ such that $p^*\leq\widetilde m\leq b^*$ if and only if $p^*\leq b^*$. If $p^*$ and $b^*$ are integer-valued and $p^*\leq b^*$, then $m$ may be chosen integer-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For normalized supermodular and submodular set functions on the same ground set, a modular function lies between them exactly when the lower function is pointwise at most the upper function. With integer-valued bounds, an integral separator exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists m:S\to\mathbb R:\ p^*\leq\widetilde m\leq b^*\iff p^*\leq b^*,\quad\text{with }m\text{ integral when }p^*,b^*\text{ are integer-valued}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid construction from a closure-system capacity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The minimum defining b' is taken over members of the closure system containing the queried subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal K\) be a closure system on \(S\), and let \(b:\mathcal K\to\mathbb Z_+\) be nonnegative and intersecting submodular. Define
\[
b'(Z):=\min\{b(X):Z\subseteq X\in\mathcal K\}\qquad(Z\subseteq S).
\]
Then \(b'\) is nondecreasing and intersecting submodular. Moreover,
\[
\mathcal I_{\mathcal K}(b):=\{I\subseteq S:|I\cap Y|\le b(Y)\text{ for every }Y\in\mathcal K\}
\]
satisfies the matroid independence axioms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative intersecting-submodular capacity on a closure system extends to all subsets by minimizing over containing closed sets. The extension is nondecreasing and intersecting submodular, and the subsets obeying every induced cardinality bound form the independent sets of a matroid.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal K\text{ is a closure system on }S
b:\mathcal K\to\mathbb Z_+\text{ is nonnegative and intersecting submodular}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b'\text{ is nondecreasing and intersecting submodular, and }\mathcal I_{\mathcal K}(b)\text{ is a matroid independence system.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Submodular, supermodular, and modular set and bi-set functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes extended-value conventions, restricted pair classes, normalization conventions, and the singleton representation of finite normalized modular functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set-function is \(b:2^V\to\mathbb R\cup\{\pm\infty\}\), conventionally normalized by \(b(\varnothing)=0\). It is submodular on \(X,Y\) when \(b(X)+b(Y)\ge b(X\cap Y)+b(X\cup Y)\), with the inequality deemed satisfied if a left term is \(+\infty\); it is supermodular when the reverse inequality holds, deemed satisfied if a left term is \(-\infty\). Full, intersecting, crossing, and positive variants restrict the quantified pairs accordingly. A function is modular when equality holds for every pair; if it is finite-valued and normalized, then \(b(X)=\sum_{v\in X}b(v)\). For bi-set functions, replace \(\cap,\cup\) by \(\sqcap,\sqcup\), and conventionally assign value zero to trivial bi-sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The extract defines normalized set functions and their submodular, supermodular, and modular inequalities, including extended-value conventions and full, intersecting, crossing, and positive variants. The same definitions extend to bi-sets using meet and join. Every finite normalized modular set function is the sum of its singleton values.
assumptions_latex: \text{for the additive representation, }b\text{ is finite-valued and modular}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b\text{ modular and finite-valued}\implies b(X)=\sum_{v\in X}b(v)\quad\forall X\subseteq V.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite and let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\). The function \(f\) is supermodular if, for every \(A,B\subseteq V\), \[f(A)+f(B)\le f(A\cup B)+f(A\cap B).\] Equivalently, \(-f\) is submodular, and marginal returns are increasing: if \(A\subseteq B\subseteq V\) and \(e\in V\setminus B\), then \[f(A\cup\{e\})-f(A)\le f(B\cup\{e\})-f(B).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set function is supermodular when the submodular inequality is reversed; equivalently, its negative is submodular and its marginal returns increase with the set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positively T-Intersecting Supermodular Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A relaxation of positive intersecting supermodularity relative to a distinguished subset of the ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a subset of the ground set. A set function \(p\) is positively \(T\)-intersecting supermodular if, for all subsets \(X,Y\) such that \(X\cap Y\cap T\neq\varnothing\), \(p(X)>0\), and \(p(Y)>0\), one has \[p(X)+p(Y)\le p(X\cap Y)+p(X\cup Y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set function is positively T-intersecting supermodular when the supermodular inequality is required for every pair of positive-valued sets whose intersection meets T.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p(X)+p(Y)\le p(X\cap Y)+p(X\cup Y)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Supermodular generator matroid and its corank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matroid existence and corank formula for a subcardinal intersecting-supermodular function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p:2^S\to\mathbb Z\) be intersecting supermodular and satisfy \(p(X)\le |X|\) for every \(X\subseteq S\). Then \(\mathcal G^p:=\{Z\subseteq S:|Z\cap X|\ge p(X)\text{ for every }X\subseteq S\}\) is the set of generators of a matroid \(M^p\). Moreover, \(\operatorname{corank}(M^p)=\max\{\sum_{i=1}^t p(X_i):\{X_1,\ldots,X_t\}\text{ is a subpartition of }S\}.\)
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every subcardinal intersecting-supermodular integer set function defines a matroid whose generators are the subsets satisfying all of its intersection lower bounds. The matroid's corank equals the maximum sum of p over a subpartition of the ground set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal G^p\text{ is the generator family of a matroid }M^p,\qquad \operatorname{corank}(M^p)=\max_{\{X_1,\ldots,X_t\}\text{ subpartition of }S}\sum_{i=1}^t p(X_i).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function \(\mu:2^V\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) is supermodular if \(-\mu\) is submodular. Under the stated convention, \(\mu(\varnothing)=0\) and \(\mu(V)>-\infty\); equivalently, \(-\mu\in\mathcal S[\mathbb R]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set function that may take negative-infinite values is supermodular when its negation is submodular. It is normalized at the empty set and has a finite ground-set value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mu\text{ is supermodular}\iff -\mu\in\mathcal S[\mathbb R]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Colorings covering an intersecting supermodular function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the definition, its immediate necessary condition, and the stated harmless normalizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let h be integer-valued and intersecting supermodular on S, and let k\in\mathbb Z_{>0}. A k-coloring of S covers h if every X\subseteq S contains at least h(X) distinct colors. Necessarily, h(X)\le\min\{k,|X|\} for every X\subseteq S. Without changing coverability or intersecting supermodularity, singleton values equal to 0 may be raised to 1, so one may assume h(\{v\})=1 for every v\in S; one may also take k=\max_{X\subseteq S}h(X).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A k-coloring covers h when each subset sees at least h of the colors. This requires h(X) not to exceed either k or the size of X. Zero singleton requirements may be normalized to one without affecting coverability, and k may be chosen as the maximum value of h.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{covering means }|\{\text{colors on }X\}|\ge h(X)\ (\forall X\subseteq S),\quad h(X)\le\min\{k,|X|\};\text{ w.l.o.g. }h(\{v\})=1\text{ and }k=\max_{X\subseteq S}h(X).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Covering generator system of a subcardinal supermodular function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the candidate generator family associated with an intersecting-supermodular set function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p:2^S\to\mathbb Z\) be intersecting supermodular, with \(p(\varnothing)=0\), and subcardinal: \(p(X)\le |X|\) for every \(X\subseteq S\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an integer-valued intersecting-supermodular function that vanishes at the empty set and never exceeds cardinality, its covering generator system consists of the subsets meeting every set X in at least p(X) elements. knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal G^p:=\{Z\subseteq S:|Z\cap X|\ge p(X)\ \forall X\subseteq S\}\text{ is well-defined and }S\in\mathcal G^p.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Submodular and Supermodular Functions on a Product Lattice
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The economic correspondences apply when f is interpreted as a utility function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), define \(x\vee y\) and \(x\wedge y\) componentwise. The function \(f\) is submodular if \[f(x)+f(y)\ge f(x\vee y)+f(x\wedge y)\qquad(\forall x,y\in\mathbb R^n),\] and supermodular if the reverse inequality holds for all \(x,y\in\mathbb R^n\). When \(f\) represents utility, submodularity corresponds to goods being substitutes and supermodularity to goods being complements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended-real function on R^n is submodular when its values at two points sum to at least its values at their componentwise maximum and minimum; it is supermodular when the reverse inequality holds. For utility functions these cases correspond, respectively, to substitutes and complements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is submodular}\iff f(x)+f(y)\ge f(x\vee y)+f(x\wedge y)\ \forall x,y;\quad f\text{ is supermodular}\iff f(x)+f(y)\le f(x\vee y)+f(x\wedge y)\ \forall x,y.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constrained transversal for maximum supermodular demands
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The admissible subsets simultaneously hit all maximum-demand sets and preserve the residual lower-cardinality inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let h be intersecting supermodular and satisfy h(X)\le\min\{k,|X|\} for every X\subseteq S, where k=\max_{X\subseteq S}h(X). Then there exists C\subseteq S such that C\cap Y\ne\varnothing whenever h(Y)=k, and |X\setminus C|\ge h(X)-1 for every X\subseteq S with X\cap C\ne\varnothing. The collection of all subsets C satisfying these conditions is the feasible-set family of a generalized matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: There is a subset hitting every set of maximum supermodular demand while leaving at least h(X)-1 elements outside it for every set it meets. All subsets satisfying these requirements form a generalized matroid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists C\subseteq S:\ (\forall Y\subseteq S)\,[h(Y)=k\Rightarrow C\cap Y\ne\varnothing]\ \land\ (\forall X\subseteq S)\,[X\cap C\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow|X\setminus C|\ge h(X)-1],\text{ and all such }C\text{ form a g-matroid feasible family}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique border functions for polymatroids and contra-polymatroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical envelope representations of polymatroidal polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(b\ge0\) is submodular and \(b(S)\) is finite, then \(P(b)\) is a polymatroid with unique defining border function \(b_{\mathrm{omin}}\); equivalently, \(b_{\mathrm{omin}}\) is a polymatroid function and \(P(b)=P(b_{\mathrm{omin}})\). If \(p\) is supermodular, then \(C(p)\) is a contra-polymatroid with unique border function \(p_{\mathrm{imax}}\); moreover, \(p_{\mathrm{imax}}\) is nonnegative and supermodular and \(C(p)=S'(p_{\mathrm{imax}})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative submodular function finite on the ground set defines a polymatroid whose unique border function is its outer-minimum envelope. A supermodular function defines a contra-polymatroid whose unique border function is its nonnegative supermodular inner-maximum envelope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P(b)=P(b_{\mathrm{omin}})\text{ with unique border }b_{\mathrm{omin}};\qquad C(p)=S'(p_{\mathrm{imax}})\text{ with unique nonnegative supermodular border }p_{\mathrm{imax}}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Co-rank formula for the matroid induced by p
knowledge_statements.scope_note: For the previously defined matroid M^p on S and its co-rank function t^p.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(Z\subseteq S\),\[t^p(Z)=\max\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{q}p(X_i)-\left|\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^{q}X_i\right)\setminus Z\right|:\{X_1,\ldots,X_q\}\text{ is a subpartition of }S\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every subset Z of S, the co-rank of Z in the matroid induced by p equals the maximum, over all subpartitions of S, of the sum of the p-values of their members minus the number of elements in their union that lie outside Z.
assumptions_latex: M^p\text{ is the previously defined matroid on ground set }S\text{ induced by }p.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t^p(Z)=\max_{\{X_1,\ldots,X_q\}\text{ subpartition of }S}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{q}p(X_i)-\left|\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^{q}X_i\right)\setminus Z\right|\right).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Skew supermodularity and the pair-requirement function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines skew supermodularity and a set function induced by symmetric nonnegative pair requirements on an undirected graph's vertex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A set function R:2^V\to\mathbb{R} is skew supermodular if, for every X,Y\subseteq V, at least one of
\[
R(X)+R(Y)\le R(X\cap Y)+R(X\cup Y)
\]
or
\[
R(X)+R(Y)\le R(X\setminus Y)+R(Y\setminus X)
\]
holds. Given an undirected graph G=(V,E) and a nonnegative symmetric function r:V\times V\to\mathbb{R}_{+}, define
\[
R_r(X):=\begin{cases}
0,&X\in\{\varnothing,V\},\\
\max\{r(x,y):x\in X,\ y\in V\setminus X\},&\varnothing\subset X\subset V.
\end{cases}
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set function is skew supermodular when every two subsets satisfy either the intersection–union supermodular inequality or the two-differences inequality. A nonnegative symmetric pair-requirement function r induces R_r by taking the maximum requirement crossing a nontrivial cut and assigning zero to the empty set and the full vertex set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R\text{ is skew supermodular as defined above, and }R_r(X)=0\text{ for }X\in\{\varnothing,V\}\text{ while }R_r(X)=\max_{x\in X,\,y\in V\setminus X}r(x,y)\text{ otherwise.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Contrapolymatroids, extended contrapolymatroids, and their base vectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions of the lower-bound polyhedra associated with a supermodular set function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a set function \(g:2^S\to\mathbb R\), define \[Q_g:=\{x\in\mathbb R^S:x\geq\mathbf0,\ x(U)\geq g(U)\ \text{for every }U\subseteq S\}\] and \[EQ_g:=\{x\in\mathbb R^S:x(U)\geq g(U)\ \text{for every }U\subseteq S\}.\] If \(g\) is supermodular, these are respectively its contrapolymatroid and extended contrapolymatroid. A vector \(x\in Q_g\) or \(x\in EQ_g\) is a base vector of that polyhedron when \(x(S)=g(S)\); a base vector of \(g\) means a base vector of \(EQ_g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The contrapolymatroid of a supermodular function consists of nonnegative vectors satisfying all associated lower-bound subset inequalities; the extended contrapolymatroid omits nonnegativity. A feasible vector is a base vector when its total sum equals the function value on the ground set.
assumptions_latex: g\text{ is supermodular when the named polyhedral classes are invoked}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q_g=\{x\geq0:x(U)\geq g(U)\ \forall U\subseteq S\},\quad EQ_g=\{x:x(U)\geq g(U)\ \forall U\subseteq S\},\quad x\text{ is a base vector}\iff x(S)=g(S)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Preservation of T-intersecting supermodularity under bi-set maximization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A closure construction that maximizes over elements outside the terminal set and truncates to zero outside the designated inner-set regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a bi-set function \(p_1\), define, for \(Z=(Z_O,Z_I)\),
\[p(Z):=\begin{cases}\max\{p_1(Z_O,Z_I\cup K):K\subseteq Z_O\setminus T\},&Z_I\subseteq T,\\0,&Z_I\nsubseteq T.\end{cases}\]
If \(p_1\) is \(T\)-intersecting supermodular, respectively positively \(T\)-intersecting supermodular, then \(p\) has the corresponding property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing a bi-set function over additions from the outer set outside T, and assigning zero when the inner set is not contained in T, preserves T-intersecting supermodularity and its positive variant.
assumptions_latex: p(Z)=\begin{cases}\max\{p_1(Z_O,Z_I\cup K):K\subseteq Z_O\setminus T\},&Z_I\subseteq T,\\0,&Z_I\nsubseteq T\end{cases}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\text{ is (positively) }T\text{-intersecting supermodular.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite and let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\). The function \(f\) is modular exactly when \[f(A)+f(B)=f(A\cup B)+f(A\cap B)\] for all \(A,B\subseteq V\). This holds exactly when there are weights \(w_e\in\mathbb{R}\), one for each \(e\in V\), such that \[f(S)=f(\varnothing)+\sum_{e\in S}w_e\qquad\text{for every }S\subseteq V.\] The weights are uniquely determined by \(w_e=f(\{e\})-f(\varnothing)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite set function is modular exactly when it is a constant plus the sum of fixed element weights, or equivalently when the lattice inequality always holds with equality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singleton-complement characterization of modularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization of finite-valued modular functions within the submodular class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $b:2^S\to\mathbb R$ be a finite-valued submodular function. Then $b$ is modular if and only if $$b(\{v\})+b(S\setminus\{v\})=b(S)$$ for every $v\in S$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-valued submodular set function is modular exactly when every singleton and its complement have values summing to the value of the whole ground set.
assumptions_latex: b:2^S\to\mathbb R\text{ is finite-valued and submodular}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b\text{ is modular}\iff \forall v\in S,\ b(\{v\})+b(S\setminus\{v\})=b(S).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weight representation of modular functions on ring families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents finite-valued normalized modular functions on a ring-family as restrictions of additive vertex-weight functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R\) be a ring-family on \(V\) with \(\varnothing\in\mathcal R\), and let \(h:\mathcal R\to\mathbb R\) be finite-valued and modular with \(h(\varnothing)=0\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite-valued normalized modular function defined on a ring-family containing the empty set is the restriction of an additive weight function on the ground set.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists m:V\to\mathbb R\ \forall X\in\mathcal R,\quad h(X)=\sum_{v\in X}m(v)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Additive Representation of Normalized Modular Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization of normalized modular set functions by additive element weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfy \(F(\varnothing)=0\). Then \(F\) is modular, equivalently both submodular and supermodular, if and only if there exists \(s\in\mathbb{R}^p\) such that, for every \(A\subseteq V\), \[F(A)=\sum_{k\in A}s_k.\]

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is modular}\iff \exists s\in\mathbb{R}^p\;\forall A\subseteq V,\;F(A)=\sum_{k\in A}s_k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The wall-cardinality function is a modular bi-set function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a ground set and, for every bi-set \(X=(X_O,X_I)\), define \(w(X)=|X_O-X_I|\). Then for all bi-sets \(X,Y\) on \(V\), \[w(X)+w(Y)=w(X\sqcap Y)+w(X\sqcup Y).\] Hence \(w\) is modular on the bi-set lattice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every pair of bi-sets on a common ground set, the sum of their wall sizes equals the sum of the wall sizes of their meet and join. Thus wall size is a modular bi-set function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w(X)+w(Y)=w(X\sqcap Y)+w(X\sqcup Y).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modular Sandwich Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise interpolation between ordered submodular and supermodular set functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f$ be a submodular set function and $g$ a supermodular set function on the same ground set $S$. If $f(X)\geq g(X)$ for every $X\subseteq S$, then there exists a modular set function $h$ such that $f(X)\geq h(X)\geq g(X)$ for every $X\subseteq S$. If $f$ and $g$ are integer-valued, then $h$ may be chosen integer-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a submodular set function pointwise dominates a supermodular one, there is a modular set function lying pointwise between them. When both bounding functions are integer-valued, the modular function can also be integer-valued.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists h\text{ modular such that }\forall X\subseteq S,\ f(X)\geq h(X)\geq g(X);\text{ if }f,g\text{ are integer-valued, }h\text{ may be integer-valued.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modularity classes of finite set functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real-valued set functions on the power set of a finite ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be finite and \(f:2^U\to\mathbb R\). The function \(f\) is submodular if, for all \(X,Y\subseteq U\),\[f(X\cap Y)+f(X\cup Y)\le f(X)+f(Y).\]It is supermodular if the reverse inequality holds for all \(X,Y\subseteq U\), and modular if equality holds for all \(X,Y\subseteq U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real-valued function on subsets of a finite ground set is submodular when its intersection-union sum never exceeds the sum at the two original sets, supermodular when the inequality is reversed, and modular when equality always holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}f\text{ submodular}&\iff \forall X,Y\subseteq U,\ f(X\cap Y)+f(X\cup Y)\le f(X)+f(Y),\\f\text{ supermodular}&\iff \forall X,Y\subseteq U,\ f(X\cap Y)+f(X\cup Y)\ge f(X)+f(Y),\\f\text{ modular}&\iff \forall X,Y\subseteq U,\ f(X\cap Y)+f(X\cup Y)=f(X)+f(Y).\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite and let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set function is normalized when its value at the empty set is zero. Subtracting the empty-set value normalizes any function without changing its modularity or monotonicity class.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite and let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\). The function \(f\) is nondecreasing if \(A\subseteq B\) implies \(f(A)\le f(B)\), and nonincreasing if \(A\subseteq B\) implies \(f(A)\ge f(B)\). Equivalently, with \(\Delta_e f(S)=f(S\cup\{e\})-f(S)\), nondecreasing functions satisfy \(\Delta_e f(S)\ge0\), while nonincreasing functions satisfy \(\Delta_e f(S)\le0\), for every \(S\subseteq V\) and \(e\in V\setminus S\). Functions satisfying neither predicate form the nonmonotone regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inclusion can make a set function never decrease, never increase, or behave nonmonotonically. The first two regimes are equivalently characterized by the signs of all one-element marginal increments.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Sign Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise sign classes on the entire power set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite and let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\). The function \(f\) is nonnegative if \[f(S)\ge 0\qquad\text{for every }S\subseteq V,\] and it is nonpositive if \[f(S)\le 0\qquad\text{for every }S\subseteq V.\] It is sign-changing if there exist \(A,B\subseteq V\) such that \[f(A)<0<f(B).\] A function is sign-changing exactly when it belongs to neither weak-sign class. The nonnegative and nonpositive classes intersect precisely in the identically zero function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set function is nonnegative when all its values are at least zero, nonpositive when all its values are at most zero, and sign-changing when it takes both a negative and a positive value. The two weak-sign classes overlap only at the zero function.
assumptions_latex: V\text{ is a finite ground set}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\forall S\subseteq V,\ f(S)\ge 0),\quad (\forall S\subseteq V,\ f(S)\le 0),\quad\text{or}\quad (\exists A,B\subseteq V,\ f(A)<0<f(B))

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite and suppose \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) is normalized. If \(f\) is nondecreasing, then \[f(S)\ge f(\varnothing)=0\qquad\text{for every }S\subseteq V,\] so \(f\) is nonnegative. If \(f\) is nonincreasing, then \[f(S)\le f(\varnothing)=0\qquad\text{for every }S\subseteq V,\] so \(f\) is nonpositive. Neither converse holds in general: pointwise sign restrictions alone do not order values on nested nonempty sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalization turns increasing set functions into nonnegative functions and decreasing set functions into nonpositive functions. Sign restrictions alone do not imply monotonicity.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite. A function \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) is a symmetric submodular function if it is submodular and invariant under complementation: \[f(S)=f(V\setminus S)\qquad\text{for every }S\subseteq V.\] Symmetry implies \(f(\varnothing)=f(V)\). Moreover, for any \(A,B\subseteq V\), its values depend on an unordered bipartition rather than on the choice of shore, while submodularity retains the inequality \(f(A)+f(B)\ge f(A\cup B)+f(A\cap B)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric submodular function is submodular and assigns the same value to every set and its complement, so it naturally measures an unordered bipartition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integer rectangle-covering min-max equality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the equality between minimum total nonnegative-integer rectangle-covering weight and maximum demand over an independent rectangle family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $S,T$ be finite, and let $h:\mathcal P(S)\times\mathcal P(T)\to\mathbb Z_+$ satisfy
\[
h(X_1\cap X_2,Y_1\cup Y_2)+h(X_1\cup X_2,Y_1\cap Y_2)\ge h(X_1,Y_1)+h(X_2,Y_2)
\]
whenever $X_1\cap X_2\ne\varnothing$, $Y_1\cap Y_2\ne\varnothing$, and $h(X_i,Y_i)>0$ for $i=1,2$, and suppose $h(X,Y)=0$ whenever $X=\varnothing$ or $Y=\varnothing$. Then
\[
\min_{\substack{z:S\times T\to\mathbb Z_+\\ z(X\times Y)\ge h(X,Y)\ \forall X\subseteq S,\,Y\subseteq T}}z(S\times T)
=
\max_{\mathcal F\text{ independent}}\sum_{(X,Y)\in\mathcal F}h(X,Y),
\]
where $z(X\times Y)=\sum_{(x,y)\in X\times Y}z(x,y)$ and independence means that distinct $(X_1,Y_1),(X_2,Y_2)\in\mathcal F$ have $X_1\cap X_2=\varnothing$ or $Y_1\cap Y_2=\varnothing$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonnegative-integer set-pair demand function satisfying the restricted supermodular inequality and vanishing when either set is empty, the minimum total nonnegative-integer weight that covers every Cartesian rectangle's demand equals the maximum total demand of a family of pairwise disjoint rectangles.
assumptions_latex: h\text{ satisfies the positive-intersecting supermodular inequality}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{z\in\mathbb Z_+^{S\times T}:\ z(X\times Y)\ge h(X,Y)\ \forall X,Y}z(S\times T)=\max_{\mathcal F\text{ independent}}h(\mathcal F).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Submodular and Increasing Set Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions for real-valued functions on the power set of a set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a set and \(f:2^E\to\mathbb{R}\). The function \(f\) is submodular if, for all \(X,Y\subseteq E\), \[f(X)+f(Y)\ge f(X\cup Y)+f(X\cap Y).\] It is increasing if, for all \(X,Y\subseteq E\), \(X\subseteq Y\) implies \(f(X)\le f(Y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a set E and a real-valued function f on its subsets, f is submodular when the sum of its values on any two subsets is at least the sum of its values on their union and intersection. It is increasing when inclusion of subsets never decreases its value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[f\text{ is submodular}\iff (\forall X,Y\subseteq E)\ f(X)+f(Y)\ge f(X\cup Y)+f(X\cap Y)\bigr],\quad \bigl[f\text{ is increasing}\iff (\forall X,Y\subseteq E)\ X\subseteq Y\Rightarrow f(X)\le f(Y)\bigr].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hypergraph and dypergraph cut-function identities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes all three identities and the resulting submodularity and supermodularity classifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every hypergraph \(H\) and all \(X,Y\subseteq V(H)\), \[i_H(X)+i_H(Y)=i_H(X\cap Y)+i_H(X\cup Y)-d_H(X,Y),\] \[p_H(X)+p_H(Y)=p_H(X\cap Y)+p_H(X\cup Y)-d_H^*(X,Y).\] For every dypergraph \(D\) and all \(X,Y\subseteq V(D)\), \[\varrho_D(X)+\varrho_D(Y)=\varrho_D(X\cap Y)+\varrho_D(X\cup Y)+d_D(X,Y).\] Consequently, \(d_H,e_H,\varrho_D,\delta_D\) are submodular, whereas \(i_H,p_H\) are supermodular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hypergraph incidence and partition functions satisfy exact intersection-union identities with correction terms, and the analogous in-degree identity holds for dypergraphs. The functions d_H, e_H, rho_D, and delta_D are submodular, while i_H and p_H are supermodular.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a hypergraph and \(X,Y\subseteq V(H)\) in the first two identities.
\(D\) is a dypergraph and \(X,Y\subseteq V(D)\) in the third identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_H,e_H,\varrho_D,\delta_D\text{ are submodular, and }i_H,p_H\text{ are supermodular.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Symmetric submodular functions and nontrivial minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines symmetric submodularity and identifies the boundary that makes its minimization problem nontrivial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A submodular function \(f:2^U\to\mathbb{R}\) is symmetric if \(f(A)=f(U\setminus A)\) for every \(A\subseteq U\). Every such function satisfies \(f(\varnothing)=f(U)\le f(A)\) for all \(A\subseteq U\). Hence unrestricted minimization is trivial, and the nontrivial problem minimizes \(f(A)\) over \(\varnothing\ne A\subsetneq U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A submodular set function is symmetric when every set and its complement have equal values. The empty set and the whole ground set are global minimizers, so the nontrivial minimization problem is restricted to nonempty proper subsets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(\varnothing)=f(U)\le f(A)\quad\forall A\subseteq U;\qquad \min_{\varnothing\ne A\subsetneq U}f(A)\text{ is the nontrivial variant.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complement-symmetry definition together with its elementary consequence for unrestricted minimization of a submodular function.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-intersecting supermodularity and independent rectangle families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the restricted lattice inequality, independence of set pairs, and the sum notation used for rectangle-covering results.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $S,T$ be finite and $h:\mathcal P(S)\times\mathcal P(T)\to\mathbb R$. The positive-intersecting supermodular condition is
\[
h(X_1\cap X_2,Y_1\cup Y_2)+h(X_1\cup X_2,Y_1\cap Y_2)\ge h(X_1,Y_1)+h(X_2,Y_2)
\]
whenever $X_1\cap X_2\ne\varnothing$, $Y_1\cap Y_2\ne\varnothing$, and $h(X_i,Y_i)>0$ for $i=1,2$. A family $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal P(S)\times\mathcal P(T)$ is independent when every two distinct $(X_1,Y_1),(X_2,Y_2)\in\mathcal F$ satisfy $X_1\cap X_2=\varnothing$ or $Y_1\cap Y_2=\varnothing$; equivalently, the rectangles $X\times Y$ indexed by $\mathcal F$ are pairwise disjoint. Define $h(\mathcal F)=\sum_{(X,Y)\in\mathcal F}h(X,Y)$ and, for $z:S\times T\to\mathbb R$, define $z(X\times Y)=\sum_{(x,y)\in X\times Y}z(x,y)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finite sets S and T, the function h obeys the stated supermodular inequality whenever both coordinate intersections are nonempty and both original function values are positive. A family of set pairs is independent exactly when its associated Cartesian-product rectangles are pairwise disjoint. The displayed sums define h on such a family and z on a rectangle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: h(X_1\cap X_2,Y_1\cup Y_2)+h(X_1\cup X_2,Y_1\cap Y_2)\ge h(X_1,Y_1)+h(X_2,Y_2),\quad \mathcal F\text{ independent}\iff\{X\times Y:(X,Y)\in\mathcal F\}\text{ is pairwise disjoint}.

A set function \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) is integer-valued if \[f(S)\in\mathbb{Z}\qquad\text{for every }S\subseteq V.\] Integer-valuedness is an arithmetic restriction independent of submodularity, supermodularity, modularity, normalization, and monotonicity. Thus an integer-valued submodular function is precisely a function satisfying both the pointwise integrality condition and the submodular lattice inequality; neither condition alone implies the other.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integer-valued set function takes an integer value on every subset. This arithmetic condition can be combined independently with submodularity, normalization, monotonicity, and related classes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Separation of intersecting supermodular and submodular functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and integrality of a modular separator under the subpartition compatibility condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $p$ and $b$ be, respectively, intersecting supermodular and intersecting submodular functions on a ground set $S$. There exists $m:S\to\mathbb R$ with $p\leq\widetilde m\leq b$ if and only if $p^{\wedge}\leq b^{\vee}$. Equivalently, for every two subpartitions $\{X_i\}$ and $\{Y_j\}$ of $S$ satisfying $\bigcup_iX_i=\bigcup_jY_j$, one has $\sum_i p(X_i)\leq\sum_j b(Y_j)$. If $p$ and $b$ are integer-valued and this condition holds, then $m$ may be chosen integer-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An intersecting supermodular lower function and an intersecting submodular upper function admit a modular separator exactly when every pair of subpartitions with the same union satisfies the corresponding sum inequality, equivalently when the full closures obey the required pointwise order. Integer-valued data admit an integral separator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists m:S\to\mathbb R:\ p\leq\widetilde m\leq b\iff p^{\wedge}\leq b^{\vee}\iff\left[\sum_i p(X_i)\leq\sum_j b(Y_j)\text{ for all subpartitions with }\bigcup_iX_i=\bigcup_jY_j\right],\text{ and integral data permit integral }m.

knowledge_statements.title: Rational-Valued Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rational codomain restriction for finite set functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite. A set function \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) is rational-valued if \[f(S)\in\mathbb{Q}\qquad\text{for every }S\subseteq V.\] Every integer-valued set function is rational-valued, but the converse fails: the constant function \[f(S)=\frac{1}{2}\qquad\text{for every }S\subseteq V\] is rational-valued and modular but not integer-valued. Rational-valuedness is otherwise independent of submodularity, monotonicity, normalization, and the weak-sign predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rational-valued set function takes rational values on every subset. Every integer-valued function is rational-valued, while the constant modular function with value one half shows that the converse fails.
assumptions_latex: V\text{ is a finite ground set}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(2^V)\subseteq\mathbb{Q}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite and let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{Q}\). Because \(2^V\) is finite, there exists a positive integer \(q\) divisible by the denominator of every value \(f(S)\), and hence \[(qf)(S)=qf(S)\in\mathbb{Z}\qquad\text{for every }S\subseteq V.\] Multiplication by any positive scalar preserves submodularity, supermodularity, modularity, both monotonicity directions, and weak sign. It also preserves normalization. Thus positive common-denominator scaling converts every rational-valued member of any such class into an integer-valued member of the same class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite ground set, one common positive denominator scales every rational-valued function to an integer-valued one while preserving modularity, monotonicity, sign, and normalization classes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Crossing-submodular flows and their polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines crossing families, crossing-submodular functions, submodular flows, and the extended-polymatroid representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D=(V,A), let \mathcal C\subseteq 2^V be crossing, meaning that T,U\in\mathcal C, T\cap U\neq\varnothing, and T\cup U\neq V imply T\cap U,T\cup U\in\mathcal C, and let f:\mathcal C\to\mathbb R be crossing submodular: f(T)+f(U)\ge f(T\cap U)+f(T\cup U) for every such pair. A submodular flow is an x\in\mathbb R^A satisfying x(\delta^{\mathrm{in}}(U))-x(\delta^{\mathrm{out}}(U))\le f(U) for every U\in\mathcal C. Its feasible set P is the submodular flow polyhedron, equivalently P=\{x\in\mathbb R^A:Mx\in EP_f\}, where M is the V\times A incidence matrix and Mx is the excess vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a crossing family and a function submodular on crossing pairs, a submodular flow satisfies the prescribed net-inflow upper bound for every set in the family. The resulting polyhedron equivalently consists of arc vectors whose incidence-matrix excess vector belongs to the extended polymatroid of the function.
assumptions_latex: \forall T,U\in\mathcal C:\ (T\cap U\neq\varnothing\land T\cup U\neq V)\Rightarrow f(T)+f(U)\ge f(T\cap U)+f(T\cup U)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^A:\forall U\in\mathcal C,\ x(\delta^{\mathrm{in}}(U))-x(\delta^{\mathrm{out}}(U))\le f(U)\right\}=\{x\in\mathbb R^A:Mx\in EP_f\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subflow feasibility theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes bounded submodular-flow feasibility separately for fully, intersecting, and crossing submodular set functions, including the integral case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(f\le g\) be functions on \(A\), and let \(b\) be a fully, intersecting, or crossing submodular set function on \(V\) with \(b(\varnothing)=b(V)=0\). A feasible submodular flow exists if and only if the corresponding condition holds: (A) if \(b\) is fully submodular, \(\varrho_f(Z)-\delta_g(Z)\le b(Z)\) for every \(Z\subseteq V\); (B) if \(b\) is intersecting submodular, \(\varrho_f(Z)-\delta_g(Z)\le\sum_i b(V_i)\) for every \(Z\subseteq V\) and every partition \(\{V_1,\ldots,V_t\}\) of \(Z\); (C) if \(b\) is crossing submodular, \(\varrho_f(Z)-\delta_g(Z)\le\sum_{X\in\mathcal F}b(X)\) for every \(Z\subseteq V\) and every tree-composition \(\mathcal F\) of \(Z\). If \(f,g,b\) are integral and a feasible subflow exists, then an integral feasible subflow exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded submodular flow is feasible exactly when its lower-bound inflow minus upper-bound outflow satisfies the appropriate cut inequality: a single-set inequality for fully submodular functions, all partition inequalities for intersecting submodular functions, and all tree-composition inequalities for crossing submodular functions. Integral data guarantee an integral feasible subflow whenever any feasible subflow exists.
assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a digraph and \(f,g:A\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(f\le g\).
\(b:2^V\to\mathbb R\) is fully, intersecting, or crossing submodular, with \(b(\varnothing)=b(V)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible submodular flow exists exactly under condition (A), (B), or (C), according to the submodularity regime; moreover, \(f,g,b\) integral implies existence of an integral feasible subflow whenever the system is feasible.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: General cross-free box-TDI model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The theorem gives sufficient conditions for the displayed bounded set-indexed system to be box-TDI.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be finite, \(n\in\mathbb Z_+\), \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal P(S)\), \(b,c\in(\mathbb R\cup\{\pm\infty\})^n\), \(f:\mathcal C\to\mathbb R\), and \(h:\mathcal C\to\{0,\pm1\}^n\). Assume: (i) for every cross-free subcollection \(\{T_1,T_2,T_3\}\subseteq\mathcal C\) and every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), there exist \(u,v\in S\) such that, for \(i=1,2,3\), \(h(T_i)_j=1\) if and only if \((u,v)\) enters \(T_i\), and \(h(T_i)_j=-1\) if and only if \((u,v)\) leaves \(T_i\); and (ii) for every crossing \(T,U\in\mathcal C\), there exist \(T',U'\in\mathcal C\), with \(T'\subset T\), such that \[f(T)+f(U)-f(T')-f(U')\geq\bigl(h(T)+h(U)-h(T')-h(U')\bigr)x\] for every \(x\) satisfying \(b\leq x\leq c\). Then the system \[b\leq x\leq c,\qquad h(T)x\leq f(T)\quad(T\in\mathcal C)\] is box-TDI.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The bounded set-indexed system is box-TDI if its coordinates admit the stated directed-arc representation on every cross-free triple and every crossing pair admits the stated uncrossing inequality throughout the box.
assumptions_latex: \text{Condition (i) holds for every cross-free three-set subcollection and coordinate}
\text{Condition (ii) holds for every crossing pair and all }x\text{ with }b\leq x\leq c
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left\{b\leq x\leq c,\ h(T)x\leq f(T)\ (T\in\mathcal C)\right\}\text{ is box-TDI}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(S\subseteq E\), define \(r_M(S)=\max\{|I|:I\subseteq S,\ I\in\mathcal I\}\). Then \(r_M(\varnothing)=0\), \(0\le r_M(S)\le |S|\), and \(S\subseteq T\) implies \(r_M(S)\le r_M(T)\). Moreover, for all \(S,T\subseteq E\), \[r_M(S)+r_M(T)\ge r_M(S\cup T)+r_M(S\cap T).\] Thus a finite matroid is represented by an integer-valued normalized, monotone, submodular set function whose value is the maximum size of an independent subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid rank assigns each set the largest size of an independent subset; it is integer-valued, normalized, monotone, submodular, and bounded by cardinality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid Induced by a Submodular Function on a Set Lattice
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matroid construction and rank formula from a nonnegative integer-valued lattice-submodular function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal E\) be a lattice of subsets of \(E\) that is closed under intersection and contains \(\varnothing\) and \(E\). Let \(f:\mathcal E\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) be submodular with \(f(\varnothing)=0\), and define
\[
\mathcal I(\mathcal E,f)=\{X\subseteq E:|X\cap T|\le f(T)\text{ for every }T\in\mathcal E\}.
\]
Then \(\mathcal I(\mathcal E,f)\) is the family of independent sets of a matroid on \(E\). For every \(X\subseteq E\), its rank is
\[
r(X)=\min\{f(T)+|X\setminus T|:T\in\mathcal E\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized, nonnegative integer-valued submodular function on an intersection-closed lattice containing the empty set and ground set induces a matroid through the stated intersection bounds. Its rank is the minimum of f(T) plus the number of elements outside T.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal E\subseteq 2^E\text{ is a lattice under inclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal I(\mathcal E,f)\text{ is a matroid independence family and }\forall X\subseteq E,\ r(X)=\min\{f(T)+|X\setminus T|:T\in\mathcal E\}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A polymatroid rank model on \(E\) is a function \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R_+\) satisfying \(f(\varnothing)=0\), \(f(S)\le f(T)\) whenever \(S\subseteq T\), and \[f(S)+f(T)\ge f(S\cup T)+f(S\cap T)\] for all \(S,T\subseteq E\). Its associated polymatroid is \[P(f)=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^E:x(S)\le f(S)\text{ for every }S\subseteq E\},\] where \(x(S)=\sum_{e\in S}x_e\). The function \(f\) is the rank function determining every subset inequality of this polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representation of Polymatroids by Unions of Matroid Flats
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization of polymatroid set functions through matroid-rank representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be a function on \(2^E\). Then \(f\) is a polymatroid if and only if there exist a matroid \(M\) and a map \(\varphi:E\to\mathcal F(M)\) into the flats of \(M\) such that, for every \(X\subseteq E\),
\[
f(X)=r_M\!\left(\bigcup_{x\in X}\varphi(x)\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set function is a polymatroid exactly when it can be represented as the matroid rank of the union of flats assigned to its ground-set elements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is a polymatroid}\iff\exists M\,\exists\varphi:E\to\mathcal F(M)\,\forall X\subseteq E,\ f(X)=r_M\left(\bigcup_{x\in X}\varphi(x)\right)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank Formula for the Matroid Induced by a Polymatroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank evaluation in the matroid associated with a polymatroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be a polymatroid on \(2^E\). For every \(X\subseteq E\), the rank of \(X\) in \(M(f)\) is
\[
r_f(X)=\min\{f(Y)+|X\setminus Y|:Y\subseteq X\}.
\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Freely Adding an Element to a Polymatroid Element
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of free addition, preservation of polymatroid structure, and order independence of repeated additions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be a polymatroid on \(2^E\), let \(x\in E\), and let \(x'\notin E\). Retain \(f\) on \(2^E\) and define, for every \(X\subseteq E\),
\[
f(X\cup\{x'\})=\begin{cases}
f(X),&f(X\cup\{x\})=f(X),\\
f(X)+1,&f(X\cup\{x\})>f(X).
\end{cases}
\]
The extended function is a polymatroid and is said to be obtained by freely adding \(x'\) to \(x\). The order of successive free additions is irrelevant; consequently, adding one corresponding copy of each element of \(E\) yields a well-defined polymatroid \(f'\) on \(E\dot\cup E'\) whose restriction to \(2^E\) is \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A copy x' is freely added to x by leaving the value at X unchanged when x adds no value to X and otherwise assigning f(X)+1. The extension remains a polymatroid, successive additions are order-independent, and adding one copy of every element gives a well-defined extension restricting to f.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f'\text{ is a polymatroid extension of }f\text{, and the described successive free additions are order-independent}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(r\) is the rank function of a matroid on \(E\) if and only if \(r(\varnothing)=0\), \(r\) is monotone and submodular, and \(0\le r(S)\le |S|\) for every \(S\subseteq E\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hypergraph and digraph induced-edge set systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Only nonempty induced edge or arc sets are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a hypergraph \(H=(V,\mathcal E)\), define
\[
\mathcal K_H:=\{I_H(X):X\subseteq V,\ I_H(X)\ne\varnothing\},
\]
where \(I_H(X)\) is the set of hyperedges induced by \(X\). For a digraph \(D=(V,A)\), define
\[
\mathcal K_D:=\{I_D(\mathbf X):\mathbf X\text{ is a bi-set on }V,\ I_D(\mathbf X)\ne\varnothing\},
\]
where an arc \(uv\) is induced by \(\mathbf X=(X_O,X_I)\) when \(u\in X_O\) and \(v\in X_I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a hypergraph, K_H consists of all nonempty sets of hyperedges induced by vertex subsets. For a digraph, K_D consists of all nonempty sets of arcs induced by bi-sets; an arc uv is induced when its tail lies in the outer set and its head lies in the inner set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal K_H=\{I_H(X):X\subseteq V,\ I_H(X)\ne\varnothing\},\qquad \mathcal K_D=\{I_D(\mathbf X):\mathbf X\text{ a bi-set},\ I_D(\mathbf X)\ne\varnothing\}.

children.title: Coverage Models
children.top_down_role: Set functions generated by weighted or unweighted coverage structure.

assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite set of selectable items and \(U\) is a finite universe.
\(C_e\subseteq U\) for each \(e\in E\), and \(a_u\ge0\) for each \(u\in U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The weighted coverage function \(f\) is normalized, monotone, and submodular.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: weighted union coverage is a canonical submodular construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite nonnegative weighted set-union coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each selected set \(S\subseteq E\), define \[f(S)=\sum_{u\in\bigcup_{e\in S}C_e}a_u.\] Equivalently, \(f(S)=\sum_{u\in U}a_u\mathbf 1\{S\cap D_u\ne\varnothing\}\), where \(D_u=\{e\in E:u\in C_e\}\). Then \(f(\varnothing)=0\), \(f\) is monotone, and for all \(S,T\subseteq E\), \[f(S)+f(T)\ge f(S\cup T)+f(S\cap T).\] Each universe element contributes once whenever at least one selected item covers it, producing diminishing marginal coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted coverage sums the weights of universe elements covered by at least one selected item and is normalized, monotone, and submodular.
knowledge_statements.title: Coverage Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted-coverage construction and its submodularity are standard and precise, but the record supplies no inspectable citation.

children.title: Facility-Location Models
children.top_down_role: Set functions generated by facility-selection and client-value structure.

assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite facility set and \(D\) is a finite client set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The facility-location objective \(F\) is normalized, monotone, and submodular.

notation.meaning: nonnegative service score of facility j for client i
facility-location value of the selected facilities

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sums of clientwise maximum service scores are canonical facility-location submodular functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite nonnegative maximum-similarity facility-location objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S\subseteq E\), define \[F(S)=\sum_{i\in D}\max_{j\in S}s_{ij},\] using the convention \(\max_{j\in\varnothing}s_{ij}=0\). Then \(F(\varnothing)=0\), \(F\) is monotone, and \(F\) is submodular. Equivalently, whenever \(A\subseteq B\subseteq E\) and \(e\in E\setminus B\), \[F(A\cup\{e\})-F(A)\ge F(B\cup\{e\})-F(B).\] The marginal value of a facility is the sum of improvements it provides beyond each client's best currently selected service score.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facility location sums each client's best score among selected facilities; nonnegative scores make this objective normalized, monotone, and submodular.
knowledge_statements.title: Facility-Location Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The maximum-service facility-location representation and diminishing-returns formula are mathematically consistent, but no authoritative source with a locator is supplied.

children.title: Coverage–Location Overlap
children.top_down_role: Shared representational territory and separation boundaries between the model families.

assumptions_latex: \(s_{ij}\ge0\) takes finitely many values for every client \(i\in D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Facility-location functions are nonnegative weighted sums of threshold-coverage functions, and binary-score facility location is exactly weighted coverage.

notation.meaning: facilities serving client i at threshold t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite layer-cake decomposition gives the coverage representation directly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite threshold decomposition linking coverage and facility location.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(i\in D\), list the distinct positive scores as \(0=t_{i,0}<t_{i,1}<\cdots<t_{i,m_i}\) and set \(C_{i,k}=\{j\in E:s_{ij}\ge t_{i,k}\}\). Then \[F(S)=\sum_{i\in D}\max_{j\in S}s_{ij}=\sum_{i\in D}\sum_{k=1}^{m_i}(t_{i,k}-t_{i,k-1})\mathbf 1\{S\cap C_{i,k}\ne\varnothing\}.\] Hence every finite nonnegative facility-location model is a weighted sum of coverage indicators. If \(s_{ij}\in\{0,a_i\}\), the formula reduces exactly to weighted coverage of clients with weights \(a_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facility location decomposes into weighted threshold-coverages; with binary service scores, it is exactly a weighted coverage function.
knowledge_statements.title: Coverage–Location Overlap

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite threshold decomposition is algebraically consistent and fits the overlap leaf, including the binary-score specialization, but it lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Entropy Models
children.top_down_role: Submodular set functions arising from entropy quantities.

assumptions_latex: \((X_e)_{e\in E}\) are jointly distributed discrete random variables on finite alphabets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The joint-entropy set function \(h(S)=H(X_S)\) is normalized, monotone, and submodular.

notation.meaning: tuple of random variables indexed by S
joint entropy as a set function

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Shannon entropy submodularity is the standard strong-subadditivity model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shannon entropy of finite-alphabet variable subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(h:2^E\to\mathbb R_+\) by \(h(S)=H(X_S)\), with \(X_\varnothing\) constant and hence \(h(\varnothing)=0\). For \(S\subseteq T\subseteq E\), \(h(S)\le h(T)\). For all \(S,T\subseteq E\), Shannon's strong subadditivity gives \[h(S)+h(T)\ge h(S\cup T)+h(S\cap T).\] Equivalently, conditioning cannot increase the marginal entropy of an additional variable. Thus joint entropies form normalized, monotone, submodular set-function models, subject to further information inequalities not shared by arbitrary polymatroid ranks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint Shannon entropy of selected finite-alphabet variables is a normalized, monotone, submodular set function, though entropy vectors satisfy additional constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Entropy Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Entropy submodularity is standard, but no source is supplied. The additional claim about information inequalities should also be sourced and qualified by the number of variables and the distinction between entropic and almost-entropic regions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Entropy and Gaussian log-determinant submodular models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete joint-entropy set functions, their symmetrization as mutual information, and the nondegenerate Gaussian log-determinant specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let V=\{1,\ldots,p\}. If X_1,\ldots,X_p are finite-valued random variables and F(A)=H(X_A), then F is nonnegative, nondecreasing, and submodular. Moreover, G(A)=F(A)+F(V\setminus A)-F(V)=I(X_A;X_{V\setminus A}) is symmetric and submodular. If X\in\mathbb R^p is Gaussian with covariance Q\succ0, then H(X_A)=\tfrac12\log\det(2\pi e\,Q_{AA}), and hence A\mapsto\log\det Q_{AA} is submodular. Discrete entropic set functions satisfy restrictions not shared by all submodular functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint entropy of subsets of finitely valued random variables is a nonnegative, nondecreasing submodular set function. Its symmetrization is the mutual information between a subset and its complement and is symmetric and submodular. For a Gaussian vector with positive-definite covariance, the principal-submatrix log-determinant function is submodular. Entropic functions obey additional restrictions beyond ordinary submodularity.
assumptions_latex: X_1,\ldots,X_p\text{ are finite-valued for the discrete-entropy claims}
X\in\mathbb R^p\text{ is Gaussian with covariance }Q\succ0\text{ for the log-determinant claim}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(A)=H(X_A)\text{ is nonnegative, nondecreasing, and submodular};\quad G(A)=I(X_A;X_{V\setminus A})\text{ is symmetric and submodular};\quad A\mapsto\log\det Q_{AA}\text{ is submodular}.

children.title: Information-Gain Models
children.top_down_role: Submodular models based on information gain and uncertainty reduction.

assumptions_latex: \(Y\) and \((X_e)_{e\in E}\) are discrete random variables on finite alphabets.
The variables \((X_e)_{e\in E}\) are conditionally independent given \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The information-gain function \(g(S)=I(Y;X_S)\) is normalized, monotone, and submodular.

notation.meaning: information gained about Y from variables indexed by S
tuple of observations indexed by S

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conditional independence makes conditional entropy modular, yielding the standard submodular information-gain model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Submodular mutual information under conditional independence of observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S\subseteq E\), define \[g(S)=I(Y;X_S)=H(X_S)-H(X_S\mid Y)=H(Y)-H(Y\mid X_S).\] Then \(g(\varnothing)=0\) and \(g\) is monotone. Conditional independence given \(Y\) implies \(H(X_S\mid Y)=\sum_{e\in S}H(X_e\mid Y)\), which is modular in \(S\). Since \(H(X_S)\) is submodular, \(g\) is submodular. Without the conditional-independence assumption, mutual information \(I(Y;X_S)\) remains monotone but need not be submodular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Information gained about a target is monotone and becomes submodular when observations are conditionally independent given that target; without this assumption submodularity can fail.

assumptions_latex: \(E\) is finite and \(A_e\) is a real symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix for each \(e\in E\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: log determinant of a positive-definite baseline plus selected positive-semidefinite increments is a standard submodular matrix model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite additive matrix increments with a positive-definite baseline.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(S\subseteq E\), define \[f(S)=\log\det\!\left(A_0+\sum_{e\in S}A_e\right)-\log\det(A_0).\] The positive-definite baseline makes every determinant positive and gives \(f(\varnothing)=0\). Nonnegative positive-semidefinite increments make \(f\) monotone. Moreover, for \(S\subseteq T\subseteq E\) and \(e\in E\setminus T\), \[f(S\cup\{e\})-f(S)\ge f(T\cup\{e\})-f(T),\] so \(f\) is submodular. This supplies a canonical matrix-valued diminishing-returns model used for information accumulation and experimental design.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normalized log determinant of a positive-definite baseline plus selected positive-semidefinite increments is a monotone submodular set function.

knowledge_statements.title: Information–Matrix Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-Gaussian information gain represented by positive-semidefinite measurement information matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the unknown vector have positive-definite prior precision \(\Lambda_0\), and let measurement \(i\in V\) contribute a positive-semidefinite information matrix \(M_i\). For \(S\subseteq V\), the Gaussian information gain is represented by
\[F(S)=\frac12\log\frac{\det\!\left(\Lambda_0+\sum_{i\in S}M_i\right)}{\det(\Lambda_0)}.\]
Thus \(F(\varnothing)=0\), and the posterior precision is \(\Lambda_S=\Lambda_0+\sum_{i\in S}M_i\). The function \(F\) is monotone and submodular: for \(A\subseteq B\subseteq V\) and \(i\notin B\), \(F(A\cup\{i\})-F(A)\ge F(B\cup\{i\})-F(B)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent Gaussian measurement information adds at the matrix level, while its log-determinant information gain forms a normalized, monotone submodular set function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(S)=\tfrac12[\log\det(\Lambda_0+\sum_{i\in S}M_i)-\log\det\Lambda_0]\) is normalized, monotone, and submodular.

notation.meaning: information matrix contributed by measurement i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation content kind fits the leaf, and the matrix formula and submodularity claim are mathematically plausible under the stated positive-definiteness and positive-semidefiniteness assumptions. However, no citation supports either the Gaussian information interpretation or the log-determinant submodularity assertion, so the record cannot be accepted at candidate-review level.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the unique partition into connected reductions and the corresponding additive representation of the submodular function.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines both minor operations and states preservation of submodularity, including the finiteness condition for contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let b be submodular on S. For T\subseteq S, the restriction b\mid T is b restricted to 2^T and is submodular. If b(T) is finite, the contraction b/T on S\setminus T is defined by (b/T)(X)=b(X\cup T)-b(T) for every X\subseteq S\setminus T; it is also submodular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting a submodular function to subsets of a chosen ground-set subset preserves submodularity. knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b\mid T\text{ and }b/T\text{ are submodular, with }(b/T)(X)=b(X\cup T)-b(T).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonization of a Submodular Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of a normalized nondecreasing submodular minorant and its base-polyhedral representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:2^V\to\mathbb{R} be submodular with F(\varnothing)=0. Define G(A)=\min_{B\supseteq A}F(B)-\min_{B\subseteq V}F(B). Then G is submodular and nondecreasing, with G(\varnothing)=0. Moreover, B(G)=B(F)\cap\{s\in\mathbb{R}^V:s\geq0\}, and G(A)\leq F(A) for every A\subseteq V.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing F over supersets of A and subtracting the global minimum produces a normalized, nondecreasing submodular function. Its base polyhedron is the nonnegative part of the original base polyhedron, and it is pointwise no larger than F.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ is submodular and nondecreasing},\quad G(\varnothing)=0,\quad B(G)=B(F)\cap\{s:s\geq0\},\quad G(A)\leq F(A)\ \forall A\subseteq V.

knowledge_statements.title: Submodular Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elimination of auxiliary ground-set elements by partial minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\) and \(U\) be disjoint finite sets, and let \(f:2^{V\cup U}\to\mathbb{R}\) be submodular. Define the reduced function on \(V\) by
\[g(S)=\min_{T\subseteq U}f(S\cup T),\qquad S\subseteq V.\]
Then \(g\) is submodular on \(2^V\). If a normalized reduction is required, replacing \(g\) by \(g-g(\varnothing)\) preserves submodularity and gives value zero at the empty set. This operation eliminates the auxiliary variables indexed by \(U\) without leaving the class of finite-valued submodular functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing a submodular function over auxiliary Boolean variables produces a submodular function on the retained variables.
assumptions_latex: \(V\cap U=\varnothing\) and both sets are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(S)=\min_{T\subseteq U}f(S\cup T)\) is submodular on \(2^V\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property content kind fits this closure result, and partial minimization over a finite auxiliary Boolean ground set does preserve submodularity. A specific authoritative source is nevertheless required to support the theorem and confirm that this operation is the intended local meaning of submodular reduction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restriction of a Submodular Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Submodularity, Lovász-extension, and polyhedral behavior under restriction to a subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:2^V\to\mathbb{R} be submodular with F(\varnothing)=0, and let A\subseteq V. Define F_A:2^A\to\mathbb{R} by F_A(B)=F(B) for B\subseteq A. Then F_A is submodular. If f is the Lovász extension of F, the Lovász extension of F_A is f_A(w_A)=f(w_A,0_{V\setminus A}). Moreover, s\in P(F_A) if and only if there exists t\in\mathbb{R}^{V\setminus A} such that (s,t)\in P(F).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restriction to a subset preserves submodularity. The restricted Lovász extension is obtained by setting outside coordinates to zero, and the restricted submodular polyhedron is the coordinate projection of the original polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_A\text{ is submodular},\quad f_A(w_A)=f(w_A,0_{V\setminus A}),\quad P(F_A)=\operatorname{proj}_A P(F).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedra of a vector reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the submodular polyhedron of a vector-reduced system and, under the superbase condition, its base polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the vector reduction $(2^E,f^x)$ of a submodular system $(\mathcal D,f)$, $P(f^x)=P(f)^x$. If $x$ is a superbase, that is, $x\in P(f^\#)$, then $B(f^x)=B(f)^x$, where $B(f)^x=\{y\mid y\in B(f),\ y\le x\}$.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Contraction of a Submodular Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Submodularity, Lovász-extension, and polyhedral behavior under contraction by a subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:2^V\to\mathbb{R} be submodular with F(\varnothing)=0, and let A\subseteq V. Define F^A:2^{V\setminus A}\to\mathbb{R} by F^A(B)=F(A\cup B)-F(A). Then F^A is submodular. If f is the Lovász extension of F, the Lovász extension of F^A is f^A(w_{V\setminus A})=f(1_A,w_{V\setminus A})-F(A). Moreover, t\in P(F^A) if and only if there exists s\in P(F) such that s(A)=F(A) and s_{V\setminus A}=t.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contraction by A preserves submodularity. Its Lovász extension fixes the A-coordinates to one and subtracts F(A), while its polyhedron is the projection of the tight face s(A)=F(A) onto the remaining coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F^A\text{ is submodular},\quad f^A(w_{V\setminus A})=f(1_A,w_{V\setminus A})-F(A),\quad P(F^A)=\operatorname{proj}_{V\setminus A}\bigl(P(F)\cap\{s:s(A)=F(A)\}\bigr).
