children.title: Ground-Set Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Restriction operations on selected portions of the ground set.

knowledge_statements.title: Ground-Set Restrictions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restriction of a set function to subsets of a retained ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) and let \(W\subseteq V\). The ground-set restriction of \(f\) to \(W\) is the function
\[f|_W:2^W\to\mathbb{R},\qquad (f|_W)(S)=f(S)\quad(S\subseteq W).\]
If \(f\) is submodular on \(2^V\), then \(f|_W\) is submodular on \(2^W\). Normalization, monotonicity, and integer-valuedness are also inherited whenever they hold for \(f\). In minor terminology, restricting to \(W\) deletes the elements of \(V\setminus W\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restriction keeps only subsets of a chosen ground set and preserves submodularity and the usual inherited properties.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((f|_W)(S)=f(S)\) defines a submodular function on \(2^W\).

notation.meaning: restriction of f to ground set W

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition content kind and restriction convention fit the leaf, and the stated inherited properties are standard and internally consistent. The record supplies no inspectable source or locator, so it requires an authoritative citation before acceptance.

children.title: Ground-Set Contractions
children.top_down_role: Contraction operations relative to fixed ground-set elements.

knowledge_statements.title: Ground-Set Contractions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized contraction by conditioning a set function on a fixed subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) and fix \(C\subseteq V\). The contraction of \(f\) by \(C\) is the function on \(V\setminus C\) defined by
\[(f/C)(S)=f(S\cup C)-f(C),\qquad S\subseteq V\setminus C.\]
If \(f\) is submodular, then \(f/C\) is submodular, since adjoining the same fixed set preserves the submodular inequality. Moreover, \((f/C)(\varnothing)=0\), regardless of whether \(f\) was normalized. Monotonicity and integer-valuedness are inherited when present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contraction fixes a subset as already selected, subtracts its value, and yields a normalized submodular function on the remaining elements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((f/C)(S)=f(S\cup C)-f(C)\) is normalized and submodular on \(2^{V\setminus C}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition content kind fits the leaf, and the normalized contraction formula correctly preserves submodularity, monotonicity, and integer-valuedness. Because contraction normalization conventions vary, an authoritative source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Minor-Type Relations
children.top_down_role: Structural relations generated by successive restrictions and contractions.

knowledge_statements.title: Minor-Type Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minor relation generated by ground-set deletion and contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a submodular function \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\), choose disjoint sets \(C,D\subseteq V\) and put \(W=V\setminus(C\cup D)\). A normalized minor of \(f\) obtained by contracting \(C\) and deleting \(D\) is the function \(g:2^W\to\mathbb{R}\) given by
\[g(S)=f(S\cup C)-f(C),\qquad S\subseteq W.\]
The result is submodular. The minor-type relation is reflexive and transitive: any finite sequence of restrictions and contractions can be consolidated into disjoint contracted and deleted sets, up to the additive normalization used above.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A submodular minor results from contracting some elements and deleting others; such operations preserve submodularity and compose transitively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(S)=f(S\cup C)-f(C)\) is a submodular minor on \(V\setminus(C\cup D)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition content kind fits a minor-type relation, and the displayed deletion-contraction form is coherent with the prerequisite records. The normalization convention and the reflexive, transitive, and consolidation claims have no cited support and require an authoritative source.

children.title: Function Translations
children.top_down_role: Translations of function values or arguments within submodular systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Function Translations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertical translation of a set function by a constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) be submodular and let \(c\in\mathbb{R}\). Define the vertical translation \(g:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) by
\[g(S)=f(S)+c,	\qquad S\subseteq V.\]
Then \(g\) is submodular, because the two copies of \(c\) cancel from every submodular inequality. All marginal differences are unchanged: for \(S\subseteq V\) and \(i\notin S\), \(g(S\cup\{i\})-g(S)=f(S\cup\{i\})-f(S)\). Translation preserves minimizers and maximizers but preserves normalization only when \(c=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding one constant to every function value preserves submodularity, marginal values, and optimizers, though generally not normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g=f+c\) is submodular and has the same marginal differences and optimizers as \(f\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property content kind fits the stated invariance result, and vertical translation preserves submodularity, marginals, and optimizer sets as claimed. A source is needed both for the result and to confirm that vertical translation, rather than another translation operation, is the intended local sense of the title.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-valued extension of an extended-real submodular function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preserves every finite value while making all formerly infinite-domain values arbitrarily large.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $b$ be submodular and let $\mathcal F:=\{Z\subseteq S:b(Z)<\infty\}$. For every prescribed integer $K\ge0$, there exists a finite-valued submodular function $b'$ such that $b'(Z)=b(Z)$ for every $Z\in\mathcal F$ and $b'(Z)\ge K$ for every $Z\notin\mathcal F$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every extended-real submodular function can be replaced by a finite-valued submodular function that agrees on its finite domain and takes any prescribed large lower bound outside that domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists b'\text{ finite-valued and submodular such that }b'|_{\mathcal F}=b|_{\mathcal F}\text{ and }b'(Z)\ge K\ \forall Z\notin\mathcal F

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Upper-box intersection theorem for submodular polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers submodular polyhedra, polymatroids, and the nonempty base-polyhedron case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $b$ be submodular and $g:S\to\mathbb R\cup\{\infty\}$. Then $S(b)\cap T(\le g)=S(b\bigtriangledown g)$, and $b\bigtriangledown g$ is its unique submodular border function. If $b$ is a polymatroid function and $g\ge0$, then $P(b)\cap T(\le g)=P(b\bigtriangledown g)$. If additionally $b(S)<\infty$ and $(b\bigtriangledown g)(S)=b(S)$, then $B(b)\cap T(\le g)$ is nonempty and equals $B(b\bigtriangledown g)$, whose upper border function is $b\bigtriangledown g$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting a submodular polyhedron with coordinate-wise upper bounds preserves submodular-polyhedron structure, with border function given by the indicated convolution. The analogous polymatroid result holds for nonnegative bounds, and equality at the ground set yields a nonempty base-polyhedron intersection.
assumptions_latex: \text{For the polymatroid conclusion: }b\text{ is a polymatroid function and }g\ge0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S(b)\cap T(\le g)=S(b\bigtriangledown g);\quad P(b)\cap T(\le g)=P(b\bigtriangledown g);\quad B(b)\cap T(\le g)=B(b\bigtriangledown g)\ne\varnothing\text{ under their respective assumptions}

children.title: Submodular Sums
children.top_down_role: Additive combinations of submodular functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Submodular Sums
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of submodular functions under nonnegative linear combinations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_j:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) be submodular for \(j=1,\ldots,m\), and let \(\lambda_j\ge0\). Then
\[F(S)=\sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_j f_j(S),\qquad S\subseteq V,\]
is submodular. If every \(f_j\) is normalized, monotone, or integer-valued, then \(F\) is respectively normalized, monotone, or integer-valued in the last case when every \(\lambda_j\) is a nonnegative integer. Allowing a negative coefficient does not preserve submodularity in general, because it reverses the corresponding submodular inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonnegative linear combination of submodular functions on the same ground set is submodular; negative weights can destroy the property.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_j f_j\) is submodular.

notation.meaning: weighted sum of the component functions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property content kind fits the closure statement. The nonnegative-combination result, the qualifications concerning monotonicity and integer values, and the warning about negative coefficients are mathematically consistent, but no inspectable source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Decomposable Submodular Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The component property called “simple” is source-relative and is not defined in this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A submodular function \(F\) on \(2^V\) is decomposable if there exist submodular functions \(F_1,\ldots,F_r\), regarded as simple components, such that \[\forall A\subseteq V,\qquad F(A)=\sum_{i=1}^{r}F_i(A).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A submodular function is decomposable when it is the pointwise sum of finitely many submodular component functions regarded as simple.
assumptions_latex: F_i\text{ is a submodular function on }2^V\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,r
F_1,\ldots,F_r\text{ belong to a source-dependent class regarded as simple}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall A\subseteq V,\quad F(A)=\sum_{i=1}^{r}F_i(A)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible submodular-flow characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient cut inequalities for bounded submodular flows, with an integral existence clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(f,g:A\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(f\le g\), and let \(b:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be submodular with \(b(V)=0\). There exists \(x:A\to\mathbb R\) such that \(f\le x\le g\) and \(\varrho_x(Z)-\delta_x(Z)\le b(Z)\) for every \(Z\subseteq V\) if and only if \(\varrho_f(Z)-\delta_g(Z)\le b(Z)\) for every \(Z\subseteq V\). If \(f\), \(g\), and \(b\) are integral, these inequalities imply the existence of an integral \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded submodular flow exists exactly when every vertex subset satisfies the corresponding lower-inflow versus upper-outflow inequality determined by the submodular function. Integral data guarantee an integral feasible flow.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists x:A\to\mathbb R:\ f\le x\le g,\ \forall Z\subseteq V,\ \varrho_x(Z)-\delta_x(Z)\le b(Z)\iff \forall Z\subseteq V,\ \varrho_f(Z)-\delta_g(Z)\le b(Z);\quad f,g,b\text{ integral}\implies\exists x\text{ integral}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial-Time Crossing-Closure Decomposition of a Threshold Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive incidence-vector decomposition for a threshold level set of a positive weighted family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite, let \(U_1,\ldots,U_t\subseteq V\), let \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_t\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\), and let \(T\subseteq V\) satisfy \(T=\{x\in V:(\sum_{i=1}^t\lambda_i\chi^{U_i})_x\geq\mu\}\) for some \(\mu\in\mathbb Q\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transformation to a nondecreasing submodular function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A modular perturbation formed from full-set marginal gains converts a normalized submodular function into a nondecreasing submodular function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be submodular with \(F(\varnothing)=0\). For every \(k\in V\), define \(s_k=F(V)-F(V\setminus\{k\})\), let \(s(A)=\sum_{k\in A}s_k\), and set \(G(A)=F(A)-s(A)\). Then \(G\) is submodular and nondecreasing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting the modular function whose coefficients are the elements' marginal gains at the full ground set produces a nondecreasing submodular function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ is submodular and }\forall A\subseteq B\subseteq V,\ G(A)\le G(B)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full-set marginal perturbation yields monotonicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A particular constant and modular perturbation preserves submodularity and makes the resulting function monotone nondecreasing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $U$ be finite, let $f:2^U\to\mathbb R$ be submodular, and let $\beta\in\mathbb R$. Define $g:2^U\to\mathbb R$ by
\[
g(X)=f(X)-\beta+\sum_{e\in X}\bigl(f(U\setminus\{e\})-f(U)\bigr).
\]
Then $g$ is submodular and monotone nondecreasing.

children.title: Modular Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Modification of submodular functions by modular terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Modular Perturbations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Addition of a modular function to a submodular function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) be submodular and let \(m\) be modular, equivalently
\[m(S)=c+\sum_{i\in S}w_i\]
for constants \(c,w_i\in\mathbb{R}\). Then \(g=f+m\) is submodular. More precisely, its submodular slack is unchanged:
\[g(A)+g(B)-g(A\cup B)-g(A\cap B)=f(A)+f(B)-f(A\cup B)-f(A\cap B).\]
Thus modular perturbations preserve every submodular inequality, although arbitrary weights \(w_i\) can change monotonicity and the sets minimizing or maximizing the function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding element weights and a constant leaves all submodular slacks unchanged, but may alter monotonicity and optimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f+m\) is submodular and has the same submodular slack as \(f\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property content kind fits the leaf, and addition of a modular function leaves every submodular slack unchanged. The notation and qualifications are consistent, but an authoritative citation with a specific locator is absent.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Chain Independence of Minors Induced by a Modular Sublattice
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The result concerns the collection of consecutive minors obtained from a maximal chain in a sublattice on which the submodular function is modular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal D,f)\) be a submodular system on \(E\), and suppose that \(f\) is modular on a sublattice \(\mathcal D_0\subseteq\mathcal D\) containing \(\varnothing\) and \(E\). For any maximal chain \(\varnothing=S_0\subset S_1\subset\cdots\subset S_k=E\) of \(\mathcal D_0\), the collection \[\left\{(\mathcal D,f)\cdot S_i/S_{i-1}:i=1,\ldots,k\right\}\] is independent of the chosen maximal chain of \(\mathcal D_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a submodular function is modular on a sublattice containing the empty and ground sets, the collection of consecutive minors induced by a maximal chain of that sublattice does not depend on which maximal chain is selected.

\mathcal D_0\subseteq\mathcal D\text{ is a sublattice with }\varnothing,E\in\mathcal D_0

children.title: Perturbation Equivalence Classes
children.top_down_role: Structural equivalence induced by translations and modular modifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Perturbation Equivalence Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of set functions modulo additive modular terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For functions \(f,g:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\), define \(f\sim g\) when \(g-f\) is modular; equivalently, there exist \(c\in\mathbb{R}\) and \(w\in\mathbb{R}^V\) such that
\[g(S)=f(S)+c+\sum_{i\in S}w_i\qquad(S\subseteq V).\]
This relation is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. Functions in one equivalence class have identical submodular slacks for every pair of subsets. Consequently, either every representative is submodular or none is, although representatives need not share normalization, monotonicity, or optimizer sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two set functions are perturbation-equivalent when their difference is modular; equivalence preserves all submodular slacks and hence submodularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\sim g\iff g-f\) is modular, and \(f\) is submodular if and only if \(g\) is submodular.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition content kind fits the leaf, and equivalence modulo modular functions is an equivalence relation preserving submodular slack. The proposed equivalence convention and its consequences require a specific authoritative source before acceptance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Base-Polyhedron Representation by Full Truncation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the nonemptiness-dependent border representation and the integer-valued integrality consequence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partition Characterization of Base-Polyhedron Nonemptiness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonemptiness criteria for base polyhedra defined by near submodular or near supermodular functions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Truncations as Border Functions of Submodular and Supermodular Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral representations induced by near submodular or near supermodular set functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let b be near submodular. Then S(b) is a submodular polyhedron with fully submodular border function b^{\vee}. If b(S) is finite, B(b) is a possibly empty base-polyhedron; if \sum_i b(S_i)\geq b(S) for every partition \{S_i\} of S, its fully submodular upper border function is b^{\vee}. If additionally b\geq0, then P(b) is a polymatroid whose border function is b'(Z)=\min\left\{\sum_i b(X_i):\{X_i\}\text{ is a subpartition of }S,\ Z\subseteq\bigcup_iX_i\subseteq S\right\}. Let p be near supermodular. Then S'(p) is a supermodular polyhedron with unique fully supermodular border function p^{\wedge}. If p(S) is finite, B'(p) is a base-polyhedron; if p^{\wedge}(S)=p(S), its lower border function is p^{\wedge}. Moreover, C(p) is a contra-polymatroid with border function p'(Z)=\max\left\{\sum_i p(X_i):\{X_i\}\text{ is a subpartition of }Z\right\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near submodular and near supermodular systems admit fully semimodular border functions given by lower and upper truncation. Under the stated finiteness and ground-set conditions this extends to their base polyhedra; nonnegative lower systems yield polymatroids, while upper systems yield contra-polymatroids, with monotone truncations as border functions.
assumptions_latex: \sum_i b(S_i)\geq b(S)\text{ for every partition of }S\text{ for the upper-border assertion}
p(S)\text{ is finite for the base-polyhedron assertion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b^{\vee}\text{ and }p^{\wedge}\text{ are the stated fully submodular and supermodular border functions, while the monotone lower and upper truncations are border functions of }P(b)\text{ and }C(p),\text{ respectively.}

knowledge_statements.title: Ordinary Truncation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-capping truncation for normalized monotone submodular functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\) be normalized, monotone, and submodular, and let \(\alpha\ge0\). The ordinary truncation of \(f\) at level \(\alpha\) is
\[T_\alpha f(S)=\min\{f(S),\alpha\},\qquad S\subseteq V.\]
The function \(T_\alpha f\) is again normalized, monotone, and submodular. Its values agree with \(f\) below the truncation level and equal \(\alpha\) above it. The monotonicity hypothesis is essential for this general value-capping closure statement; capping an arbitrary submodular function need not preserve submodularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Capping a normalized monotone submodular function at a nonnegative level yields another normalized monotone submodular function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_\alpha f(S)=\min\{f(S),\alpha\}\) is normalized, monotone, and submodular.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition content kind fits ordinary value-capping truncation, and the hypotheses are sufficient for the stated closure properties. The naming convention and the claim that monotonicity is essential to the general closure statement need support from an authoritative source with a precise locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Dilworth Truncation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition-envelope truncation of an intersecting-submodular set function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfy \(f(\varnothing)=0\) and be intersecting submodular: the submodular inequality holds whenever \(A\cap B\ne\varnothing\). Its Dilworth truncation is defined by \(Df(\varnothing)=0\) and, for nonempty \(S\subseteq V\),
\[Df(S)=\min_{\mathcal P\in\Pi(S)}\sum_{X\in\mathcal P}f(X),\]
where \(\Pi(S)\) is the set of partitions of \(S\) into nonempty blocks. Then \(Df\) is fully submodular and \(Df(S)\le f(S)\). It is the greatest submodular function dominated by \(f\) that agrees with \(f\) on singleton sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dilworth truncation minimizes total block value over partitions and converts an intersecting-submodular function into a fully submodular one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Df(S)=\min_{\mathcal P\in\Pi(S)}\sum_{X\in\mathcal P}f(X)\) is submodular and satisfies \(Df\le f\).

notation.meaning: partitions of S into nonempty blocks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The partition-envelope definition is a plausible fit for the Dilworth truncation leaf, but the record also asserts full submodularity and a greatest-dominated-function characterization. Those nontrivial claims, especially the maximality clause under exactly the stated hypotheses, require an authoritative theorem-level citation before their reliability can be established.

For every set }T\text{ in the domain of the Dilworth truncation }h\text{ of }f,\ h(T)\text{ can be determined in oracle-polynomial time.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dilworth truncation, bi-truncation, and crossing-submodular slices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The truncation formulas and bi-truncation terminology refer to the preceding constructions. The constant-sum slice assertion is a separate geometric property retained with its nonemptiness condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{The partition function }f_{\mathrm p}\text{ defined for an intersecting-submodular or crossing-submodular function }f:\mathcal F\to\mathbb R\text{ by minimizing }\sum_{i\in I}f(X_i)\text{ over admissible partitions }\{X_i:i\in I\}\text{ is called the Dilworth truncation of }f.\text{ In the crossing-case construction, }\widehat f_2^{\#}\text{ is the Dilworth truncation of the intersecting-supermodular function }(f_{\mathrm p})^{\#},\text{ and }f_2\text{ is called the bi-truncation of }f.\text{ Because }B(f)=B(f^{\#}),\text{ a dual formula for }f_2\text{ can be obtained by beginning with }f^{\#}.\text{ If }f\text{ is crossing-submodular on a crossing family, }P(f)\text{ need not be a submodular polyhedron; nevertheless, for every constant }k,\ P(f)\cap\{x:x(E)=k\}\neq\varnothing\Longrightarrow P(f)\cap\{x:x(E)=k\}\text{ is a base polyhedron.}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The partition-minimum construction for an intersecting- or crossing-submodular function is called its Dilworth truncation. In the crossing-case construction, applying Dilworth truncation to the relevant dual intersecting-supermodular function yields the dual of the bi-truncation; an equivalent formula can start from the dual function because the two base polyhedra agree. A crossing-submodular polyhedron need not itself be submodular, but every nonempty constant-total-value slice of it is a base polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathcal F\to\mathbb R\text{ is intersecting-submodular or crossing-submodular on the corresponding intersecting or crossing family }\mathcal F.
\text{The terms }\widehat f_2^{\#}\text{ and }f_2\text{ use the preceding crossing-case construction.
\text{For the slice property, }f\text{ is crossing-submodular on a crossing family and }P(f)\cap\{x:x(E)=k\}\neq\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_{\mathrm p}\text{ is the Dilworth truncation of }f;\qquad f_2\text{ is the bi-truncation of }f;\qquad P(f)\cap\{x:x(E)=k\}\neq\varnothing\Longrightarrow P(f)\cap\{x:x(E)=k\}\text{ is a base polyhedron.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dilworth-truncation rank formulas and crossing-case base feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The induced systems and their notation are inherited from Theorem 2.5. The crossing-case rank formula applies only when the associated base polyhedron is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{(i) Let }f:\mathcal F\to\mathbb R\text{ be intersecting-submodular on an intersecting family }\mathcal F\subseteq2^E,\ \varnothing,E\in\mathcal F,\ f(\varnothing)=0.\text{ Define }f_{\mathrm p}(Y)=\min\left\{\sum_{i\in I}f(X_i):\{X_i:i\in I\}\text{ partitions }Y,\ X_i\in\mathcal F\right\},\text{ taking }f_{\mathrm p}(Y)=+\infty\text{ if no admissible partition exists. Then }\mathcal D_1=\{Y\subseteq E:f_{\mathrm p}(Y)<+\infty\}\text{ and }f_1=f_{\mathrm p}|_{\mathcal D_1}.\quad\text{(ii) Let }f\text{ be crossing-submodular on a crossing family }\mathcal F\subseteq2^E\text{ with the same normalization, and define }f^{\#}(X)=f(E)-f(E\setminus X)\text{ when }E\setminus X\in\mathcal F.\text{ Then }B(f)\neq\varnothing\iff f(E)=f_{\mathrm p}(E)=(f^{\#})_{\mathrm p}(E),\text{ equivalently }\sum_{j\in J}f^{\#}(Y_j)\le f(E)\le\sum_{i\in I}f(X_i)\text{ for every pair of partitions }\{X_i\}_{i\in I},\{Y_j\}_{j\in J}\text{ of }E\text{ such that }X_i\in\mathcal F\text{ and }E\setminus Y_j\in\mathcal F.\text{ If }B(f)\neq\varnothing,\text{ let }\mathcal F_{\mathrm p}=\{X\subseteq E:f_{\mathrm p}(X)<+\infty\},\ (f_{\mathrm p})^{\#}(X)=f(E)-f_{\mathrm p}(E\setminus X),\text{ and define }\widehat f_2^{\#}(Y)=\max\left\{\sum_{i\in I}(f_{\mathrm p})^{\#}(X_i):\{X_i:i\in I\}\text{ partitions }Y,\ E\setminus X_i\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm p}\right\}.\text{ Then }f_2=\widehat f_2|_{\mathcal D_2},\quad \mathcal D_2=\{X\subseteq E:\widehat f_2(X)<+\infty\},\text{ where an empty minimum is }+\infty\text{ and an empty maximum is }-\infty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a normalized intersecting-submodular function, its partition minimum is the rank function of the induced submodular system on the sets admitting an admissible partition. For a normalized crossing-submodular function, the associated base polyhedron is nonempty exactly when the primal partition minimum and dual partition maximum both equal the total value, equivalently when all admissible primal and dual partitions satisfy the stated two-sided inequality. Conditional on nonemptiness, a second dual partition construction gives the bi-truncated rank function on its finite domain.
assumptions_latex: \text{In (i), }\mathcal F\text{ is intersecting and }f\text{ is intersecting-submodular on }\mathcal F.
\text{In (ii), }\mathcal F\text{ is crossing and }f\text{ is crossing-submodular on }\mathcal F.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_1=f_{\mathrm p}|_{\mathcal D_1};\qquad B(f)\neq\varnothing\iff f(E)=f_{\mathrm p}(E)=(f^{\#})_{\mathrm p}(E);\qquad B(f)\neq\varnothing\Longrightarrow f_2=\widehat f_2|_{\mathcal D_2}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dilworth truncation of a submodular function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the partition formula and records the source's maximal characterization of the resulting function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be a submodular set function on \(S\). Its Dilworth truncation \(\widehat f:\mathcal P(S)\to\mathbb R\) is defined by \[\widehat f(U):=\min\left\{\sum_{P\in\mathcal Q}f(P)\;\middle|\;\mathcal Q\text{ is a partition of }U\text{ into nonempty sets}\right\}\quad(U\subseteq S).\] Thus \(\widehat f(\varnothing)=0\). Moreover, \(\widehat f\) is the unique largest submodular function \(g\) satisfying \(g(U)\le f(U)\) for every nonempty \(U\subseteq S\) and \(g(\varnothing)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Dilworth truncation of f is the minimum, over partitions of U into nonempty parts, of the sum of f on those parts. It is zero at the empty set and is the unique largest submodular function bounded above by f on nonempty subsets and equal to zero at the empty set.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is a submodular set function on }S
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat f(U)=\min_{\mathcal Q\text{ partition of }U\text{ into nonempty sets}}\sum_{P\in\mathcal Q}f(P),\quad \widehat f(\varnothing)=0,\quad \widehat f=\max\{g:g\text{ is submodular},\ g(\varnothing)=0,\ g(U)\le f(U)\ \forall U\ne\varnothing\}.

knowledge_statements.title: Truncation Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of ordinary and Dilworth truncations on polymatroid rank functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\) be normalized, monotone, and submodular. Because submodularity and \(f(\varnothing)=0\) imply \(f(S)\le\sum_{X\in\mathcal P}f(X)\) for every partition \(\mathcal P\) of \(S\), its Dilworth truncation satisfies \(Df=f\). Hence, for every \(\alpha\ge0\),
\[T_\alpha f(S)=\min\{f(S),\alpha\}\le Df(S)=f(S).\]
Pointwise equality holds exactly when \(f(S)\le\alpha\); equality on every subset holds exactly when \(f(V)\le\alpha\). Thus ordinary truncation may lower a polymatroid rank function, whereas unshifted Dilworth truncation does not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polymatroid rank function, Dilworth truncation changes nothing, while ordinary truncation caps values and is therefore no larger.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_\alpha f\le Df=f\), with global equality if and only if \(f(V)\le\alpha\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property content kind fits a truncation comparison. Under the record's unshifted partition-envelope definition, the conclusion that a normalized submodular function satisfies Df=f is mathematically coherent, as is the comparison with ordinary truncation. A source is still required to verify that these are the intended two truncation conventions and to support the exact equality claims.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equitable covering by a maximum of two supermodular requirements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A coloring-existence theorem for the pointwise maximum of two positively intersecting supermodular functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let \(p_1,p_2\) be positively intersecting supermodular functions on a ground set \(S\), and define \(p(X)=\max\{p_1(X),p_2(X)\}\). If \(p(X)\le \min\{k,|X|\}\) for every \(X\subseteq S\), then there exists a coloring \(c:S\to\{1,\ldots,k\}\) such that \(|c(X)|\ge p(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq S\). Moreover, it may be chosen equitable: \(\lfloor |S|/k\rfloor\le |c^{-1}(i)|\le\lceil |S|/k\rceil\) for every color \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the pointwise maximum of two positively intersecting supermodular requirements never exceeds either k or the size of the set, then the ground set has a k-coloring in which every subset sees at least its required number of colors. The color classes can all have floor or ceiling of |S|/k elements.
assumptions_latex: p_1,p_2\text{ are positively intersecting supermodular functions on }S
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists c:S\to\{1,\ldots,k\}\;\forall X\subseteq S:\ |c(X)|\ge p(X),\qquad \forall i:\ \lfloor |S|/k\rfloor\le |c^{-1}(i)|\le\lceil |S|/k\rceil.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower and Upper Partition Truncations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the paired partition-based truncations of set functions, including their pointwise bounds and conventional terminology.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a set function \(b\), its lower truncation is \[b^{\vee}(Z):=\min\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{t}b(X_i):\{X_1,\ldots,X_t\}\text{ is a partition of }Z,\ t\ge 1\right\}.\] For a set function \(p\), its upper truncation is \[p^{\wedge}(Z):=\max\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{t}p(X_i):\{X_1,\ldots,X_t\}\text{ is a partition of }Z,\ t\ge 1\right\}.\] Since the one-block partition \(\{Z\}\) is admissible, \(b^{\vee}(Z)\le b(Z)\) and \(p^{\wedge}(Z)\ge p(Z)\). Lower truncation is also called Dilworth truncation; unqualified truncation conventionally means lower truncation for submodular functions and upper truncation for supermodular functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower truncation minimizes, and upper truncation maximizes, the sum of function values over all nonempty partitions of a set. The one-block partition gives the corresponding pointwise lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b^{\vee}(Z)\le b(Z)\quad\text{and}\quad p^{\wedge}(Z)\ge p(Z).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nondecreasing Concave Composition Preserves Submodularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of nondecreasing submodular functions under nondecreasing concave scalar composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:2^V\to\mathbb{R} be nondecreasing and submodular, with F(A)\in K for every A\subseteq V, where K\subseteq\mathbb{R} is convex. If \varphi:K\to\mathbb{R} is nondecreasing and concave, then H:2^V\to\mathbb{R}, defined by H(A)=\varphi(F(A)), is submodular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composing a nondecreasing submodular set function with a nondecreasing concave scalar function preserves submodularity, provided the function's range lies in the convex domain of the scalar function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\mapsto\varphi(F(A))\text{ is submodular}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partition closure and submodular partition-sum extension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the unambiguous construction, normalization, lattice-closure, and submodularity claims. The extract's maximality paragraph has inconsistent domain symbols and is not formalized here.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }\mathcal C\subseteq2^E\text{ be intersecting and let }f:\mathcal C\to\mathbb Q\text{ be submodular on intersecting pairs. Define }\widetilde{\mathcal C}=\{T\subseteq E:T\text{ can be partitioned into members of }\mathcal C\}\text{ and }\widetilde f(T)=\min\left\{\sum_{i=1}^t f(T_i):t\geq0,\ T_i\in\mathcal C\setminus\{\varnothing\},\ T_1,\ldots,T_t\text{ partition }T\right\}.\text{ Then }\varnothing\in\widetilde{\mathcal C},\ \widetilde f(\varnothing)=0,\ \widetilde{\mathcal C}\text{ is the smallest lattice family containing }\mathcal C,\text{ and }\widetilde f\text{ is submodular on all pairs in }\widetilde{\mathcal C}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sets partitionable into members of the intersecting family form its smallest lattice-family closure. The minimum total f-value over partitions into nonempty members defines a submodular extension on that closure, with value zero at the empty set.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathcal C\to\mathbb Q\text{ is submodular on intersecting pairs}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde{\mathcal C}\text{ is the smallest lattice family containing }\mathcal C,\quad \widetilde f(\varnothing)=0,\quad\text{and }\widetilde f\text{ is submodular on }\widetilde{\mathcal C}.

knowledge_statements.title: Submodular Convolution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infimal convolution of finite-valued set functions over disjoint decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\) be finite and let \(f,g:2^V\to\mathbb R\). Their submodular convolution, or infimal convolution, is the set function \(f\mathbin{\square}g:2^V\to\mathbb R\) defined by
\[
(f\mathbin{\square}g)(X)=\min_{Y\subseteq X}\bigl(f(Y)+g(X\setminus Y)\bigr),\qquad X\subseteq V.
\]
Equivalently, the minimum ranges over ordered disjoint pairs \((Y,Z)\) satisfying \(Y\mathbin{\dot\cup}Z=X\). The term “submodular convolution” names this operation in the submodular setting; submodularity of both operands alone is not asserted to imply submodularity of the result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convolution assigns each set the minimum total cost of partitioning it into two disjoint parts evaluated by the two operand functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((f\mathbin{\square}g)(X)=\min_{Y\subseteq X}\{f(Y)+g(X\setminus Y)\}\) for every \(X\subseteq V\).

notation.meaning: infimal convolution of the two set functions
disjoint union of Y and Z

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convolution as Partition Truncation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents lower convolution through the lower partition truncation of a singleton-modified set function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(b\) be submodular on \(S\) and \(g:S\to\mathbb R\cup\{\infty\}\). For nonempty \(X\subseteq S\), define \[b'(X):=\begin{cases}b(X),&|X|\ge 2,\\ \min\{b(\{v\}),g(v)\},&X=\{v\}.\end{cases}\] Then, for every nonempty \(Z\subseteq S\), \[(b\mathbin{\triangledown}g)(Z)=(b')^{\vee}(Z).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A submodular function convolved with element weights equals the lower partition truncation of the function obtained by replacing each singleton value with the smaller of its original value and its element weight.
assumptions_latex: b\text{ is a submodular function on }S.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (b\mathbin{\triangledown}g)(Z)=(b')^{\vee}(Z).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convolution with a Modular Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Submodularity and polyhedral representation of convolution with a modular function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:2^V\to\mathbb{R} be submodular with F(\varnothing)=0, and let z\in\mathbb{R}^V, where z(S)=\sum_{i\in S}z_i. Define G(A)=\min_{B\subseteq A}\{F(B)+z(A\setminus B)\}. Then G is submodular, G(\varnothing)=0, and P(G)=P(F)\cap\{s\in\mathbb{R}^V:s\leq z\}. Moreover, G(A)\leq F(A) and G(A)\leq z(A) for every A\subseteq V.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convolution of a normalized submodular function with a modular function remains normalized and submodular. Its submodular polyhedron is the original polyhedron intersected with componentwise upper bounds, and its value does not exceed either input value on any set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ is submodular},\quad G(\varnothing)=0,\quad P(G)=P(F)\cap\{s:s\leq z\},\quad G(A)\leq F(A),\ G(A)\leq z(A)\ \forall A\subseteq V.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Submodularity of Inner and Outer Minimization Transforms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the two minimization transforms and records their monotonicity, closure, and convolution properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(b\) be a nonnegative submodular function. Define \[b_{\mathrm{imin}}(Z):=\min\{b(X):X\subseteq Z\},\qquad b_{\mathrm{omin}}(Z):=\min\{b(X):X\supseteq Z\}.\] Then \(b_{\mathrm{imin}}\) is fully submodular and nonincreasing, while \(b_{\mathrm{omin}}\) is fully submodular and nondecreasing; in particular, \(b_{\mathrm{omin}}\) is a polymatroid function. Moreover, if \(g\equiv0\), then \(b\mathbin{\triangledown}g=b_{\mathrm{imin}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing a nonnegative submodular function over subsets produces a fully submodular nonincreasing function; minimizing it over supersets produces a fully submodular nondecreasing polymatroid function. Inner minimization is convolution with zero element weights.
assumptions_latex: b\text{ is a nonnegative submodular function}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b_{\mathrm{imin}}\text{ is fully submodular and nonincreasing};\quad b_{\mathrm{omin}}\text{ is fully submodular, nondecreasing, and polymatroidal};\quad b\mathbin{\triangledown}0=b_{\mathrm{imin}}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modular convolution and coordinate truncation of a polymatroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents coordinate upper-bound truncation through convolution with a modular function and states the normalized maximality property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathcal P(S)\to\mathbb R\) be submodular and let \(a\in\mathbb R^S\). Define \[(f\mid a)(U):=\min_{T\subseteq U}\bigl(f(T)+a(U\setminus T)\bigr),\qquad U\subseteq S.\] Then \(f\mid a\) is submodular and \[EP_{f\mid a}=\{x\in EP_f:x\le a\},\qquad P_{f\mid a}=\{x\in P_f:x\le a\}.\] Consequently, intersecting an extended polymatroid or polymatroid with coordinate upper bounds again yields an extended polymatroid or polymatroid, respectively. If additionally \(f(\varnothing)=0\), then \(f\mid a\) is the unique pointwise-largest submodular function \(f'\) satisfying \(f'(\varnothing)=0\), \(f'\le f\), and \(f'(U)\le a(U)\) for every \(U\subseteq S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convolving a submodular function with an additive weight function preserves submodularity and imposes coordinate upper bounds on its associated polyhedra. Under normalization, the result is the unique pointwise-largest normalized submodular function dominated by both the original function and the additive bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\mid a\text{ is submodular},\quad EP_{f\mid a}=EP_f\cap\{x:x\le a\},\quad P_{f\mid a}=P_f\cap\{x:x\le a\};\quad f(\varnothing)=0\implies f\mid a\text{ has the stated unique pointwise-maximality property}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower and upper convolution and divolution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Four min–max operations combining a set function with an extended-real modular function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m:S\to\mathbb R\cup\{\pm\infty\}\) take at most one of \(+\infty\) and \(-\infty\), and let \(h\) be a set function on \(S\). For \(Z\subseteq S\), define \(h_{\downarrow m}(Z):=\min_{X\supseteq Z}\{h(X)-\widetilde m(X-Z)\}\), \(h_{\uparrow m}(Z):=\max_{X\supseteq Z}\{h(X)-\widetilde m(X-Z)\}\), \((h\bigtriangledown m)(Z):=\min_{X\subseteq Z}\{h(X)+\widetilde m(Z-X)\}\), and \((h\bigtriangleup m)(Z):=\max_{X\subseteq Z}\{h(X)+\widetilde m(Z-X)\}\). When \(m\equiv0\), these are respectively \(h_{\mathrm{omin}},h_{\mathrm{omax}},h_{\mathrm{imin}},h_{\mathrm{imax}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower and upper divolution optimize over supersets after subtracting the modular value of the removed elements; lower and upper convolution optimize over subsets after adding the modular value of the added elements. With the zero modular function, they reduce to the four outer and inner min–max envelopes.
assumptions_latex: m:S\to\mathbb R\cup\{\pm\infty\}\text{ takes either }+\infty\text{ or }-\infty\text{, but not both}
h:2^S\to\overline{\mathbb R}\text{ is a set function}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: h_{\downarrow m},\ h_{\uparrow m},\ h\bigtriangledown m,\ h\bigtriangleup m\text{ are defined by the stated superset/subset min--max formulas, with the four envelope operations recovered when }m\equiv0.

knowledge_statements.title: System Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of submodular systems under nonnegative linear aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\) be finite, let \(f_1,\ldots,f_m:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be submodular, and let \(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m\ge 0\). For any \(c\in\mathbb R\), define
\[
h(X)=c+\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i f_i(X),\qquad X\subseteq V.
\]
Then \(h\) is submodular. If every \(f_i\) is normalized and \(c=0\), then \(h(\varnothing)=0\); if every \(f_i\) is also nondecreasing, then \(h\) is nondecreasing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative weighted sum of submodular functions remains submodular; normalization and monotonicity are retained under the stated extra conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h(A)+h(B)\ge h(A\cup B)+h(A\cap B)\) for all \(A,B\subseteq V\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: follows directly by nonnegative aggregation of the defining submodular inequalities
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The aggregation closure property and its qualifications are correct and appropriately classified, but the record has no citation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aggregation of two ground-set elements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of set-function aggregation and its submodularity and paramodularity closure properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let t_1,t_2\in S, T:=\{t_1,t_2\}, t\notin S, and S':=(S\setminus T)\cup\{t\}. For a set function b on S, define b' on S' by b'(X):=b(X) when t\notin X and b'(X):=b((X\setminus\{t\})\cup T) when t\in X. Then b' is obtained from b by aggregating t_1 and t_2. If b is submodular, then b' is submodular; if (p,b) is paramodular, then the correspondingly aggregated pair (p',b') is paramodular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregation replaces two ground-set elements by one new element. Sets not containing the new element retain their old value, while a set containing it is evaluated after replacing it by both original elements. This operation preserves submodularity and, when applied to both functions, paramodularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b'(X)=\begin{cases}b(X),&t\notin X,\\b((X\setminus\{t\})\cup T),&t\in X,\end{cases}\quad b\text{ submodular}\Rightarrow b'\text{ submodular},\quad(p,b)\text{ paramodular}\Rightarrow(p',b')\text{ paramodular.}

knowledge_statements.title: Submodular Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection by partial minimization over a disjoint block of variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\) and \(W\) be disjoint finite sets and let \(f:2^{U\cup W}\to\mathbb R\) be submodular. Define the projection of \(f\) onto \(U\) by
\[
g(A)=\min_{B\subseteq W} f(A\cup B),\qquad A\subseteq U.
\]
Because the domain \(2^W\) is finite, each minimum is attained. Then \(g:2^U\to\mathbb R\) is submodular; explicitly, \(g(A)+g(C)\ge g(A\cup C)+g(A\cap C)\) for all \(A,C\subseteq U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing a submodular function over an entire block of Boolean variables produces a submodular function on the remaining variables.
assumptions_latex: \(U\cap W=\varnothing\) and both sets are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(A)=\min_{B\subseteq W}f(A\cup B)\) defines a submodular function on \(2^U\).

notation.meaning: projection or partial minimization of f onto U

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partial Minimization of a Submodular Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elimination of a disjoint auxiliary ground-set block by partial minimization, including continuous and polyhedral representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let V\cap W=\varnothing, |V|=p, |W|=q, and let G:2^{V\cup W}\to\mathbb{R} be submodular with Lovász extension g:\mathbb{R}^{p+q}\to\mathbb{R}. For A\subseteq V define F(A)=\min_{B\subseteq W}G(A\cup B)-\min_{B\subseteq W}G(B). Then F is submodular and F(\varnothing)=0. If \min_{B\subseteq W}G(B)=0, then for every w\in\mathbb{R}_+^p the Lovász extension f of F satisfies f(w)=\min_{v\in\mathbb{R}_+^q}g(w,v), and P(F)=\{s\in\mathbb{R}^p:\exists t\in\mathbb{R}_+^q\text{ such that }(s,t)\in P(G)\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial minimization over a disjoint auxiliary block, followed by normalization, produces a normalized submodular function. If the auxiliary minimum is zero, its Lovász extension is the nonnegative partial minimum of the original extension, and its polyhedron is obtained by eliminating nonnegative auxiliary coordinates.
assumptions_latex: g:\mathbb{R}^{p+q}\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is the Lovász extension of }G
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is submodular and }F(\varnothing)=0;\quad \min_{B\subseteq W}G(B)=0\Rightarrow\left[f(w)=\min_{v\in\mathbb{R}_+^q}g(w,v)\ \forall w\in\mathbb{R}_+^p,\ P(F)=\{s:\exists t\geq0,(s,t)\in P(G)\}\right].

knowledge_statements.title: Composition Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar composition boundary for monotone submodular set functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:2^V\to I\) be nondecreasing and submodular, where \(I\subseteq\mathbb R\) is an interval, and let \(\phi:I\to\mathbb R\) be nondecreasing and concave. Then \(h=\phi\circ f\) is submodular. Concavity cannot be replaced by arbitrary convexity: on \(V=\{1,2\}\), take \(f(X)=|X|\) and \(\phi(t)=t^2\). The resulting \(h(X)=|X|^2\) violates submodularity because
\[
h(\{1\})+h(\{2\})=2<4=h(V)+h(\varnothing).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nondecreasing concave scalar composition preserves monotone submodularity, while even squaring a modular cardinality function can destroy submodularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi\circ f\) is submodular; unrestricted convex scalar composition is not closure-preserving.

notation.meaning: interval containing the range of f
set function mapping X to φ(f(X))

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composition of a Subset
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a subset composition by adjoining its complement and records partition and co-partition cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \varnothing\ne Z\subset S and let \mathcal K be a hypergraph on S. Define \mathcal K^+:=\mathcal K\cup\{S\setminus Z\}. The family \mathcal K is a composition of Z if \mathcal K^+ is regular on S; its ground-degree is \deg(\mathcal K^+)-1. A partition of Z has ground-degree 0. If \{Z_1,\ldots,Z_t\} partitions S\setminus Z, then \{S\setminus Z_1,\ldots,S\setminus Z_t\} is a co-partition and a composition of Z of ground-degree t-1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hypergraph is a composition of a nonempty subset Z when adjoining S minus Z makes it regular on S; its ground-degree is one less than that regular degree. Partitions of Z have ground-degree zero, while a co-partition induced by t complement blocks has ground-degree t minus one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal K\text{ is a composition of }Z\iff \mathcal K^+\text{ is regular on }S,\qquad d_{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathcal K)=\deg(\mathcal K^+)-1.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tight Modular-Bound Iteration for a Difference of Submodular Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The stated local-minimum conclusion contains an apparent inequality-direction inconsistency: it calls the limit a local minimum while saying its one-element neighbors have smaller objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F,G:2^V\to\mathbb{R} be submodular and set H=F-G. Starting from A\subseteq V, choose a modular function s with s(B)\leq G(B) for all B\subseteq V and s(A)=G(A), then replace A by any element of \operatorname*{argmin}_{B\subseteq V}\{F(B)-s(B)\}; repeat until convergence. The extract asserts that a limiting set A is a one-element local minimum, while stating literally that H(A\cup\{k\})<H(A) for k\in V\setminus A and H(A\setminus\{k\})<H(A) for k\in A.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For submodular set functions F and G, repeatedly construct a modular lower bound of G that is tight at the current set and minimize F minus that bound. The extract claims convergence to a one-element local minimum, but its literal boundary condition says that every one-element addition or deletion has a smaller objective value, which reverses the usual local-minimum inequality.
assumptions_latex: s\text{ is modular},\quad s(B)\leq G(B)\ \forall B\subseteq V,\quad s(A)=G(A)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{At convergence, the extract calls }A\text{ a one-element local minimum but states }H(A\cup\{k\})<H(A)\ (k\notin A),\quad H(A\setminus\{k\})<H(A)\ (k\in A).

knowledge_statements.title: Closure-Preserving Operations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic operations preserving finite-set submodularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be submodular. For fixed \(D\subseteq V\), both the restriction \(f|_D:2^D\to\mathbb R\), given by \((f|_D)(X)=f(X)\), and the contraction \(f/D:2^{V\setminus D}\to\mathbb R\), given by
\[
(f/D)(X)=f(X\cup D)-f(D),
\]
are submodular. Submodularity is also preserved by adding a modular function and by taking finite nonnegative linear combinations of submodular functions on the same ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restriction, contraction, modular perturbation, and finite nonnegative aggregation preserve submodularity.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite and \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) is submodular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f|_D\) and \(f/D\) are submodular, as are modular perturbations and nonnegative linear combinations.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosure Phenomena
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise minimization is not closed within submodular set functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On \(V=\{1,2\}\), define modular, hence submodular, functions \(f(X)=\mathbf 1_{\{1\in X\}}\) and \(g(X)=\mathbf 1_{\{2\in X\}}\). Their pointwise minimum \(h(X)=\min\{f(X),g(X)\}\) satisfies \(h(\varnothing)=h(\{1\})=h(\{2\})=0\) and \(h(V)=1\). Consequently,
\[
h(\{1\})+h(\{2\})=0<1=h(V)+h(\varnothing),
\]
so \(h\) is not submodular. Thus pointwise minimization, unlike partial minimization over variables, does not preserve submodularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pointwise minimum of two modular functions can fail submodularity, already on a two-element ground set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h=\min\{f,g\}\) is not submodular although \(f\) and \(g\) are modular.

notation.meaning: pointwise minimum of f and g

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Separable and Inseparable Sets for a Submodular Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines separability through additivity across a nontrivial partition of a subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:2^V\to\mathbb{R} be submodular with F(\varnothing)=0. A set A\subseteq V is separable if and only if there exists B with \varnothing\neq B\subsetneq A such that F(A)=F(B)+F(A\setminus B). A is inseparable if it is not separable.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure Boundary Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact universal criterion for an operation to preserve submodularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An operation \(T\) on finite-valued set functions is submodularity-preserving precisely when, for every finite ground set \(V\), every admissible submodular input tuple \(\boldsymbol f\), and all \(A,B\subseteq V\), its output \(h=T(\boldsymbol f)\) satisfies
\[
h(A)+h(B)-h(A\cup B)-h(A\cap B)\ge 0.
\]
Accordingly, a closure claim is disproved by one admissible input tuple and one pair \((A,B)\) for which this deficit is negative. If \(T\) changes the ground set, the same criterion is applied on its output ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An operation preserves submodularity exactly when every admissible output satisfies every lattice inequality; one negative deficit is a complete failure certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) maps its admissible finite-valued inputs to a set function \(h\).
Every component of \(\boldsymbol f\) required to be submodular is submodular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) is closure-preserving if and only if the displayed deficit is nonnegative for every admissible \(\boldsymbol f,A,B\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact specialization of the defining submodular inequality to an operation's outputs
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The criterion is an exact universal restatement of closure under the defining lattice inequalities and fits the condition leaf, but no source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure systems and intersecting submodularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition assumes the ground set belongs to the system and uses closure of unions to define the join.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal K\subseteq 2^S\) satisfy \(S\in\mathcal K\) and
\[
X,Y\in\mathcal K,\ X\cap Y\ne\varnothing\implies X\cap Y\in\mathcal K.
\]
Then \(\mathcal K\) is a closure system. For \(X\subseteq S\), let \(\underline X\) denote the unique smallest member of \(\mathcal K\) containing \(X\). For intersecting \(X,Y\in\mathcal K\), define \(X\wedge Y:=X\cap Y\) and \(X\vee Y:=\underline{X\cup Y}\). A function \(b:\mathcal K\to\mathbb Z_+\) is intersecting submodular on \(\mathcal K\) if
\[
b(X)+b(Y)\ge b(X\wedge Y)+b(X\vee Y)
\]
for every intersecting pair \(X,Y\in\mathcal K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closure system on S contains S and is closed under intersections of members having nonempty intersection. The closure of a subset is its unique smallest containing member. For intersecting members, meet is intersection and join is the closure of their union. A nonnegative integer-valued function is intersecting submodular when the submodular inequality holds for every intersecting pair using these meet and join operations.
assumptions_latex: X,Y\in\mathcal K,\ X\cap Y\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow X\cap Y\in\mathcal K
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b\text{ is intersecting submodular}\iff \forall X,Y\in\mathcal K\text{ with }X\cap Y\ne\varnothing,\ b(X)+b(Y)\ge b(X\wedge Y)+b(X\vee Y).

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Failure Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smallest ground-set obstruction to closure under pointwise minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pair on \(V=\{1,2\}\) given by \(f(X)=\mathbf 1_{\{1\in X\}}\) and \(g(X)=\mathbf 1_{\{2\in X\}}\) is a cardinality-minimal family witnessing failure of closure under pointwise minimum. Both functions are modular, but \(h=\min\{f,g\}\) has values \(h(\varnothing)=h(\{1\})=h(\{2\})=0\) and \(h(V)=1\), violating the sole nontrivial two-element lattice inequality. No smaller ground set can witness failure, because every real-valued function on a ground set of cardinality at most one is submodular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two modular indicator functions on two elements form a smallest possible counterexample to closure under pointwise minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are the two singleton-membership indicators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\{f,g\}\) is not submodular, and no counterexample exists on a ground set with fewer than two elements.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Symmetric submodular polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a sign-symmetric polyhedron from a normalized nondecreasing submodular function and identifies two explicit norm-ball instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be nondecreasing and submodular with \(F(\varnothing)=0\). For \(|s|(A)=\sum_{i\in A}|s_i|\), define \[|P|(F)=\left\{s\in\mathbb R^{|V|}:\forall A\subseteq V,\ |s|(A)\le F(A)\right\}=\left\{s\in\mathbb R^{|V|}:|s|\in P(F)\right\}.\] If \(F(A)=|A|\), then \(|P|(F)\) is the \(\ell_\infty\)-unit ball. If \(F(A)=\min\{|A|,1\}\), then \(|P|(F)\) is the \(\ell_1\)-unit ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The symmetric submodular polyhedron contains vectors whose coordinatewise absolute values satisfy the submodular inequalities. Cardinality produces the infinity-norm unit ball, while cardinality truncated at one produces the one-norm unit ball.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Intersecting and Crossing Families and Submodular Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pair-restricted variants of the usual submodularity definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family $\mathcal F\subseteq2^E$ is intersecting if $X\cup Y,X\cap Y\in\mathcal F$ whenever $X,Y\in\mathcal F$ and $X\cap Y\ne\varnothing$. A function $f:\mathcal F\to\mathbf R$ is intersecting-submodular if $f(X)+f(Y)\ge f(X\cup Y)+f(X\cap Y)$ for every such pair. The family is crossing if the same closure holds whenever $X\cap Y$, $X\setminus Y$, $Y\setminus X$, and $E\setminus(X\cup Y)$ are all nonempty; $f$ is crossing-submodular if the inequality holds for every crossing pair. Unprefixed submodularity on a distributive lattice requires the inequality for all pairs in the lattice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting and crossing families are closed under union and intersection only for intersecting or crossing pairs, respectively. Intersecting-submodular and crossing-submodular functions satisfy the submodular inequality on those corresponding pairs; ordinary submodularity on a distributive lattice requires it for every pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(X)+f(Y)\ge f(X\cup Y)+f(X\cap Y)\text{ for every qualifying intersecting or crossing pair }X,Y.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Submodular Flow Polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines bounded submodular flows on a directed graph and records their incidence representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $D=(V,A)$, let $f:A\to\mathbf Z\cup\{-\infty\}$ and $g:A\to\mathbf Z\cup\{\infty\}$ satisfy $f\le g$, and let $b:2^V\to\mathbf Z\cup\{\infty\}$ be crossing submodular with $b(\varnothing)=0$ and finite $b(V)$. For $x\in\mathbf R^A$, define $\Psi_x(Z)=\varrho_x(Z)-\delta_x(Z)$. The vector $x$ is a submodular flow confined by $b$ when $\Psi_x(Z)\le b(Z)$ for every $Z\subseteq V$, and it is feasible when additionally $f\le x\le g$. The feasible set is the submodular flow polyhedron $Q(f,g;b)$. Since $\Psi_x(V)=0$, one may normalize $b(V)=0$. Moreover, $\Psi_x$ is modular and its singleton restriction satisfies $\dot\Psi_x=Q_Dx$, where $Q_D$ is the incidence matrix of $D$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given integer lower and upper arc bounds and a normalized crossing-submodular set function, a submodular flow is a real arc vector whose net inflow into every vertex set is at most the set-function value. Imposing the arc bounds gives the submodular flow polyhedron. Net inflow is a modular set function, its singleton values equal the incidence-vector image, and the confining function may be normalized to have value zero on the whole vertex set.
assumptions_latex: f:A\to\mathbf Z\cup\{-\infty\},\quad g:A\to\mathbf Z\cup\{\infty\},\quad f\le g
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q(f,g;b)=\{x\in\mathbf R^A:f\le x\le g,\ \varrho_x(Z)-\delta_x(Z)\le b(Z)\ \forall Z\subseteq V\},\quad b(V)\text{ may be normalized to }0,\quad \dot\Psi_x=Q_Dx.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Submodular system and its polyhedron-base pair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint definition of a normalized submodular system, its inequality polyhedron, and its full-set equality slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let E be finite, let \mathcal D\subseteq2^E be a distributive lattice with \varnothing,E\in\mathcal D, and let f:\mathcal D\to\mathbf R be submodular with f(\varnothing)=0. Then (\mathcal D,f) is a submodular system on E, with rank f(E). Its submodular polyhedron and base polyhedron are P(f)=\{x\in\mathbf R^E:x(X)\leq f(X)\ \forall X\in\mathcal D\} and B(f)=\{x\in P(f):x(E)=f(E)\}. Elements of P(f) are subbases and elements of B(f) are bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized submodular function on a distributive set lattice containing the empty and full sets defines a submodular system. Its submodular polyhedron satisfies all rank inequalities, and its base polyhedron is the slice on which the full-set inequality is tight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P(f)=\{x\in\mathbf R^E:x(X)\leq f(X)\ \forall X\in\mathcal D\},\qquad B(f)=P(f)\cap\{x:x(E)=f(E)\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive submodular polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the intersection of a submodular polyhedron with the nonnegative orthant and states its monotone-closure representation for a nonmonotone function.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Submodular and Base Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Jointly defines the submodular polyhedron, its base polyhedron, and the latter's fixed-total slice representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) be submodular with \(F(\varnothing)=0\), and let \(s(A)=\sum_{k\in A}s_k\). Then
\[
P(F)=\{s\in\mathbb{R}^p: s(A)\leq F(A)\text{ for every }A\subseteq V\},
\]
and
\[
B(F)=\{s\in\mathbb{R}^p:s(V)=F(V),\ s(A)\leq F(A)\text{ for every }A\subseteq V\}=P(F)\cap\{s:s(V)=F(V)\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a normalized submodular function, the submodular polyhedron contains the vectors whose coordinate sums over every subset do not exceed the function value. The base polyhedron is its slice where the full-set inequality is tight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P(F)=\{s\in\mathbb{R}^p:\forall A\subseteq V,\ s(A)\leq F(A)\},\qquad B(F)=P(F)\cap\{s:s(V)=F(V)\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Base-Polyhedral Representations of Submodular and Semimodular Flows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Collects the incidence-vector equivalence, supermodular and paramodular forms, and full-truncation normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\dot\Psi_x$ be the singleton net-inflow vector of a directed-graph flow $x$. If $b$ is crossing submodular, then $x$ is a subflow confined by $b$ if and only if $\dot\Psi_x\in B(b)$. If $p$ is crossing supermodular, then the constraints $f\le x\le g$ and $\varrho_x(Z)-\delta_x(Z)\ge p(Z)$ for every $Z\subseteq V$ likewise define a submodular flow polyhedron $Q'(f,g;p)$. If $(p,b)$ is an intersecting paramodular pair, then $Q(p,b)\cap\{z:\widetilde z(V)=0\}$ is a $0$-base-polyhedron, so $\{x:\dot\Psi_x\in Q(p,b)\}=\{x:p(Z)\le\varrho_x(Z)-\delta_x(Z)\le b(Z)\ \forall Z\subseteq V\}$ is also a submodular flow polyhedron. Finally, if $Q(f,g;b)\ne\varnothing$, then $Q(f,g;b)=Q(f,g;b^{\downarrow})$, where $b^{\downarrow}$ is the fully submodular truncation of $b$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flow satisfies crossing-submodular net-inflow constraints exactly when its singleton imbalance vector lies in the corresponding base polyhedron. Crossing-supermodular lower constraints and two-sided constraints from an intersecting paramodular pair give equivalent base-polyhedral flow descriptions. Any nonempty submodular flow polyhedron defined by a crossing-submodular function can also be defined by that function's fully submodular truncation.
assumptions_latex: D=(V,A)\text{ is a directed graph and }x\in\mathbf R^A
p\text{ is crossing supermodular in the lower-bound representation}
(p,b)\text{ is an intersecting paramodular pair in the two-sided representation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ is a subflow confined by }b\iff\dot\Psi_x\in B(b);\quad Q'(f,g;p)\text{ and }\{x:\dot\Psi_x\in Q(p,b)\}\text{ are submodular flow polyhedra};\quad Q(f,g;b)=Q(f,g;b^{\downarrow})\text{ when nonempty}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Characteristic Cone of a Submodular Subdifferential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent inequality descriptions of the recession cone and its independence from the function values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathcal D\), the characteristic (recession) cone of \(\partial f(X)\) is \[C_f(X)=\{z\in\mathbf R^E\mid z(Y)-z(X)\le 0\ \forall Y\in\mathcal D\}\] \[=\{z\in\mathbf R^E\mid z(Y)-z(X)\le0\ \forall Y\in[\varnothing,X]_{\mathcal D}\cup[X,E]_{\mathcal D}\}.\] Thus \(C_f(X)\) depends only on \(\mathcal D\) and \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The recession cone of the subdifferential at X consists of vectors whose set sum at every domain set is no greater than the set sum at X. It suffices to impose the inequalities on domain sets below or above X, and the cone depends only on the domain and X.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_f(X)=\{z\in\mathbf R^E:\forall Y\in\mathcal D,\ z(Y)-z(X)\le0\}=\{z\in\mathbf R^E:\forall Y\in[\varnothing,X]_{\mathcal D}\cup[X,E]_{\mathcal D},\ z(Y)-z(X)\le0\},\quad C_f(X)\text{ depends only on }\mathcal D\text{ and }X.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Submodular circulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the directed-graph linear program and its ordinary-circulation specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }D=(V,A)\text{ be directed, let }\mathcal C\subseteq2^V\text{ be crossing, let }f:\mathcal C\to\mathbb Q\text{ be submodular on crossing pairs, and let }l,u,c\in(\mathbb Q\cup\{\pm\infty\})^A.\text{ Consider }\max\sum_{a\in A}c(a)x(a)\text{ subject to }\sum_{a\in\delta^+(W)}x(a)-\sum_{a\in\delta^-(W)}x(a)\leq f(W)\quad(W\in\mathcal C),\qquad l(a)\leq x(a)\leq u(a)\quad(a\in A).\text{ A solution of this linear program is called a submodular circulation. If }\mathcal C=\{\{v\}:v\in V\}\text{ and }f\equiv0,\text{ the model reduces to ordinary directed-graph circulations.}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A submodular circulation solves a directed-graph linear program whose arc vector obeys lower and upper bounds and whose net outflow from every set in a crossing family is bounded by a function submodular on crossing pairs. Singleton sets with zero bounds recover ordinary circulations.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathcal C\to\mathbb Q\text{ is submodular on crossing pairs}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Solutions of the stated linear program are submodular circulations; }\mathcal C=\{\{v\}:v\in V\},\ f\equiv0\text{ gives ordinary circulations.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subgradient–Binary-Subgradient Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between primal subgradients and binary subgradients of the conjugate, together with the lattice structure of the binary subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathcal D\to\mathbf R\) be submodular. For every \(x\in\mathbf R^E\) and \(X\in\mathcal D\), \[x\in\partial f(X)\iff X\in\partial_2 f^*(x).\] Moreover, \(\partial_2 f^*(x)\) is a sublattice of \(\mathcal D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector is a subgradient of a submodular function at a set exactly when that set is a binary subgradient of the conjugate at the vector. The binary subdifferential is a sublattice of the domain.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Face Classification of the Symmetric Submodular Polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructs and exhaustively characterizes faces using stable sets, inseparable incremental blocks, and sign patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq V\) be stable for \(F\), let \(C=A_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}A_m\), and for each \(j\) define \(G_j(D)=F(A_1\cup\cdots\cup A_{j-1}\cup D)-F(A_1\cup\cdots\cup A_{j-1})\) on \(D\subseteq A_j\). Assume each \(A_j\) is inseparable for \(G_j\), and let \(\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}^C\). The set of \(s\in|P|(F)\) satisfying \((\varepsilon\circ s)(A_1\cup\cdots\cup A_j)=F(A_1\cup\cdots\cup A_j)\) for every \(j=1,\ldots,m\) is a face of \(|P|(F)\) with nonempty relative interior in the intersection of these \(m\) hyperplanes. Conversely, every face of \(|P|(F)\) arises from such data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a stable set, order a partition of it into blocks that are inseparable for the successive contracted increment functions, and choose a sign pattern. Requiring signed cumulative block sums to be tight defines a face with nonempty relative interior in the corresponding hyperplane intersection, and every face of the symmetric submodular polyhedron is obtained this way.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left\{s\in|P|(F):(\varepsilon\circ s)(A_1\cup\cdots\cup A_j)=F(A_1\cup\cdots\cup A_j),\ j=1,\ldots,m\right\}\text{ is a face with nonempty relative interior in the hyperplane intersection, and every face of }|P|(F)\text{ has this form.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Intersection closure of submodular polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient condition under which intersecting two submodular polyhedra preserves submodular-polyhedral form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let b_1,b_2:2^S\to\mathbb{R} be submodular, and suppose b_1-b_2 is nondecreasing; in particular, this holds when b_1 is nondecreasing and b_2 is nonincreasing. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Canonical Representations of Intersecting- and Crossing-Submodular Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes uniqueness and preservation of integer-valuedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: (i) Let $f$ be intersecting-submodular on an intersecting family $\mathcal F\subseteq2^E$, with $\varnothing,E\in\mathcal F$ and $f(\varnothing)=0$, and define $\mathrm P(f)=\{x\in\mathbf R^E:x(X)\le f(X)\ \forall X\in\mathcal F\}$. Then there is a unique submodular system $(\mathcal D_1,f_1)$ on $E$ such that $\mathrm P(f)=\mathrm P(f_1)$; if $f$ is integer-valued, then $f_1$ is integer-valued. (ii) Let $f$ be crossing-submodular on a crossing family $\mathcal F\subseteq2^E$, with $\varnothing,E\in\mathcal F$, $f(\varnothing)=0$, and nonempty $\mathrm B(f)=\{x\in\mathbf R^E:x(X)\le f(X)\ \forall X\in\mathcal F,\ x(E)=f(E)\}$. Then there is a unique submodular system $(\mathcal D_2,f_2)$ on $E$ such that $\mathrm B(f)=\mathrm B(f_2)$; if $f$ is integer-valued, then $f_2$ is integer-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every normalized intersecting-submodular inequality system has a unique ordinary submodular-system representation of the same polyhedron. Every normalized crossing-submodular system with a nonempty base has a unique ordinary submodular-system representation of the same base. Integer-valuedness is preserved in both cases.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal F\subseteq2^E\text{ is respectively intersecting or crossing, with }\varnothing,E\in\mathcal F.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!\,(\mathcal D_1,f_1):\mathrm P(f)=\mathrm P(f_1),\qquad \exists!\,(\mathcal D_2,f_2):\mathrm B(f)=\mathrm B(f_2),\quad\text{with integrality preserved}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Greedy optimization over the positive submodular polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear optimization and its Lovász-extension value formula for the positive submodular polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:2^{[p]}\to\mathbb{R} be submodular and nondecreasing, with F(\varnothing)=0. For w\in\mathbb{R}^p, choose an ordering w_{j_1}\ge\cdots\ge w_{j_p}, set A_k=\{j_1,\ldots,j_k\} and A_0=\varnothing, and define s_{j_k}=F(A_k)-F(A_{k-1}) when w_{j_k}>0 and s_{j_k}=0 otherwise. Then s\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in P_+(F)}w^\top u, and \max_{u\in P_+(F)}w^\top u=f(w_+) for every w\in\mathbb{R}^p.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a normalized nondecreasing submodular function, sort the weights, retain the corresponding marginal increments at positive-weight coordinates, and set the remaining coordinates to zero. This maximizes the linear objective over the positive submodular polyhedron, with optimum equal to the Lovász extension at the positive part of the weight vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in P_+(F)}w^\top u,\qquad \max_{u\in P_+(F)}w^\top u=f(w_+)\quad\forall w\in\mathbb{R}^p.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subgradient and Subdifferential of a Submodular Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-function subgradients at a member of a distributive lattice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R\) be submodular on a distributive lattice \(\mathcal D\subseteq 2^E\) with \(\varnothing,E\in\mathcal D\). knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\partial f(X)\iff x(Y)-x(X)\le f(Y)-f(X)\) for every \(Y\in\mathcal D\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Network-flow representation of a monotone submodular function and its positive submodular polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a sink-set function from capacitated multi-source, multi-sink flows and gives its min-cut representation, submodularity, monotonicity, and positive-polyhedron characterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S,V\subseteq W\), let \(c:W\times W\to\mathbb R_+\), and define \(\varphi(A,B)=\sum_{k\in A,\,j\in B}\varphi(k,j)\). Let \(\mathcal F\) be the set of functions \(\varphi:W\times W\to\mathbb R_+\) satisfying \(\varphi\le c\), \(\varphi(W,\{w\})-\varphi(\{w\},W)=0\) for every \(w\in W\setminus(S\cup V)\), \(\varphi(W,\{s\})-\varphi(\{s\},W)\le0\) for every \(s\in S\), and \(\varphi(W,\{t\})-\varphi(\{t\},W)\ge0\) for every \(t\in V\). For \(A\subseteq V\), define \(F(A)=\max_{\varphi\in\mathcal F}\bigl[\varphi(W,A)-\varphi(A,W)\bigr]\). Then \[F(A)=\min_{\substack{X\subseteq W:\,S\subseteq X,\ A\subseteq W\setminus X}}c(X,W\setminus X).\] Consequently, \(F\) is nondecreasing and submodular. Moreover, \[s\in P(F)\cap\mathbb R_+^V\iff \exists\varphi\in\mathcal F\ \text{such that}\ \forall k\in V,\quad s_k=\varphi(W,\{k\})-\varphi(\{k\},W).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a capacitated network with source set S and sink set V, consider nonnegative capacity-feasible flows that conserve flow at all other vertices, have nonpositive net inflow at sources, and nonnegative net inflow at sinks. For each subset A of sinks, its maximum aggregate net inflow equals the minimum capacity of a cut separating every source from A. This defines a nondecreasing submodular function. A nonnegative vector belongs to its submodular polyhedron exactly when its coordinates are the individual sink net inflows of a feasible flow.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall A\subseteq V:\ F(A)=\min_{X\subseteq W:\,S\subseteq X,\,A\subseteq W\setminus X}c(X,W\setminus X);\quad F\text{ is nondecreasing and submodular};\quad s\in P(F)\cap\mathbb R_+^V\iff\exists\varphi\in\mathcal F\ \forall k\in V:\ s_k=\varphi(W,\{k\})-\varphi(\{k\},W).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:2^V\to\mathbb{R} be submodular, and suppose that for some nontrivial A\subset V, F(V)=F(A)+F(V\setminus A). Then, for every B\subseteq V, F(B)=F(B\cap A)+F(B\cap(V\setminus A)).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a submodular function is additive across a nontrivial partition of its ground set, then it decomposes additively across that partition on every subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall B\subseteq V,\quad F(B)=F(B\cap A)+F(B\cap(V\setminus A)).
