knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lovász extension as support function and chain representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the Lovász extension for a normalized submodular function on a simple distributive lattice and records its effective domain, homogeneity, and chain evaluation formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D=2^{\mathcal P}\), where \(\mathcal P=(E,\preccurlyeq)\), and let \(f:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R\) be submodular with \(f(\varnothing)=0\). Define \(\widehat f(c)=\max\{\langle c,x\rangle:x\in P(f)\}\). Then \(\widehat f\) is convex and satisfies \(\widehat f(\lambda c)=\lambda\widehat f(c)\) for \(\lambda>0\). Moreover, \(\widehat f(c)<+\infty\) if and only if \(c\) is nonnegative and monotone nonincreasing on \(\mathcal P\). Every such \(c\) has a unique representation \(c=\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i\chi_{A_i}\), where \(\varnothing\ne A_1\subset\cdots\subset A_k\) are in \(\mathcal D\) and \(\lambda_i>0\), and \(\widehat f(c)=\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i f(A_i)\). When \(c=0\), \(k=0\) and both sums are empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lovász extension is the support function of the submodular polyhedron. It is finite exactly on nonnegative order-reversing vectors, whose unique nested-chain decomposition gives the corresponding weighted sum of set-function values; the zero vector has the empty decomposition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat f(c)=\max_{x\in P(f)}\langle c,x\rangle,\quad \widehat f(c)<+\infty\iff c\text{ is nonnegative and monotone nonincreasing},\quad \widehat f(c)=\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i f(A_i)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lovász Extension by Ordered Prefix Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered-prefix definition of the Lovász extension for an extended-real-valued set function on a finite ground set, including the stated infinity convention and extension property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=\{v_1,\ldots,v_n\}\) be finite and let \(\rho:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{\pm\infty\}\). For \(p\in\mathbb{R}^V\), choose an ordering such that \(p_j=p(v_j)\) satisfies \(p_1\ge\cdots\ge p_n\), and put \(V_j=\{v_1,\ldots,v_j\}\). Then \[p=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}(p_j-p_{j+1})\chi_{V_j}+p_n\chi_V,\] and the Lovász extension is defined by \[\widehat\rho(p)=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}(p_j-p_{j+1})\rho(V_j)+p_n\rho(V),\] with the convention \(0\cdot(\pm\infty)=0\). Moreover, \(\widehat\rho(\chi_X)=\rho(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order the coordinates of a vector nonincreasingly and form the nested prefix subsets. The Lovász extension applies the same coefficients to the set-function values, with zero times either infinity defined as zero. On every characteristic vector it agrees with the original set function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\rho(p)=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}(p_j-p_{j+1})\rho(V_j)+p_n\rho(V),\qquad \widehat\rho(\chi_X)=\rho(X)\ \ (\forall X\subseteq V).

knowledge_statements.title: Multilinear Extension Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent-random-set representation of a set function on the unit cube.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite set \(E\) and \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R\), the multilinear extension \(F:[0,1]^E\to\mathbb R\) is \[F(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq E}f(S)\prod_{e\in S}x_e\prod_{e\notin S}(1-x_e)=\mathbb E[f(R_x)],\] where each \(e\in E\) belongs to \(R_x\) independently with probability \(x_e\). The function \(F\) is affine in each coordinate separately and satisfies \(F(\mathbf1_S)=f(S)\) for every \(S\subseteq E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The multilinear extension is the expected set-function value under independent inclusion with prescribed marginals; it is coordinatewise affine and agrees on Boolean vertices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x)=\mathbb E[f(R_x)]\), and \(F(\mathbf1_S)=f(S)\) for every \(S\subseteq E\).

notation.meaning: Random subset with independent inclusion probabilities x.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Closures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower convex closure of a set function through distributions with fixed marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be finite and \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R\). Its convex closure \(f^-:[0,1]^E\to\mathbb R\) is \[f^-(x)=\min\left\{\sum_{S\subseteq E}\lambda_S f(S):\lambda_S\ge0,\ \sum_S\lambda_S=1,\ \sum_S\lambda_S\mathbf1_S=x\right\}.\] Equivalently, \(f^-(x)\) is the minimum of \(\mathbb E[f(R)]\) over all random subsets \(R\subseteq E\) satisfying \(\mathbb P(e\in R)=x_e\). It is the greatest convex function on \([0,1]^E\) whose Boolean-vertex values do not exceed those of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex closure minimizes expected set-function value over all joint distributions with prescribed marginals and is the greatest convex underestimator at Boolean vertices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^-(x)=\min\{\mathbb E[f(R)]:\mathbb P(e\in R)=x_e\text{ for all }e\in E\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distributional formula and greatest-convex-underestimator characterization are correct, but the record lacks an authoritative citation with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex closure of a set function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise convex-envelope definition based on prescribed upper bounds at hypercube vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite with \(|V|=p\), and let \(F:2^V\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(F(\varnothing)=0\). The convex closure of \(F\) is the pointwise largest convex function \(f:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) such that \(f(\mathbf 1_A)\leq F(A)\) for every \(A\subseteq V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite ground set V and a set function F normalized by F(empty set) = 0, the convex closure is the largest extended-real-valued convex function on R^p whose value at each subset incidence vector does not exceed F at that subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is the pointwise largest convex }g:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\text{ satisfying }g(\mathbf 1_A)\leq F(A)\quad\forall A\subseteq V

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Concave closure sign duality and its computational and tightness boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign-dual representation of the concave closure, together with the stated submodular maximization barrier and vertex-versus-interior boundary for constant-plus-modular upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a set function \(F:2^V\to\mathbb R\), its concave closure is the negative of the convex closure of \(-F\). Computing concave closures in general would provide polynomial-time algorithms for submodular-function maximization. For submodular \(F\), at every vertex \(\mathbf 1_A\) of the hypercube there exists a constant-plus-modular upper bound that is tight at \(A\); such tight bounds cannot in general be obtained at an interior point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The concave closure of F is the negative of the convex closure of −F. A general procedure for computing it would imply polynomial-time submodular maximization. For a submodular function, a constant-plus-modular upper bound can be made tight at any selected hypercube vertex, but such interior-point tightness is unavailable in general.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is submodular for the constant-plus-modular upper-bound assertion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F^{\mathrm{ccv}}=-(-F)^{\mathrm{cvx}};\quad \forall A\subseteq V\ \exists\,U=c+m\text{ with }m\text{ modular},\ U(B)\geq F(B)\ \forall B\subseteq V,\ U(A)=F(A),\text{ whereas analogous tightness at interior points fails in general}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines extended-real-valued M-natural concavity on the integer lattice and records its principal structural, local-optimality, and demand properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let U:\mathbb Z^K	o\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\} have nonempty effective domain, let \chi_0=0, and interpret a maximum over an empty set as -\infty. Then U is M^
atural-concave iff, for every x,y\in\operatorname{dom}U and i\in\operatorname{supp}^+(x-y),
U(x)+U(y)\le \max\!\left\{U(x-\chi_i)+U(y+\chi_i),\ \max_{j\in\operatorname{supp}^-(x-y)} igl[U(x-\chi_i+\chi_j)+U(y+\chi_i-\chi_j) igr]ight\}.
Equivalently, \min_{i\in\operatorname{supp}^+(x-y)}\max_{j\in\operatorname{supp}^-(x-y)\cup\{0\}}[\Delta U(x;j,i)+\Delta U(y;i,j)]\ge0. Such a function has \widehat U(x)=U(x) for x\in\mathbb Z^K, is submodular, and a point x\in\operatorname{dom}U is a global maximizer iff no move x\mapsto x-\chi_i+\chi_j or x\mapsto x\pm\chi_j improves it. It also satisfies the single-improvement, gross-substitutes, and stepwise-gross-substitutes properties, and \arg\max U[-p] is M^
atural-convex for every p\in\mathbb R^K. The last four properties each characterize M^
atural-concavity under their stated hypotheses, whereas submodularity and concave extensibility, even together, do not imply M^
atural-concavity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended-real function on the integer lattice is M-natural-concave exactly when it satisfies the stated unit-transfer exchange inequality. Such functions are concave-extensible and submodular, admit a local characterization of global maxima, satisfy single-improvement and gross-substitutes properties, and have M-natural-convex demand sets. Submodularity plus concave extensibility alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U\text{ is }M^\natural\text{-concave}\iff U\text{ satisfies the }M^\natural\text{-exchange property, with the listed consequences and characterizations.}

children.title: Closure Gap Structure
children.top_down_role: Structural separation between convex and concave envelope values.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure Gap Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise width between extremal expectations having identical marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every finite \(E\), set function \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R\), and \(x\in[0,1]^E\), define the closure gap by \(\Gamma_f(x)=f^+(x)-f^-(x)\). Then \[\Gamma_f(x)\ge0,\qquad f^-(x)\le F(x)\le f^+(x),\] where \(F(x)=\mathbb E[f(R_x)]\) is the multilinear extension generated by independent marginals. Moreover, \(\Gamma_f(x)=0\) exactly when every probability distribution on \(2^E\) with marginal vector \(x\) has the same expected value of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The concave closure dominates the multilinear extension, which dominates the convex closure; their gap vanishes exactly when dependence cannot change the expectation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le\Gamma_f(x)=f^+(x)-f^-(x)\) and \(f^-(x)\le F(x)\le f^+(x)\).

notation.meaning: Closure gap at marginal vector x.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The closure inequalities and zero-gap characterization follow from the extremal fixed-marginal definitions and are correctly stated, but no source is supplied.

children.title: Exactness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Function classes or domains where a closure representation becomes exact.

knowledge_statements.title: Exactness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global closure exactness characterizes modular set functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be finite and \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R\). The following are equivalent: \(f^-(x)=f^+(x)\) for every \(x\in[0,1]^E\); every two distributions on \(2^E\) having the same marginals give the same expectation of \(f\); and \(f\) is modular, meaning that constants \(c\in\mathbb R\) and \(w\in\mathbb R^E\) exist with \[f(S)=c+\sum_{e\in S}w_e\quad(S\subseteq E).\] In this regime, both closures and the multilinear extension equal \(c+w^\top x\) throughout the cube.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex and concave closures coincide everywhere exactly for modular set functions; then every standard continuous extension equals the same affine function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^-=f^+\text{ on }[0,1]^E\iff f(S)=c+\sum_{e\in S}w_e\), and then \(f^-(x)=F(x)=f^+(x)=c+w^\top x\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The global exactness characterization by modularity is mathematically correct and appropriately classified as a theorem, but it requires an authoritative source and locator.

children.title: Explicit Representations
children.top_down_role: Direct tabular, algebraic, or coefficient-based encodings.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truth-table encoding and its direct evaluation access model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a ground set \(E\) with \(|E|=n\), an explicit representation of \(f:2^E\to\mathbb Q\) lists the pair \((S,f(S))\) for every \(S\subseteq E\), using fixed finite encodings of subsets and rational numbers. The representation contains \(2^n\) value entries. Given a direct-addressed or suitably indexed table, a value query \(S\mapsto f(S)\) is answered by lookup. A procedure that scans all entries and performs work polynomial in the entry bit length per entry runs in time polynomial in the total explicit encoding length, although that length is exponential in \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit set-function encoding lists all values, enables indexed lookup, and has exponentially many entries in the ground-set size; full-table scans are polynomial in the encoding length when their per-entry work is polynomially bounded.
assumptions_latex: Subsets and rational values use fixed finite encodings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The representation contains \(2^n\) values and supports indexed evaluation of \(f(S)\).

notation.meaning: Stored value associated with subset S.

children.title: Combinatorial Representations
children.top_down_role: Encodings through graphs, matroids, networks, or related discrete structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact graph-cut representation of a submodular function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a finite directed graph with nonnegative capacities \(c:A\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\), and let \(E\subseteq V\). A graph-cut representation of \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R\) consists of \(G\), \(c\), auxiliary vertices \(U=V\setminus E\), and a constant \(\kappa\) such that \[f(S)=\kappa+\min_{T\subseteq U}c\bigl(\delta^+(S\cup T)\bigr)\qquad(S\subseteq E).\] This representation is compact when \(|V|+|A|\) and the capacity encoding length are polynomial in \(|E|\). For fixed \(S\), evaluation reduces to a minimum-cut problem in which vertices of \(S\) are constrained to the source side, vertices of \(E\setminus S\) are constrained to the sink side, and auxiliary vertices may lie on either side.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph-cut representation encodes a set function by a capacitated directed graph, possibly with auxiliary vertices; evaluating a chosen subset reduces to a minimum cut with selected and unselected ground vertices fixed to opposite sides.
assumptions_latex: Auxiliary vertices may be assigned to either cut side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(S)=\kappa+\min_{T\subseteq V\setminus E}c(\delta^+(S\cup T))\) for every \(S\subseteq E\).

notation.meaning: Total capacity of arcs leaving W.

children.title: Encoding Translations
children.top_down_role: Conversions and succinctness tradeoffs between explicit and combinatorial encodings.

knowledge_statements.title: Encoding Translations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial translations between explicit encodings of finite combinatorial objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R_1\) and \(\mathcal R_2\) be representation schemes for the same class \(\mathcal C\). A translation from \(\mathcal R_1\) to \(\mathcal R_2\) is a map \(T\) such that every valid encoding \(e\in\mathcal R_1\) of \(C\in\mathcal C\) is mapped to a valid encoding \(T(e)\in\mathcal R_2\) of that same object. The translation is polynomial if \(T(e)\) is computable in time polynomial in \(|e|\) and \(|T(e)|\) is polynomially bounded in \(|e|\). The schemes are polynomially equivalent when polynomial translations exist in both directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An encoding translation preserves the represented object; polynomial equivalence requires polynomial-time, polynomial-size translations in both directions.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal R_1\) and \(\mathcal R_2\) encode the same finite object class \(\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e\) and \(T(e)\) represent the same \(C\), with polynomial time and output size in the polynomial case.

children.title: Value Oracles
children.top_down_role: Access through evaluations of a set function.

knowledge_statements.title: Value Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact value-query access to a set function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite ground set \(E\) and a function \(f:2^E\to\mathbb Q\), an exact value oracle is a procedure that, on every query set \(S\subseteq E\), returns the rational number \(f(S)\). In the value-oracle model, an algorithm accesses \(f\) only through such queries; its oracle complexity is the number of queries, while arithmetic and bit complexity additionally account for manipulating the returned values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A value oracle returns the exact function value for any queried subset; query complexity counts these calls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(O_f(S)=f(S)\) for every \(S\subseteq E\).

children.title: Rank Oracles
children.top_down_role: Access through rank evaluations in matroidal or polymatroidal systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rank-query access to a matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a matroid with rank function \(r_M:2^E\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), where \(r_M(S)=\max\{|I|:I\subseteq S,\ I\in\mathcal I\}\). A rank oracle for \(M\) is a procedure that, for every queried set \(S\subseteq E\), returns \(r_M(S)\). The oracle therefore exposes the maximum cardinality of an independent subset of \(S\) without being required to return such a subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid rank oracle returns the maximum size of an independent subset of each queried set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(O_r(S)=r_M(S)=\max\{|I|:I\subseteq S,\ I\in\mathcal I\}\).

children.title: Independence Oracles
children.top_down_role: Access through independence queries in combinatorial systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Independence Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean independent-set access to a matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid. An independence oracle is a procedure that, for each query \(S\subseteq E\), returns \(1\) if \(S\in\mathcal I\) and returns \(0\) otherwise. In this oracle model, the family \(\mathcal I\) need not be listed explicitly, and algorithms may learn whether a set is independent only by issuing oracle queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An independence oracle answers whether a queried subset is independent in a specified matroid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(O_{\mathcal I}(S)=\mathbf 1\{S\in\mathcal I\}\) for every \(S\subseteq E\).

children.title: Oracle Simulation Relations
children.top_down_role: Information comparisons and simulation boundaries among the oracle types.

assumptions_latex: The value oracle is specifically for the rank function \(r_M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(O_r\) simulates \(O_{\mathcal I}\) with one query, and \(O_{\mathcal I}\) simulates \(O_r(S)\) with at most \(|S|\) queries.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Query simulations among matroid value, rank, and independence access.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 Independence and rank p. 173

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid with rank function \(r_M\). For every \(S\subseteq E\), one rank-oracle query determines whether \(S\in\mathcal I\), since \(S\in\mathcal I\) if and only if \(r_M(S)=|S|\). Conversely, the value \(r_M(S)\) can be determined using at most \(|S|\) independence-oracle queries. A value oracle for the particular set function \(r_M\) is identical to a rank oracle. Hence rank, independence, and rank-value access are polynomially query-equivalent for a specified finite matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite matroid, rank and rank-value queries are identical, while independence and rank oracles simulate one another with at most linear query overhead.

children.title: Membership Oracles
children.top_down_role: Access through feasibility or set-membership queries.

knowledge_statements.title: Membership Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean membership access to a represented feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^d\). An exact membership oracle for \(K\) is a procedure that, given a query point \(y\in\mathbb Q^d\), returns \(1\) when \(y\in K\) and \(0\) when \(y\notin K\). Its response contains no separating hyperplane or quantitative distance information. For lower-dimensional or numerically represented sets, weak membership must instead specify a tolerance and a boundary convention; that distinct model is not included in this exact definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact membership oracle says only whether a rational query point belongs to the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(O_K(y)=\mathbf 1\{y\in K\}\).

children.title: Separation Oracles
children.top_down_role: Access through separating certificates for infeasible points.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact strong separation access to a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be a nonempty closed convex set. A strong separation oracle, queried at \(y\in\mathbb Q^d\), either certifies \(y\in K\) or returns \((a,\beta)\in\mathbb Q^d\times\mathbb Q\) such that \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta<a^{\mathsf T}y\) for every \(x\in K\). Thus the returned inequality is valid for all of \(K\) and strictly excludes the query point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strong separation oracle accepts a point in the convex set or returns a valid inequality strictly excluding it.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
The requested exact certificate has rational coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\in K\), or \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta<a^{\mathsf T}y\) for all \(x\in K\).

children.title: Optimization Oracles
children.top_down_role: Access through linear or structured optimization queries.

assumptions_latex: For a finite optimum, the maximum is attained and has an admissible exact representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linear optimization access to a feasible set.

source_refs.locator: Section 4.6. Separation and Optimization p. 93

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty and let queries be rational objective vectors \(c\in\mathbb Q^d\). A strong optimization oracle returns a point \(x^\star\in K\) satisfying \(c^{\mathsf T}x^\star=\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in K\}\), whenever this maximum is finite and attained. In a formulation allowing unbounded sets, the oracle must instead report unboundedness when \(\sup_{x\in K}c^{\mathsf T}x=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strong optimization oracle maximizes each queried rational linear objective, returning an optimizer or reporting unboundedness.

children.title: Oracle Equivalence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Computational reductions and nonequivalence boundaries among the interfaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Equivalence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong optimization–separation equivalence for well-described rational polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be a nonempty rational polyhedron equipped with a polynomial facet-complexity bound and the standard rational encoding model. There is an oracle-polynomial-time algorithm for strong linear optimization over \(P\) given a strong separation oracle for \(P\); conversely, strong separation for \(P\) is oracle-polynomial-time reducible to strong linear optimization over \(P\). Hence strong optimization and strong separation are polynomially equivalent in this well-described regime. Exact membership alone is not covered by this equivalence without additional geometric or weak-oracle assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For well-described rational polyhedra, strong separation and strong linear optimization reduce to each other in oracle-polynomial time; membership needs extra assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a nonempty rational polyhedron.
A polynomial facet-complexity bound and rational encoding are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{SEP}(P)\equiv_{\mathrm{poly}}\mathrm{OPT}(P)\) in the strong oracle model.

children.title: Sampling Oracles
children.top_down_role: Random-sample access to values, outcomes, or induced distributions.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random-sample access to a query-dependent distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Q\) be a query space and let \((\Omega,\mathcal F)\) be a measurable output space. A sampling oracle is specified by a family of probability measures \(\{P_q:q\in\mathcal Q\}\). On each query \(q\), it returns a random variable \(Z\sim P_q\); conditional on the submitted queries, separate calls use independent randomness unless another dependence rule is explicitly stated. The algorithm observes samples, not an exact probability table or exact expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sampling oracle draws from a distribution determined by the query, ordinarily using fresh independent randomness on each call.
assumptions_latex: \(P_q\) is a probability measure on \((\Omega,\mathcal F)\) for every \(q\in\mathcal Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(O(q)=Z\) with \(Z\sim P_q\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the sampling-oracle leaf and the formulation is plausible, but no source is supplied. In particular, the conditional independence convention is model-dependent and requires an authoritative locator before this version can be accepted.

children.title: Noisy Oracles
children.top_down_role: Access models with stochastic or adversarial observation error.

knowledge_statements.title: Noisy Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive stochastic-error access to a real-valued function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a query space \(\mathcal Q\) and function \(f:\mathcal Q\to\mathbb R\), an additive noisy oracle returns \(Y(q)=f(q)+\xi_q\) on query \(q\). A complete noisy-oracle specification states the conditional law of \(\xi_q\), including its bias, tail or moment bounds, and dependence across calls. A common unbiased sub-Gaussian model requires \(\mathbb E[\xi_q\mid q]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[\exp(\lambda\xi_q)\mid q]\le\exp(\lambda^2\sigma^2/2)\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A noisy oracle returns the true value plus random error; its bias, tails, and dependence structure are part of the model.
assumptions_latex: In the displayed common model, the noise is conditionally unbiased and \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y(q)=f(q)+\xi_q\) with the stated conditional noise law.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the noisy-oracle leaf, but no source supports the selected additive, conditionally unbiased sub-Gaussian variant. Because noisy-oracle models differ in bias, adaptivity, tails, and cross-call dependence, an authoritative source is needed to validate this exact specification.

children.title: Approximate Oracles
children.top_down_role: Access models returning controlled approximations to exact responses.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic additive or multiplicative approximation to value access.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathcal Q\to\mathbb R\). An additive \(\varepsilon\)-approximate value oracle returns \(\widetilde f(q)\) satisfying \(|\widetilde f(q)-f(q)|\le\varepsilon\) for every \(q\in\mathcal Q\). If \(f(q)\ge0\), a multiplicative \(\rho\)-approximate value oracle, with \(\rho\ge1\), returns \(\widetilde f(q)\) satisfying \(f(q)/\rho\le\widetilde f(q)\le\rho f(q)\). The approximation type, parameter, and whether the guarantee is deterministic or probabilistic must be specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate oracle returns values within a declared additive or multiplicative error guarantee for every query.
assumptions_latex: For the multiplicative convention, \(f\) is nonnegative and \(\rho\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\widetilde f(q)-f(q)|\le\varepsilon\), or \(f(q)/\rho\le\widetilde f(q)\le\rho f(q)\), according to the declared model.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the approximate-oracle leaf and the displayed additive and symmetric multiplicative conventions are internally consistent. No source is supplied, however, and multiplicative approximation conventions vary, so an authoritative locator is required for this exact formulation.

children.title: Information-Loss Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits imposed by sampling error, noise, or approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Information-Loss Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An indistinguishability boundary for randomized algorithms using imperfect value information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_0,f_1:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be two instances, and let \(P_i\) be the distribution of the complete oracle transcript observed by an adaptive randomized algorithm on \(f_i\). For an accuracy level \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), define \(S_i=\{X\subseteq V:f_i(X)\le \min_Y f_i(Y)+\varepsilon\}\). If \(S_0\cap S_1=\varnothing\), then the algorithm's average probability of returning an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal set satisfies \[\frac12\Pr_{f_0}(\widehat X\in S_0)+\frac12\Pr_{f_1}(\widehat X\in S_1)\le \frac{1+\operatorname{TV}(P_0,P_1)}2.\] Thus identical transcript laws force failure probability at least \(1/2\) on one of the two instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If two instances are nearly indistinguishable from their oracle transcripts but require disjoint approximate solutions, every algorithm has a correspondingly large failure probability.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm's output is measurable with respect to its transcript and internal randomness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\frac12\Pr_{f_0}(\widehat X\in S_0)+\frac12\Pr_{f_1}(\widehat X\in S_1)\le (1+\operatorname{TV}(P_0,P_1))/2\).

notation.meaning: Family of epsilon-optimal sets for instance i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-instance total-variation bound is mathematically plausible and fits a failure-boundary leaf, but no source or locator supports the exact transcript model and conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Succinct-Representation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A counting lower bound for universal exact encodings of submodular functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider any injective binary encoding capable of representing every labeled matroid rank function on an \(n\)-element ground set, hence a subclass of integer-valued monotone submodular functions. If \(M_n\) denotes the number of labeled matroids, some encoded rank function requires at least \(\lceil\log_2 M_n\rceil\) bits. The standard counting lower bound \[\log_2 M_n\ge \frac1n\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\] for sufficiently large \(n\) therefore gives worst-case length \(2^{\Omega(n)}\). Consequently, no polynomial-length representation can encode all submodular functions exactly, although particular subclasses may admit succinct representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Counting matroid rank functions shows that some submodular functions require exponentially many bits in any universal exact, uniquely decodable representation.
assumptions_latex: The encoding is injective and exact.
All labeled matroid rank functions must be representable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_r \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{enc}(r))\ge \lceil\log_2 M_n\rceil=2^{\Omega(n)}\).

notation.meaning: Number of labeled matroids on an n-element ground set.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits, but the stated labeled-matroid counting inequality, its range of validity, and the resulting encoding lower bound require an authoritative locator.

A number \(\widehat\lambda\ge 0\) is the minimum value of the ratio in Problem (7.133) if and only if

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Discrete Separation Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of compatible submodular and supermodular systems, including the integer-valued case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let (\mathcal D_1,f) be a submodular system on E and (\mathcal D_2,g) a supermodular system on E. If g(X)\le f(X) for every X\in\mathcal D_1\cap\mathcal D_2, then there exists x\in\mathbb R^E such that g(X)\le x(X) for every X\in\mathcal D_2 and x(X)\le f(X) for every X\in\mathcal D_1. Moreover, if f and g are integer-valued, x may be chosen in \mathbb Z^E.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Frank's Discrete Separation Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Submodular–supermodular separation on a finite ground set, preserving extended-value, normalization, domination, and integrality hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite. Let \(\rho:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be submodular and \(\mu:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}\) be supermodular. Suppose \(\rho(\varnothing)=\mu(\varnothing)=0\), \(\rho(V)<+\infty\), \(\mu(V)>-\infty\), and \(\rho(X)\ge\mu(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq V\). Then there exists \(x^*\in\mathbb{R}^V\) such that \[\rho(X)\ge x^*(X)\ge\mu(X)\qquad(\forall X\subseteq V).\] If \(\rho\) and \(\mu\) are integer-valued, \(x^*\) can be chosen in \(\mathbb{Z}^V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a normalized submodular function dominates a normalized supermodular function on every subset and their whole-set values are finite in the stated directions, a modular set function lies between them everywhere. If both functions are integer-valued, the separating vector can be integral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists x^*\in\mathbb{R}^V\ \forall X\subseteq V:\ \rho(X)\ge x^*(X)\ge\mu(X);\qquad \rho,\mu\text{ integer-valued}\Rightarrow x^*\in\mathbb{Z}^V\text{ may be chosen}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modularity Classes of Set Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions together with bipartite-matching examples and the nonbipartite failure boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f:2^S\to\mathbb R\), submodularity means \(f(X\cup Y)+f(X\cap Y)\le f(X)+f(Y)\) for all \(X,Y\subseteq S\); supermodularity reverses this inequality, and modularity means equality for all such \(X,Y\). On the vertex set of one side of a bipartite graph, surplus is submodular, deficiency is supermodular, and cardinality is modular. For nonbipartite graphs, deficiency and surplus need be neither submodular nor supermodular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set function is submodular when union plus intersection never exceeds the sum on the two sets, supermodular when the inequality is reversed, and modular when equality always holds. Bipartite surplus, deficiency, and cardinality exemplify these three classes respectively; the surplus and deficiency properties can fail in nonbipartite graphs.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Submodular and Supermodular Set Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real-valued set functions on a finite ground set, including the stated infinity and normalization conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let V be finite. Set functions are normalized here by \rho(\varnothing)=0 and are assumed to satisfy \rho(V)<+\infty. A function \mu:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\} is supermodular if -\mu is submodular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite ground set, a set function is submodular when its values satisfy the union-intersection inequality for every pair of subsets, using the stated convention for positive infinity. The adopted normalization is value zero at the empty set and a finite value on the whole ground set. A function is supermodular when its negative is submodular.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Supermodular Systems, Polyhedra, and Complement Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions and duality principles for supermodular and submodular systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function $g:\mathcal D\to\mathbf R$ is supermodular if $g(X)+g(Y)\leq g(X\cup Y)+g(X\cap Y)$ for all $X,Y\in\mathcal D$, equivalently if $-g$ is submodular. If $\varnothing,E\in\mathcal D$ and $g(\varnothing)=0$, then $(\mathcal D,g)$ is a supermodular system, with $\mathrm P(g)=\{x\in\mathbf R^E:x(X)\geq g(X)\ \forall X\in\mathcal D\}$ and $\mathrm B(g)=\{x\in\mathrm P(g):x(E)=g(E)\}$. A function is modular when it is both submodular and supermodular. Reversing the order on $\mathbf R$ converts these supermodular objects into submodular ones. For a submodular system $(\mathcal D,f)$, define $\overline{\mathcal D}=\{E\setminus X:X\in\mathcal D\}$ and $f^{\#}(E\setminus X)=f(E)-f(X)$; then $(\overline{\mathcal D},f^{\#})$ is its dual supermodular system, with the analogous construction defining the dual submodular system of a supermodular system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Supermodularity reverses the submodular inequality and yields a lower-inequality polyhedron with a fixed-total base. Modular functions satisfy both inequalities. Reversing scalar order converts supermodular objects to submodular ones, while complementing sets and using f(E)-f(X) constructs the dual system.
assumptions_latex: $\mathcal D$ is a distributive lattice of subsets of $E$.
For a supermodular system, $\varnothing,E\in\mathcal D$ and $g(\varnothing)=0$.
For complement duality, $(\mathcal D,f)$ is a submodular system on $E$.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g\text{ is supermodular}\iff -g\text{ is submodular},\qquad (\overline{\mathcal D},f^{\#})\text{ is the dual supermodular system of }(\mathcal D,f).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate Recovery on a Distributive Lattice
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of submodular and supermodular set-function values from their conjugates, with the failure boundary outside the lattice domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D\subseteq 2^E\) be a distributive lattice containing \(\varnothing\) and \(E\), let \(f:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R\) be submodular, and let \(g:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R\) be supermodular. For every \(X\in\mathcal D\), \[f(X)=\max_{x\in\mathbb R^E}\{x(X)-f^*(x)\},\qquad g(X)=\min_{x\in\mathbb R^E}\{x(X)-g^*(x)\}.\] For every \(X\in 2^E\setminus\mathcal D\), \(x\mapsto x(X)-f^*(x)\) is unbounded above and \(x\mapsto x(X)-g^*(x)\) is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Values on the lattice are recovered from the corresponding conjugates by maximization or minimization. Outside the lattice, the two expressions are respectively unbounded above and below.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal D\subseteq 2^E\) is a distributive lattice with \(\varnothing,E\in\mathcal D\).
\(f^*\) and \(g^*\) are the conjugates defined on \(\mathbb R^E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(X\in\mathcal D\), \(f(X)=\max_x\{x(X)-f^*(x)\}\) and \(g(X)=\min_x\{x(X)-g^*(x)\}\); for \(X\notin\mathcal D\), the first objective is unbounded above and the second is unbounded below.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modular Sandwich Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise modular separation of a supermodular function from a dominating submodular function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be finite and let \(f,g:2^E\to\mathbb{R}\). If \(f\) is supermodular, \(g\) is submodular, and \(f(A)\le g(A)\) for every \(A\subseteq E\), then there exists a modular function \(h:2^E\to\mathbb{R}\) such that

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Function Conjugate Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel conjugacy obtained by embedding subsets as incidence vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be submodular on finite \(V\), and write \(p(X)=\sum_{i\in X}p_i\) for \(p\in\mathbb R^V\). Define its modular conjugate by \[f^\star(p)=\max_{Y\subseteq V}\{p(Y)-f(Y)\}.\] Then every set value has the biconjugate representation \[f(X)=\sup_{p\in\mathbb R^V}\{p(X)-f^\star(p)\},\qquad X\subseteq V.\] Equivalently, this is Fenchel biconjugacy for the convex closure of the vertex data \(f(X)\) on the incidence vectors of subsets.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(X)=\sup_{p\in\mathbb R^V}\{p(X)-f^\star(p)\}\) for every \(X\subseteq V\).

knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel-Type Min–Max Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-set Fenchel duality for a submodular–supermodular pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be submodular and \(g:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be supermodular. For \(p\in\mathbb R^V\), define \[f^\star(p)=\max_{X\subseteq V}\{p(X)-f(X)\},\qquad g_\star(p)=\min_{X\subseteq V}\{p(X)-g(X)\}.\] Finite-set Fenchel duality states \[\min_{X\subseteq V}\{f(X)-g(X)\}=\max_{p\in\mathbb R^V}\{g_\star(p)-f^\star(p)\}.\] When \(f\) and \(g\) are integer-valued, an integral maximizing vector \(p\in\mathbb Z^V\) may be chosen.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transfer to the Positive Submodular Polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The hypotheses on the separable functions and duality are those inherited from Proposition 8.1; the additional stated assumption is that the submodular function is nondecreasing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume that $F$ is submodular and nondecreasing and that the hypotheses of the underlying separable base-polyhedron duality result hold. Let $(v,t)$ be primal–dual optimal for
\[
\min_{v\in\mathbb R^p}\left\{f(v)+\sum_{k\in V}\psi_k(v_k)\right\}
=
\max_{t\in B(F)}\left\{-\sum_{k\in V}\psi_k^*(-t_k)\right\}.
\]
For every $k\in V$, choose
\[
w_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{r\le (v_k)_+}\psi_k(r),\qquad
\widehat s_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{r\le t_k}\{-\psi_k^*(-r)\},\qquad
s_k=(\widehat s_k)_+.
\]
Then $(w,s)$ is primal–dual optimal for
\[
\min_{w\in\mathbb R^p}\left\{f(w_+)+\sum_{k\in V}\psi_k(w_k)\right\}
=
\max_{s\in P_+(F)}\left\{-\sum_{k\in V}\psi_k^*(-s_k)\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nondecreasing submodular function, a primal–dual optimum over the base polyhedron yields one over the positive submodular polyhedron: minimize each separable primal term below the positive part of its original coordinate, and take the positive part of a corresponding half-line dual maximizer.

(v,t)\text{ is primal\text{–}dual optimal for the stated problem over }B(F)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (w,s)\text{ is primal\text{–}dual optimal for the stated primal problem and its dual over }P_+(F).

knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The discrete subdifferential of a submodular function at a set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite ground set \(V\), a submodular function \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\), and \(A\subseteq V\), the subgradient polyhedron at \(A\) is \[\partial f(A)=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^V: f(Y)-x(Y)\ge f(A)-x(A)\text{ for every }Y\subseteq V\right\}.\] Equivalently, \(x\in\partial f(A)\) precisely when the modular function \(Y\mapsto f(A)+x(Y)-x(A)\) is a global lower bound for \(f\) and is tight at \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The subgradient polyhedron consists of modular lower bounds to the set function that agree with it at the designated set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial f(A)=\{x:f(Y)-x(Y)\ge f(A)-x(A)\text{ for all }Y\subseteq V\}\).

children.title: Greedy Chains

knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Chains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Permutation-chain construction of a greedy modular vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a submodular function \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\), a set \(A\subseteq V\), and a permutation \(\pi=(\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_n)\) whose first \(|A|\) elements are exactly \(A\). Initialize \(S_0=\varnothing\). For \(k=1,\ldots,n\), set \[S_k=S_{k-1}\cup\{\pi_k\},\qquad x^\pi_{\pi_k}=f(S_k)-f(S_{k-1}).\] Output the maximal chain \(S_0\subset S_1\subset\cdots\subset S_n=V\) and the greedy vector \(x^\pi\); the prefix condition gives \(S_{|A|}=A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order the elements with the designated set first, form successive prefixes, and assign each element its marginal value along that chain.
assumptions_latex: The permutation lists all elements of \(A\) before those of \(V\setminus A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output satisfies \(x^\pi(S_k)=f(S_k)-f(\varnothing)\) for every chain prefix \(S_k\).

notation.meaning: The first k elements of the permutation.
Greedy marginal vector associated with the permutation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The permutation-chain construction is correctly classified as an algorithm and matches the leaf, but it lacks supporting evidence and a locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique Subgradient in a Maximal-Chain Simplex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness and chain-increment characterization of the convex extension's subgradient at an interior point of a chain simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[\mathcal C:\varnothing=S_0\subset S_1\subset\cdots\subset S_n=E\]
be a maximal chain of \(\mathcal D\), and let \(c\) be an interior point of \(\mathrm P(\mathcal C)\). Then \(\widetilde f\) has a unique subgradient \(x\) at \(c\), given by
\[x(S_i\setminus S_{i-1})=f(S_i)-f(S_{i-1}),\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an interior point of the simplex induced by a maximal chain, the convex extension has a unique subgradient. Its value on each successive chain difference equals the corresponding increment of the set function.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal C:\varnothing=S_0\subset S_1\subset\cdots\subset S_n=E\text{ is a maximal chain of }\mathcal D
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial\widetilde f(c)=\{x\},\qquad x(S_i\setminus S_{i-1})=f(S_i)-f(S_{i-1})\quad(i=1,\ldots,n)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Simplicial Subdivision by Maximal Chains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric subdivision of the domain polytope by simplices associated with maximal chains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

\[\{\mathrm P(\mathcal C):\mathcal C\text{ is a maximal chain of }\mathcal D\}\]

\[\mathcal C^i:\varnothing=S_0^i\subset S_1^i\subset\cdots\subset S_n^i=E,\qquad i=1,2,\]
the simplices \(\mathrm P(\mathcal C^1)\) and \(\mathrm P(\mathcal C^2)\) have a common facet if and only if there is some \(k\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\}\) such that
\[S_j^1=S_j^2\qquad(0\le j\le n,\ j\ne k).\]

knowledge_statements.title: Extreme Subgradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extreme points of a discrete subdifferential arise from compatible permutations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be submodular and \(A\subseteq V\). For every permutation \(\pi\) that places all elements of \(A\) before all elements of \(V\setminus A\), the greedy marginal vector \(x^\pi\) belongs to \(\partial f(A)\) and is an extreme point of that polyhedron. Conversely, every extreme point of \(\partial f(A)\) is \(x^\pi\) for at least one such permutation. Distinct compatible permutations can yield the same extreme point when marginal increments are degenerate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The vertices of the discrete subdifferential are exactly greedy marginal vectors from permutations having the designated set as a prefix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{ext}(\partial f(A))=\{x^\pi:\pi\text{ places }A\text{ before }V\setminus A\}\) after duplicate vectors are identified.

notation.meaning: Greedy marginal vector of permutation pi.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property matches the leaf, but the converse characterization of every extreme point by a compatible permutation needs an authoritative theorem locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Chain–Subgradient Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy-chain characterization of discrete subgradients and their extreme points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be submodular, let \(A\subseteq V\), and let \(\pi\) be a permutation whose prefix of length \(|A|\) equals \(A\). If \(x^\pi\) is formed from successive marginal increments along the prefix chain, then \[f(Y)\ge f(A)+x^\pi(Y)-x^\pi(A)\qquad\text{for every }Y\subseteq V.\] Hence \(x^\pi\in\partial f(A)\), with equality on every prefix of the chain. Moreover, varying over all compatible permutations generates exactly the extreme points of \(\partial f(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A chain passing through the designated set produces a tight subgradient, and all extreme subgradients arise from such chains.
assumptions_latex: The permutation has \(A\) as a prefix.
Greedy coordinates are successive chain marginals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\pi\in\partial f(A)\), every chain prefix is tight, and compatible greedy vectors generate \(\operatorname{ext}(\partial f(A))\).

notation.meaning: Greedy vector generated by permutation pi.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is locally appropriate and its notation is consistent, but the tightness and exhaustive extreme-point assertions lack cited support.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Chain Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness caused by tied levels or coincident greedy marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be normalized and submodular, and maximize \(w^\top x\) over its base polyhedron. If the coordinates of \(w\) have ties, their strict level sets determine only a partial chain. Every permutation refining the tied blocks produces a compatible greedy base, and the exposed maximizing face is the convex hull of these greedy bases. Thus a tied ordering need not identify a unique chain or extreme subgradient; uniqueness holds only when all compatible refinements yield the same greedy vector, while distinct refinements may still coincide because their marginal increments agree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tied weights determine only a partial chain; compatible refinements can expose several greedy vectors, though degeneracy may also make different refinements coincide.
assumptions_latex: The weight vector has at least one tied coordinate block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in B(f)}w^\top x=\operatorname{conv}\{x^\pi:\pi\text{ refines the weak order of }w\}\).

notation.meaning: Greedy base associated with a refining permutation.
Weight vector defining the exposed face.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The tied-order phenomenon fits a failure-boundary leaf, but the exposed-face formula and its connection to extreme subgradients require a source-specific formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Tight-Set Lattices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of tight constraints under union and intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be submodular and let \(x\in P(f)=\{z\in\mathbb R^V:z(S)\le f(S)\text{ for all }S\subseteq V\}\). Define the tight-set family \(\mathcal T_x=\{S\subseteq V:x(S)=f(S)\}\). If \(A,B\in\mathcal T_x\), then submodularity and modularity give \[x(A\cap B)+x(A\cup B)=x(A)+x(B)=f(A)+f(B)\ge f(A\cap B)+f(A\cup B).\] Feasibility forces equality throughout, so \(A\cap B,A\cup B\in\mathcal T_x\). Hence \(\mathcal T_x\) is a lattice under intersection and union.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible point of a submodular polyhedron, the sets on which constraints are tight are closed under intersection and union.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A,B\in\mathcal T_x\Rightarrow A\cap B,A\cup B\in\mathcal T_x\).

notation.meaning: Family of constraints tight at x.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lattice property is standard and fits the leaf, but it has no citation and the statement includes a proof-style derivation that must be removed before acceptance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual of separable optimization with a Lovász extension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded Fenchel-duality theorem specialized to submodular Lovász-extension optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be submodular, let \(f\) be its Lovász extension, and identify \(V=\{1,\ldots,p\}\). Let each \(\psi_j:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable and strictly convex, with \(\sup_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\psi_j'(\alpha)=+\infty\) and \(\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\psi_j'(\alpha)=-\infty\). Then \[\min_{w\in\mathbb R^p}\left[f(w)+\sum_{j=1}^p\psi_j(w_j)\right]\] and \[\max_{s\in B(F)}-\sum_{j=1}^p\psi_j^*(-s_j)\] are dual optimization problems. A feasible pair \((w,s)\) is optimal if and only if \(s_k=-\psi_k'(w_k)\) for every \(k\) and \(s\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in B(F)}w^\top u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing a submodular function's Lovász extension plus smooth strictly convex separable penalties is dual to maximizing the negative conjugate penalties over its base polyhedron. A feasible pair is optimal exactly when every dual coordinate is the negative derivative of its penalty and the dual point maximizes the primal-induced linear form over the base polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: \(F:2^V\to\mathbb R\) is submodular and \(f\) is its Lovász extension
For every \(j\), \(\psi_j:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable and strictly convex
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_w[f(w)+\sum_j\psi_j(w_j)]\) is dual to \(\max_{s\in B(F)}-\sum_j\psi_j^*(-s_j)\), and \((w,s)\) is optimal iff \(s_k=-\psi_k'(w_k)\) for all \(k\) and \(s\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in B(F)}w^\top u\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic Properties of the Lovász Extension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linearity, level-set representations, translation covariance, positive homogeneity, indicator recovery, symmetry, block-constant evaluation, and threshold expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let V=\{1,\ldots,p\}, let F:2^V\to\mathbb R satisfy F(\varnothing)=0, and let f be its Lovász extension. Then:
(a) if G:2^V\to\mathbb R satisfies G(\varnothing)=0 and has Lovász extension g, then f+g is the Lovász extension of F+G, and for every \lambda\in\mathbb R, \lambda f is the Lovász extension of \lambda F;
(b) for w\in\mathbb R_+^p,
\[f(w)=\int_0^{\infty}F(\{i\in V:w_i\ge z\})\,dz;\]
(c) if F(V)=0, then for every w\in\mathbb R^p,
\[f(w)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}F(\{i\in V:w_i\ge z\})\,dz;\]
(d) for every w\in\mathbb R^p and \alpha\in\mathbb R,
\[f(w+\alpha\mathbf1_V)=f(w)+\alpha F(V);\]
(e) for every t\ge0 and w\in\mathbb R^p, \(f(tw)=t f(w)\);
(f) for every A\subseteq V, \(f(\mathbf1_A)=F(A)\);
(g) if F(A)=F(V\setminus A) for every A\subseteq V, then \(f(-w)=f(w)\) for every w\in\mathbb R^p;
(h) if V=A_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}A_m and w=\sum_{i=1}^m v_i\mathbf1_{A_i} with v_1\ge\cdots\ge v_m, then
\[f(w)=\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}(v_i-v_{i+1})F(A_1\cup\cdots\cup A_i)+v_mF(V);\]
(i) if w\in[0,1]^p and X\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1], then
\[f(w)=\mathbb E\bigl[F(\{i\in V:w_i\ge X\})\bigr].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lovász-extension operator is linear in the underlying normalized set function. It admits simplified level-set integrals under the stated domain conditions, is translation-covariant along the all-ones direction and positively homogeneous, recovers the set function on indicator vectors, maps symmetric set functions to even functions, has an ordered partition-block formula, and has a uniform-threshold expectation representation on the unit cube.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is the Lovász extension of }F
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Properties (a)--(i) hold with their stated additional hypotheses, including }G(\varnothing)=0,\ w\in\mathbb R_+^p,\ F(V)=0,\ t\ge0,\text{ symmetry of }F,\text{ the ordered partition assumptions, and }w\in[0,1]^p.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Greedy optimization over the symmetric submodular polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-weight greedy construction and support-function representation for the symmetric submodular polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:2^{[p]}\to\mathbb{R} be submodular and nondecreasing, with F(\varnothing)=0. For w\in\mathbb{R}^p, choose an ordering |w_{j_1}|\ge\cdots\ge|w_{j_p}|, set A_k=\{j_1,\ldots,j_k\} and A_0=\varnothing, and define s_{j_k}=\operatorname{sign}(w_{j_k})\bigl(F(A_k)-F(A_{k-1})\bigr). Then s\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in |P|(F)}w^\top u, and \max_{u\in |P|(F)}w^\top u=f(|w|) for every w\in\mathbb{R}^p.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a normalized nondecreasing submodular function, sort coordinates by decreasing absolute weight and give each successive marginal increment the sign of its weight. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Lovász-Extension Relaxation of Submodular Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Establishes equality of the discrete, binary, and continuous-cube minima and characterizes the relaxed minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\) be a finite ground set with \(|V|=p\), let \(F:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) be submodular, and let \(f\) be its Lovász extension. Then
\[
\min_{A\subseteq V}F(A)=\min_{w\in\{0,1\}^p}f(w)=\min_{w\in[0,1]^p}f(w).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\operatorname*{argmin}_{w\in[0,1]^p}f(w)=\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\operatorname*{argmin}_{w\in\{0,1\}^p}f(w)\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a submodular function, minimizing its Lovász extension over the unit cube is an exact relaxation of set-function minimization. The cube minimizers are exactly the convex hull of the binary minimizers.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is the Lovász extension of }F
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{A\subseteq V}F(A)=\min_{w\in\{0,1\}^p}f(w)=\min_{w\in[0,1]^p}f(w),\quad \operatorname*{argmin}_{w\in[0,1]^p}f(w)=\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\operatorname*{argmin}_{w\in\{0,1\}^p}f(w)\right)

knowledge_statements.title: Convexity Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between set-function submodularity and convexity of the Lovász extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(f(\varnothing)=0\). For \(w\in\mathbb R^V\), choose a permutation \(\pi\) with \(w_{\pi_1}\ge\cdots\ge w_{\pi_n}\), set \(S_k=\{\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_k\}\), and define the Lovász extension by \[\widehat f(w)=\sum_{k=1}^n w_{\pi_k}\bigl(f(S_k)-f(S_{k-1})\bigr).\] This value is independent of choices within tied blocks. The function \(f\) is submodular if and only if \(\widehat f\) is convex on \(\mathbb R^V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized set function is submodular exactly when its piecewise-linear Lovász extension is convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\text{ is submodular}\Longleftrightarrow \widehat f\text{ is convex on }\mathbb R^V\).

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Function View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The Lovász extension as the support function of the base polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be normalized and submodular, and define \[B(f)=\{x\in\mathbb R^V:x(S)\le f(S)\text{ for all }S\subseteq V,\ x(V)=f(V)\}.\] For every \(w\in\mathbb R^V\), the Lovász extension satisfies \[\widehat f(w)=\sigma_{B(f)}(w)=\max_{x\in B(f)}w^\top x.\] If \(\pi\) orders the coordinates of \(w\) nonincreasingly, the greedy vector with coordinates \(x^\pi_{\pi_k}=f(S_k)-f(S_{k-1})\) belongs to \(B(f)\) and attains the maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lovász extension is the support function of the base polyhedron, with a maximizing base obtained by the greedy ordering of weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat f(w)=\max_{x\in B(f)}w^\top x\) for every \(w\in\mathbb R^V\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite normalized submodular functions; inequalities use every subset of the ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The base polyhedron associated with \(f\) is
\[
B(f):=\bigl\{y\in\mathbb{R}^{V}:y(A)\le f(A)\text{ for every }A\subseteq V,\quad y(V)=f(V)\bigr\},
\]
where \(y(A):=\sum_{i\in A}y_i\). Thus a base is a modular lower bound on \(f\) that is tight on the full ground set. For finite normalized submodular \(f\), the polyhedron \(B(f)\) is nonempty; its extreme points are obtained from permutations of \(V\) by the greedy marginal-increment construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The base polyhedron consists of modular lower bounds on a normalized submodular function that agree with it on the entire ground set.
knowledge_statements.title: Base-Polyhedron View

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The base-polyhedron definition and accompanying nonemptiness and greedy-extreme-point claims are standard and mathematically consistent, but no inspectable citation supports them. The definition record also includes substantial property claims beyond its selected kind.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-element extension of a set-function pair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of the extended functions used to lift a generalized polymatroid to a base polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $S^*:=S\cup\{s^*\}$. For set functions $p,b$ on $S$, define $b^*,p^*$ on $2^{S^*}$ by
\[
b^*(X)=\begin{cases}b(X),&X\subseteq S,\\-p(S-X),&s^*\in X,\end{cases}\qquad
p^*(X)=\begin{cases}p(X),&X\subseteq S,\\-b(S-X),&s^*\in X.\end{cases}
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adjoin a new element to the ground set. On subsets not containing it, retain the original upper and lower set functions; on subsets containing it, define each extended function as the negative of the complementary value of the other original function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b^*,p^*:2^{S^*}\to\mathbb R\text{ are defined by the displayed piecewise formulas.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility of Coordinate-Bounded Near-Supermodular Base Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient conditions for lower-, upper-, and two-sided box intersections of a near-supermodular base polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let p_1 be near supermodular with p_1(S) finite, and let f:S	o\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\} and g:S	o\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\} satisfy f\leq g. Then B'(p_1)\cap T(f\leq)
eq\varnothing if and only if \widetilde f(S)\leq p_1(S) and, for every partition \{X_0,X_1,\ldots,X_t\} of S with t\geq1 and only X_0 possibly empty, \widetilde f(X_0)+\sum_{i=1}^{t}p_1(X_i)\leq p_1(S). Also, B'(p_1)\cap T(\leq g)
eq\varnothing if and only if \widetilde g(X)\geq p_1(X) for every X\subseteq S and \sum_{i=1}^{t}p_1(X_i)\leq p_1(S) for every partition \{X_1,\ldots,X_t\} of S with t\geq1. Finally, B'(p_1)\cap T(f,g)
eq\varnothing if and only if both one-sided intersections are nonempty. If p_1,f,g are integer-valued, the corresponding base polyhedra are integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a near-supermodular base polyhedron, feasibility under lower coordinate bounds is characterized by a ground-set inequality and mixed partition inequalities; feasibility under upper bounds is characterized by subset domination and partition inequalities. The two-sided box intersection is feasible exactly when both one-sided intersections are feasible, and integer data yield integral corresponding base polyhedra.
assumptions_latex: p_1,f,g\text{ are integer-valued for the integrality conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B'(p_1)\cap T(f\leq),\ B'(p_1)\cap T(\leq g),\text{ and }B'(p_1)\cap T(f,g)\text{ are nonempty exactly under the stated inequalities, and integer data imply integrality of the corresponding base polyhedra.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function identity on all of \(\mathbb{R}^V\), using the homogeneous Lovász-extension convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^V\), order the coordinates as \(x_{\pi(1)}\ge\cdots\ge x_{\pi(n)}\), put \(S_k=\{\pi(1),\ldots,\pi(k)\}\), and define \(y^\pi_{\pi(k)}=f(S_k)-f(S_{k-1})\). Then \(y^\pi\in B(f)\), and the greedy base maximizes the linear functional in direction \(x\). Consequently,
\[
\widehat f(x)=\langle y^\pi,x\rangle=\max_{y\in B(f)}\langle y,x\rangle.
\]
Ties in the ordering may change the maximizing base but not the maximum value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lovász extension is exactly the support function of the base polyhedron, with a maximizing base produced by greedy coordinate ordering.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard threshold-integral interface between submodular and convex minimization
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional reduction over the unit cube, not merely a relaxation bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The function \(f\) is submodular if and only if its Lovász extension \(\widehat f\) is convex. Moreover, for every \(x\in[0,1]^V\), the threshold sets \(S_t(x):=\{i\in V:x_i\ge t\}\) satisfy
\[
\widehat f(x)=\int_0^1 f(S_t(x))\,dt.
\]
Hence \(\widehat f(x)\ge\min_{S\subseteq V}f(S)\), while every incidence vector obeys \(\widehat f(\mathbf{1}_S)=f(S)\). Therefore
\[
\min_{x\in[0,1]^V}\widehat f(x)=\min_{S\subseteq V}f(S),
\]
and an optimal threshold set of any continuous minimizer is a discrete minimizer for almost every threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing a submodular function over subsets is equivalent to minimizing its convex Lovász extension over the unit cube.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Minimization Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimization equivalence and threshold conclusion are mathematically sound, but no source is cited and the statement contains a proof-style derivation that must be removed when sourced.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the unconstrained program.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical unconstrained finite submodular minimization program and minimizer-lattice property
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-valued unconstrained submodular minimization over the full power set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The unconstrained submodular program associated with \(f\) is
\[
p^*:=\min\{f(S):S\subseteq V\},\qquad
\operatorname{Argmin}f:=\{S\subseteq V:f(S)=p^*\}.
\]
Because \(2^V\) is finite, the minimum is attained. If \(A,B\in\operatorname{Argmin}f\), submodularity gives \(f(A\cap B)+f(A\cup B)\le 2p^*\); minimality forces both terms to equal \(p^*\). Thus the minimizers form a lattice under intersection and union and have unique inclusion-minimal and inclusion-maximal members.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unconstrained submodular program minimizes the set function over all subsets; its minimizers form a lattice under union and intersection.
knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained Submodular Programs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The program definition and minimizer-lattice property are correct, but they lack a citation. The record also embeds a proof and combines a definition with a nontrivial property theorem.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each multiplier \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\), define the Lagrangian set function and its optimal value by
\[
L_\lambda(S):=f(S)+\lambda^\top(g(S)-b),\qquad
q(\lambda):=\min_{S\subseteq V}L_\lambda(S).
\]
Since adding a modular function preserves submodularity, \(L_\lambda\) is submodular and evaluating \(q(\lambda)\) is an unconstrained submodular minimization problem. The Lagrangian dual program is \(d^*:=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}q(\lambda)\); its value supplies a lower bound for the associated constrained minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lagrangian submodular program adds nonnegative prices for modular constraint violations, leaving an unconstrained submodular minimization problem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Breakpoint Structure of Parametric Minimizer Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete breakpoint description when the scalar constraint function \(f_1\) is monotone decreasing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f_1\) is monotone decreasing. Then there exist \(\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_p\), with \(p\leq|E|\), such that the distinct values of \(\mathcal L(\lambda)\) for \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\) are the families \(\mathcal L(\lambda_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,p\), and the singleton families \(\{S^+(\lambda_i)\}=\{S^-(\lambda_{i+1})\}\), \(i=1,\ldots,p-1\). Furthermore, \(S^-(\lambda_1)=\varnothing\), \(S^+(\lambda_p)=E\), \[\mathcal L(\lambda)=\{S^+(\lambda_i)\}=\{S^-(\lambda_{i+1})\}\quad\text{when }\lambda_i<\lambda<\lambda_{i+1},\] and \[\mathcal L(\lambda)=\begin{cases}\{\varnothing\},&\lambda<\lambda_1,\\\{E\},&\lambda_p<\lambda.\end{cases}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the constraint function is monotone decreasing, the parametric minimizer families have at most |E| breakpoints. Between consecutive breakpoints there is one fixed minimizer, with only the empty set below the first breakpoint and only the ground set above the last.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_p,\quad p\leq|E|,\quad\text{with the stated complete breakpoint, interval, and endpoint description of }\mathcal L(\lambda).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given componentwise resource bounds \(b\), define
\[
\mathcal{F}_b:=\{S\subseteq V:g_j(S)\le b_j\text{ for }j=1,\ldots,m\}.
\]
The constrained submodular program is
\[
p^*:=\min_{S\in\mathcal{F}_b}f(S).
\]
The value is \(+\infty\) when \(\mathcal{F}_b=\varnothing\); otherwise finiteness of \(V\) ensures attainment. Although \(f\) is submodular, the feasible family need not be closed under union or intersection, so the lattice property of unconstrained minimizers does not automatically survive the constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained submodular program minimizes a submodular objective over subsets satisfying componentwise modular resource bounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximum-flow redistribution algorithm for Problem (*)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assumes the poset, lattice family, signed vertex sets, vectors, and Problem (*) defined in the surrounding submodular-program framework.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Start with nonnegative \(\varphi:B^*(\mathcal P)\to\mathbb R_+\), \(\alpha(p^+)\ge0\), and \(\beta(p^-)\ge0\) satisfying \(\sum_{p^+\in E^+}\alpha(p^+)\xi_{p^+}+\sum_{p^-\in E^-}\beta(p^-)\eta_{p^-}+\partial\varphi=x-\nu\), with \(\alpha(p)\beta(p)=0\) for \(p\in E^+\cap E^-\). Form the bidirected network with forward capacities \(\varphi(a)\) and reverse capacities \(+\infty\), and compute a maximum flow \(\psi\) from \(E^+\setminus E^-\) to \(E^-\setminus E^+\) satisfying flow conservation off \(E^+\cup E^-\), \(\partial\psi(p^+)\le\alpha(p^+)\), and \(-\partial\psi(p^-)\le\beta(p^-)\). Update \(\varphi(e,e')\leftarrow\varphi(e,e')-\psi(e,e')+\psi(e',e)\), \(\alpha(p^+)\leftarrow\alpha(p^+)-\partial\psi(p^+)\), and \(\beta(p^-)\leftarrow\beta(p^-)+\partial\psi(p^-)\); then find \(A\in\mathcal D\) such that \(\varphi(a)=0\) for \(a\in\Delta^-(A)\), \(\alpha(p^+)=0\) for \(p^+\in E^+\cap A\), and \(\beta(p^-)=0\) for \(p^-\in E^-\setminus A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decompose the residual vector into nonnegative signed coefficients and a nonnegative poset flow, send a constrained maximum flow through the associated bidirected network, update the decomposition by that flow, and select a lattice set A whose incoming arcs and incompatible signed coefficients all have zero residual value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists A\in\mathcal D:\ \varphi|_{\Delta^-(A)}=0,\ \alpha|_{E^+\cap A}=0,\ \beta|_{E^-\setminus A}=0

children.title: Lagrangian Relaxation Interface
children.top_down_role: Structural passage from constrained formulations to parameterized Lagrangian families.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Relaxation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak duality and an exact attained saddle-point criterion for finite set programs with modular upper-bound constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L_\lambda(S):=f(S)+\lambda^\top(g(S)-b)\) and \(q(\lambda):=\min_{S\subseteq V}L_\lambda(S)\) for \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\). For the primal and dual values
\[
p^*:=\min\{f(S):S\subseteq V,\ g(S)\le b\},\qquad d^*:=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m}q(\lambda),
\]
weak duality gives \(d^*\le p^*\). If a feasible set \(S^*\) and a multiplier \(\lambda^*\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\) satisfy
\[
S^*\in\operatorname{argmin}_{S\subseteq V}L_{\lambda^*}(S),\qquad \lambda_j^*(g_j(S^*)-b_j)=0\quad(j=1,\ldots,m),
\]
then \(d^*=p^*=f(S^*)\). Conversely, if the primal minimum and dual supremum are attained and \(d^*=p^*\), every primal-dual optimal pair satisfies these conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lagrangian values lower-bound the constrained optimum. A feasible Lagrangian minimizer with complementary slackness certifies equality, and attained zero-gap primal-dual optima satisfy the same conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(g:2^V\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is modular, \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and the primal program is feasible with finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^*\le p^*\), with equality under the stated Lagrangian optimality, feasibility, and complementary-slackness certificate.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V=\{1,2\}\), set \(f(\varnothing)=f(\{1\})=f(\{2\})=0\) and \(f(V)=-1\), and impose \(|S|\le1\). The function \(f\) is submodular and the constrained optimum is \(p^*=0\). For \(\lambda\ge0\),
\[
q(\lambda)=\min_{S\subseteq V}\{f(S)+\lambda(|S|-1)\}
             =\min\{-\lambda,0,-1+\lambda\}.
\]
Thus \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}q(\lambda)=-\tfrac12<p^*\). Hence submodularity and modular constraints alone do not guarantee exact Lagrangian relaxation; zero gap requires additional structure or a saddle-point certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Submodularity does not ensure strong Lagrangian duality: a two-element submodular problem with a cardinality bound has a positive relaxation gap.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality-parametric principal partition using inclusion-maximal minimizers and increasing parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The maximal minimizers \(S^+(\lambda)\) are nondecreasing with \(\lambda\). Let \(\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_r\) be the parameter values at which this maximal minimizer changes, and let
\[
\varnothing=S_0\subsetneq S_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq S_r=V
\]
be its successive values, with endpoint values understood for sufficiently small and sufficiently large \(\lambda\). The ordered family
\[
\mathcal{P}(f):=(S_1\setminus S_0,\ldots,S_r\setminus S_{r-1})
\]
is the principal partition of \(f\) under the cardinality parametrization; each block is labeled by the critical value at which it enters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The principal partition is formed by the successive blocks entering the maximal minimizer of a cardinality-parameterized submodular function.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak{S}(f)=\{(\lambda,\mathcal{M}_\lambda):\mathcal{M}_\lambda\text{ changes at }\lambda\}\) records the critical minimizer lattices.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(\lambda\), the family \(\mathcal{M}_\lambda\) is a nonempty distributive sublattice of \(2^V\), with least member \(S^-(\lambda)\) and greatest member \(S^+(\lambda)\). The principal structure of the cardinality-parametric family is the finite critical data
\[
\mathfrak{S}(f):=\bigl\{(\lambda,\mathcal{M}_\lambda):\mathcal{M}_\lambda\text{ changes at }\lambda\bigr\},
\]
together with the monotone extremal minimizers between critical values. It records not only the canonical maximal-minimizer chain but also all alternative minimizers occurring at ties.

children.title: Partition–Structure Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relationship between partition blocks and the encompassing principal structure.

assumptions_latex: The family \(f(S)-\lambda|S|\) uses inclusion-maximal minimizers to define its principal chain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_k=S_k\setminus S_{k-1}\) are exactly the elements entering the maximal minimizer at the \(k\)-th critical value.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard correspondence between the principal sequence and critical parametric minimizer lattices
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence for the maximal-minimizer convention; critical lattices retain refinements within tied blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_r\) be the critical values and \(\varnothing=S_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq S_r=V\) the successive inclusion-maximal minimizers. Then the ordered principal blocks satisfy
\[
P_k=S_k\setminus S_{k-1}\qquad(k=1,\ldots,r).
\]
Equivalently, \(S_k=P_1\cup\cdots\cup P_k\), so the labeled principal partition reconstructs the entire maximal-minimizer chain. At a critical value \(\lambda_k\), the associated minimizer lattice may contain sets strictly between its least and greatest members; this additional tie structure belongs to the principal structure but is not recoverable from the ordered blocks alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordered principal blocks and critical labels reconstruct the maximal-minimizer chain, while critical minimizer lattices additionally record alternatives created by ties.
