intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block-chain correspondence follows the candidate's stated convention, but the convention and the claimed division between principal partition and principal structure are unsupported by a source.

children.title: Degenerate Principal Regimes
children.top_down_role: Ties, collapsed levels, and nonunique structural decompositions.

assumptions_latex: Principal data are generated by minimizing \(f(S)-\lambda|S|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equal critical rates can merge several elements into one principal block and create multiple minimizers at the breakpoint.

notation.meaning: A modular submodular function with element weights \(c_i\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit modular example of degeneracy in cardinality-parametric minimization
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degeneracy means coincident critical values, not failure of submodularity or monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the modular, hence submodular, function \(f(S)=\sum_{i\in S}c_i\). A set minimizes \(f(S)-\lambda|S|\) by including every element with \(c_i<\lambda\), excluding every element with \(c_i>\lambda\), and choosing tied elements with \(c_i=\lambda\) arbitrarily. Therefore, if several elements share a value \(c\), the minimizer lattice at \(\lambda=c\) contains all choices of those tied elements, while the maximal minimizer adds them simultaneously as one block. In the extreme case \(c_i=c\) for every \(i\in V\), the principal chain jumps directly from \(\varnothing\) to \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coincident critical rates cause tied minimizers and merge several elements into one principal block; equal modular weights produce the extreme single-jump case.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Principal Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The modular tied-weight example and single-jump conclusion are mathematically correct and fit a failure-boundary leaf, but the record supplies no inspectable citation.

children.title: Minimum-Ratio Decompositions
children.top_down_role: Decompositions organized by minimum-ratio subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Ratio Decompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive minimum-ratio decomposition for a normalized submodular function with positive modular weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite, let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be normalized and submodular, and let \(w(S)=\sum_{i\in S}w_i\) with \(w_i>0\). Set \(A_0=\varnothing\). While \(A_{j-1}\ne V\), define \[\rho_j=\min_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V\setminus A_{j-1}}\frac{f(A_{j-1}\cup S)-f(A_{j-1})}{w(S)}.\] Let \(B_j\) be the inclusionwise maximal minimizer, and put \(A_j=A_{j-1}\cup B_j\). The ordered blocks \((B_1,\ldots,B_k)\), together with their ratios \((\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_k)\), form the minimum-ratio decomposition whenever every maximal minimizer is uniquely determined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successively choose the maximal nonempty block minimizing residual submodular value per unit weight; the resulting ordered partition and ratios constitute the minimum-ratio decomposition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((B_1,\ldots,B_k;\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_k)\) is the minimum-ratio decomposition of \((f,w)\).
review_flags: Exact project-intended convention for minimum-ratio decompositions requires an authoritative submodular-analysis source.
The existence and uniqueness convention for maximal tied minimizers needs source confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Minimum-Ratio Decompositions leaf and is internally coherent, but no cited source supports the intended contraction, ratio, or canonical maximal-minimizer convention. Source uncertainty prevents confirming that this is the exact project-intended decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Density Decompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Density formulation reciprocal to the positive-residual minimum-ratio decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the minimum-ratio construction, additionally assume \((f/A_{j-1})(S)>0\) for every nonempty residual set \(S\subseteq V\setminus A_{j-1}\). Define the residual density by \[d_{A_{j-1}}(S)=\frac{w(S)}{(f/A_{j-1})(S)}.\] At stage \(j\), choose the inclusionwise maximal set \(B_j\) maximizing \(d_{A_{j-1}}(S)\), set \(A_j=A_{j-1}\cup B_j\), and continue until \(A_k=V\). The ordered blocks and densities \((B_1,\delta_1),\ldots,(B_k,\delta_k)\), where \(\delta_j=d_{A_{j-1}}(B_j)\), form the density decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursively select the maximal residual block having greatest weight per unit residual submodular value; the blocks and attained densities form the density decomposition.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is normalized and submodular on finite \(V\).
\((f/A)(S)>0\) for each nonempty residual set considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((B_1,\delta_1),\ldots,(B_k,\delta_k)\) is the density decomposition of \((f,w)\).

notation.meaning: Density attained by the j-th block.
Union of the first j blocks.

children.title: Ratio–Density Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural links between minimum-ratio and density-based decompositions.

knowledge_statements.title: Ratio–Density Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reciprocal equivalence of minimum residual ratios and maximum residual densities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a residual stage with contracted function \(g=f/A\), and suppose \(g(S)>0\) and \(w(S)>0\) for every nonempty \(S\subseteq V\setminus A\). Then \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V\setminus A}\frac{g(S)}{w(S)}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V\setminus A}\frac{w(S)}{g(S)},\qquad \delta=\rho^{-1}.\] Consequently, applying the same inclusionwise-maximal tie rule at every contraction stage produces identical ordered blocks in the minimum-ratio and density decompositions, with \(\delta_j=1/\rho_j\) for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With positive residual values and weights, minimizing value per weight is equivalent to maximizing its reciprocal density; identical tie rules therefore yield identical blocks.
assumptions_latex: Both constructions use the same maximal tie rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_j^{\mathrm{ratio}}=B_j^{\mathrm{density}}\) and \(\delta_j=\rho_j^{-1}\) at every stage.

notation.meaning: Submodular contraction at the current accumulated set.

review_flags: The reciprocal identity is elementary, but the intended decomposition terminology and contraction convention lack a supporting source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reciprocal argmin-argmax identity is correct under strict positivity, and duality is an appropriate knowledge kind for this correspondence leaf. No source supports the named decomposition correspondence or confirms that the two recursive constructions use exactly these conventions.

children.title: Tied-Density Regimes
children.top_down_role: Degeneracies and aggregation effects caused by equal density levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Tied-Density Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lattice structure and canonical resolution of equal-density residual optimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:2^U\to\mathbb R\) be normalized and submodular, let \(w\) be positive modular, and fix \(\rho\in\mathbb R\). The minimizers of \(g(S)-\rho w(S)\) form a lattice: if \(S\) and \(T\) are minimizers, then \(S\cap T\) and \(S\cup T\) are minimizers. Hence, when the minimum value is \(0\), all sets satisfying \(g(S)/w(S)=\rho\) have a unique inclusionwise maximal union. Selecting that union gives a canonical block throughout a tied-density regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal optimal residual ratios are closed under union and intersection; their union is the unique maximal tied block and provides a canonical selection.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is finite and \(g\) is normalized submodular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{S\subseteq U}(g(S)-\rho w(S))\) is a lattice with a unique maximal member.
review_flags: A source is needed to certify that this lattice-based tie convention matches the intended decomposition framework.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lattice claim for minimizers of the parametric submodular objective is standard, and the unique maximal member follows on a finite ground set. A source is still required to connect this lattice selection rule to the exact Tied-Density Regimes container and intended decomposition framework.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integral decomposition of the submodular proximal duality gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies under the assumptions referenced in Proposition 8.1 to any base-polytope point and any primal vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the assumptions of Proposition 8.1, for \(s\in B(F)\) and \(w\in\mathbb{R}^p\), the gap defined in Eq. (8.3) satisfies
\[
\operatorname{gap}(w,s)=f(w)-w^\top s+\sum_{j=1}^p\left[\psi_j(w_j)+\psi_j^*(-s_j)+w_js_j\right]
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{gap}(w,s)=\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}\left[(F+\psi'(\alpha))(\{w\geq\alpha\})-(s+\psi'(\alpha))_-(V)\right]d\alpha.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal-dual gap decomposes into a Lovasz-extension residual plus coordinatewise conjugacy residuals and, equivalently, into an integral of threshold-set submodular residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{gap}(w,s)=f(w)-w^\top s+\sum_{j=1}^p\left[\psi_j(w_j)+\psi_j^*(-s_j)+w_js_j\right]=\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}\left[(F+\psi'(\alpha))(\{w\geq\alpha\})-(s+\psi'(\alpha))_-(V)\right]d\alpha.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: IFF Scaling Algorithm for Submodular Function Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scaling procedure based on extreme bases, augmenting paths, reduction, and double exchanges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a linear ordering $L_1$ and its associated extreme base $y_1$. Output $V$ if $y_1^+(V)=0$, and output $\varnothing$ if $y_1^-(V)=0$. Otherwise initialize $I=\{1\}$, $\lambda_1=1$, $x=y_1$, $\varphi=\mathbf 0$, and $\delta=\min\{x^+(V),|x^-(V)|\}/n^2$. Repeatedly form the set $W$ reachable from $S$ in $G_\varphi$. If $W\cap T\ne\varnothing$, augment along a $\delta$-augmenting path, reduce $(x,I)$, and repeat. If an active triple exists, apply Double-Exchange and repeat. Otherwise, output $W$ when $\delta<\Delta/n^2$; if not, reduce $(x,I)$, replace $\delta$ and $\varphi$ by $\delta/2$ and $\varphi/2$, and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The IFF scaling algorithm starts from an extreme base, alternates residual-network augmentations and active double exchanges, and halves its scale when neither operation applies. Its stated stopping tests return either a trivial minimizer or the final reachable set.
assumptions_latex: L_1\text{ is a linear ordering of }V

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fix-Minus Scaling Procedure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Procedure for detecting a sufficiently negative coordinate during an IFF fixing computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose any linear extension L_1 of D and its associated extreme base y_1. Initialize I=\{1\}, \lambda_1=1, x=y_1, \varphi=\mathbf 0, and \delta=\eta. Repeatedly let W be the vertices reachable from S in G_\varphi. If W\cap T\ne\varnothing, choose a \delta-augmenting path P, apply \operatorname{Augment}(\varphi,P) and \operatorname{Reduce}(x,I), and recompute W. Otherwise, if an active triple (i,u,v) exists, apply Double-Exchange and recompute W. If neither operation applies and some w\in U satisfies x(w)<-\widetilde n^2\delta, return such a w. Otherwise apply \operatorname{Reduce}(x,I), replace \delta by \delta/2 and \varphi by \varphi/2, and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from an extreme base associated with any linear extension of D. Repeatedly perform available augmentations or active-triple double exchanges. When neither applies, return a coordinate below the negative scaling threshold if one exists; otherwise reduce the representation, halve the scale and flow, and continue.
assumptions_latex: L_1\text{ is a linear extension of the partial order represented by }D.
y_1\text{ is the extreme base associated with }L_1.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Fix}^{-}(\widetilde\rho,D,\eta)\text{ executes the stated augmentation, exchange, threshold-test, and scale-halving loop, returning }w\in U\text{ when }x(w)<-\widetilde n^2\delta.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected-Subgradient Bound and Certificate for Submodular Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate submodular minimization obtained by rounding the projected-subgradient iterate through its superlevel sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the iterates \(w_t\) and subgradients \(s_0,\ldots,s_t\) generated by the stated projected-subgradient scheme, after \(t>0\) steps there is a set \(B\) among the \(p\) superlevel sets of \(w_t\) such that
\[
F(B)-\min_{A\subseteq V}F(A)\leq \frac{D\sqrt p}{\sqrt{2t}},
\qquad D^2=\sum_{k=1}^p\alpha_k^2.
\]
Moreover, with
\[
\bar s_t=\frac{1}{t+1}\sum_{u=0}^t s_u,
\]
that set satisfies
\[
F(B)-(\bar s_t)_-(V)\leq \frac{D\sqrt p}{\sqrt{2t}}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the projected-subgradient scheme in the proposition, after t positive steps one of the p superlevel sets of the iterate has objective error at most D square root of p divided by square root of 2t. The averaged subgradient gives an optimality certificate with the same bound.
assumptions_latex: (w_t,s_0,\ldots,s_t)\text{ are generated by the stated projected-subgradient scheme}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists B\in\operatorname{SupLevels}(w_t):\quad F(B)-\min_{A\subseteq V}F(A)\leq\frac{D\sqrt p}{\sqrt{2t}},\quad F(B)-(\bar s_t)_-(V)\leq\frac{D\sqrt p}{\sqrt{2t}}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cubic-time posimodular extension and modular-perturbation boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of posimodularity, scope of the specialized regular-minimization algorithm, and the failure of that scope under general modular perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set function $F:2^V\to\mathbb{R}$ is posimodular if, for all $A,B\subseteq V$, $F(A)+F(B)\geq F(A\setminus B)+F(B\setminus A)$. The specialized $O(p^3)$ symmetric-minimization algorithm also applies to regular minimization of posimodular functions. Posimodular functions include symmetric submodular functions, nondecreasing modular functions, and sums of such functions, but not arbitrary modular functions with potentially negative coefficients. Moreover, even for symmetric functions, minimizing a modular perturbation $F(A)-z(A)$ can be as hard as general submodular-function minimization, so this algorithm does not generally solve the corresponding proximal problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Posimodularity requires the values on two sets to dominate the values on their directed differences. The cubic symmetric-minimization algorithm extends to regular minimization of this class, which includes symmetric submodular functions, nondecreasing modular functions, and their sums. Arbitrary signed modular functions are not included, and subtracting a modular function can restore the difficulty of general submodular minimization; consequently, the algorithm is not a general proximal solver for symmetric functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ admits regular minimization by the specialized }O(p^3)\text{ algorithm, but this guarantee does not generally extend to }F-z\text{ for modular }z.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proximal Duality-Gap Certificate for Submodular Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of a primal-dual gap for the proximal Lovász-extension problem into a discrete submodular-minimization certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((w,s)\in\mathbb R^p\times B(F)\) be primal-dual candidates for minimizing
\[
\frac12\lVert w\rVert_2^2+f(w),
\]
with duality gap
\[
\varepsilon=\frac12\lVert w\rVert_2^2+f(w)+\frac12\lVert s\rVert_2^2.
\]
If \(A\) is a superlevel set of \(w\) having the smallest value of \(F\) among its superlevel sets, then
\[
F(A)-s_-(V)\leq\sqrt{\frac{p\varepsilon}{2}}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given primal-dual candidates for the proximal problem, select a superlevel set of the primal vector with minimum submodular value. Its objective value exceeds the dual certificate by at most the square root of p times the duality gap divided by two.
assumptions_latex: F:2^V\to\mathbb R\text{ is submodular and }f\text{ is its associated convex extension}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(A)-s_-(V)\leq\sqrt{\frac{p\varepsilon}{2}}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support-and-Ordering Certificate for Submodular Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient conditions under which a represented base and a subset jointly certify the base-polyhedron min–max optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i y_i\) be a represented base associated with \(\{(L_i,\lambda_i)\mid i\in I\}\), and let \(W\subseteq V\). If \(\operatorname{supp}^-(x)\subseteq W\) and \(\operatorname{supp}^+(x)\subseteq V\setminus W\), then \(x^-(V)=x(W)\). If \(u\prec_i v\) for every \(u\in W\), \(v\in V\setminus W\), and \(i\in I\), then \(x(W)=\rho(W)\). If both sets of conditions hold, then \(x\) and \(W\) attain the maximum and minimum, respectively, in the base-polyhedron min–max formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a base represented as a convex combination of ordering-generated bases, sign support separated by W gives equality between the total negative part and x(W). If every representing ordering places W before its complement, x(W) equals rho(W). Together these conditions certify that x and W are optimal in the base-polyhedron min–max problem.
assumptions_latex: \(x=\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i y_i\) is a base represented by \(\{(L_i,\lambda_i)\mid i\in I\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated support condition implies \(x^-(V)=x(W)\); the stated ordering condition implies \(x(W)=\rho(W)\); together they imply optimality of \(x\) and \(W\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restriction–Contraction Characterization of a Submodular Minimizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient conditions separating minimization over subsets of a candidate set from minimization of additions outside it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) be submodular with \(F(\varnothing)=0\), and let \(A\subseteq V\). Then \(A\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{C\subseteq V}F(C)\) if and only if
\[A\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\subseteq A}F(B)\]
and
\[\varnothing\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\subseteq V\setminus A}\bigl(F(A\cup B)-F(A)\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set A globally minimizes a normalized submodular function exactly when A minimizes its restriction to subsets of A and the empty set minimizes the residual function for additions from outside A.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{C\subseteq V}F(C)\iff\left[A\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\subseteq A}F(B)\land\varnothing\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\subseteq V\setminus A}\bigl(F(A\cup B)-F(A)\bigr)\right]

knowledge_statements.title: Base-Polyhedron Min–Max Framework
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Edmonds-type min–max identity for normalized submodular-function minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be normalized and submodular, and define \[B(f)=\{x\in\mathbb R^V:x(S)\le f(S)\text{ for every }S\subseteq V,\ x(V)=f(V)\}.\] Then \[\min_{S\subseteq V}f(S)=\max_{x\in B(f)}\sum_{i\in V}\min\{x_i,0\}.\] Thus every base supplies a lower bound on every set value through its negative coordinates, and an optimal base attains the minimum set value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum of a normalized submodular function equals the largest sum of negative coordinates attainable by a vector in its base polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{S\subseteq V}f(S)=\max_{x\in B(f)}\sum_{i\in V}\min\{x_i,0\}\).

notation.meaning: Sum of the negative parts of x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuous Fair Resource Allocation with Submodular Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the continuous model and its lower and upper coordinate thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R\) be nondecreasing in its first argument and nonincreasing in its second, and for every \(e\in E\) let \(h_e:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, nondecreasing, and onto. The continuous fair resource-allocation problem is
\[
(P_3)\qquad \min_{x\in B_{\mathbb R}(f)}g\!\left(\max_{e\in E}h_e(x(e)),\min_{e\in E}h_e(x(e))\right).
\]
If \(v_*\) and \(v^*\) are respectively the optimal values of the associated max–min and min–max problems, define
\[
l(e)=\min\{\alpha\in\mathbb R:h_e(\alpha)\ge v_*\},\qquad
u(e)=\max\{\alpha\in\mathbb R:h_e(\alpha)\le v^*\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For monotone coordinate transformations, continuous fair resource allocation minimizes a function that increases with the largest transformed allocation and decreases with the smallest transformed allocation, subject to membership in a real base polyhedron. Coordinate thresholds l and u are obtained by inverting the associated max–min and min–max optimal levels.
assumptions_latex: g:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R\text{ is nondecreasing in its first argument and nonincreasing in its second}
\forall e\in E,\ h_e:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\text{ is continuous, nondecreasing, and onto}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (P_3)=\min_{x\in B_{\mathbb R}(f)}g\!\left(\max_{e\in E}h_e(x(e)),\min_{e\in E}h_e(x(e))\right),\quad l(e)=\min\{\alpha:h_e(\alpha)\ge v_*\},\quad u(e)=\max\{\alpha:h_e(\alpha)\le v^*\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Greedy optimization over submodular and base polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy construction and support-function identities for a normalized submodular function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:2^{[p]}\to\mathbb{R} be submodular with F(\varnothing)=0. For w\in\mathbb{R}^p, choose an ordering w_{j_1}\ge\cdots\ge w_{j_p}, set A_k=\{j_1,\ldots,j_k\}, A_0=\varnothing, and define s_{j_k}=F(A_k)-F(A_{k-1}). Then s\in B(F). If w\in\mathbb{R}_+^p, then s\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in P(F)}w^\top u and \max_{u\in P(F)}w^\top u=f(w). For arbitrary w\in\mathbb{R}^p, s\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in B(F)}w^\top u and \max_{u\in B(F)}w^\top u=f(w), where f is the Lov\'asz extension of F.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a normalized submodular function, sort the weights and assign each coordinate the successive marginal value along the resulting chain. The constructed vector lies in the base polyhedron. It maximizes a nonnegative weighted linear objective over the submodular polyhedron and an arbitrary weighted linear objective over the base polyhedron; in each case the optimum is the Lovász extension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s\in B(F),\quad w\ge0\Rightarrow\max_{u\in P(F)}w^\top u=w^\top s=f(w),\quad\text{and}\quad\max_{u\in B(F)}w^\top u=w^\top s=f(w)\ \forall w\in\mathbb{R}^p.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Algorithm for the Discrete Fair Resource Allocation Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the referenced definitions of the integer programs, bounds, sets, functions, and integral bounded base polyhedra from the source context.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve \(IP_*\) and \(IP^*\), obtain optimal values \(\widehat v_*\) and \(\widehat v^*\), and construct \(\widehat l,\widehat u\). If \(\widehat l\leq\widehat u\), any \(x\in B_{\mathbf Z}(f)_{\widehat l}^{\widehat u}\) is optimal for \(IP_3\). Otherwise form \(D\), the distinct values \(d_1<\cdots<d_k\), and sets \(A_i\), and minimize the listed \(k+1\) candidate values \(g(\widehat v^*,d_1)\) and \(g(\max_{e\in A_i}\widehat h_e(\widehat u(e)+1),d_{i+1})\), \(i=1,\ldots,k\). If the first candidate is minimal, any \(\widehat x\in B_{\mathbf Z}(f)_{\widehat l\wedge\widehat u}^{\widehat u}\) is optimal. If a candidate indexed by \(i^*\) is minimal, set \(w^*=\max_{e\in A_{i^*}}\widehat h_e(\widehat u(e)+1)\), define \(l^0(e)=\min\{\alpha\in\mathbf Z:\widehat h_e(\alpha)\geq d_{i^*+1}\}\) and \(u^0(e)=\max\{\alpha\in\mathbf Z:\widehat h_e(\alpha)\leq w^*\}\) for every \(e\in E\); then any \(\widehat z\in B_{\mathbf Z}(f)_{l^0}^{u^0}\) is optimal for \(IP_3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the two auxiliary integer programs and construct their induced lower and upper bounds. If those bounds are compatible, every integral base satisfying them solves the fair-allocation problem. Otherwise compare the prescribed candidate objective values. A minimum attained by the first candidate yields an optimum in the corresponding bounded integral base polyhedron; a minimum attained by an indexed candidate defines new componentwise bounds from the discrete functions, and every integral base within those bounds is optimal.
assumptions_latex: IP_*,IP^*,IP_3,\widehat h_e,g,D,A_i,\widehat l,\widehat u\text{ are defined as in the source context.}
\widehat v_*\text{ and }\widehat v^*\text{ are optimal objective values of }IP_*\text{ and }IP^*,\text{ respectively.}
d_1<\cdots<d_k\text{ are the distinct values prescribed for }D.
B_{\mathbf Z}(f)_l^u\text{ denotes the integral bases of }f\text{ satisfying }l\leq x\leq u.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Each termination branch returns an optimal solution of }IP_3.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transfer of a Base-Polyhedron Optimum to the Submodular Polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Under the separable convex-duality hypotheses inherited from the referenced base-polyhedron result.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose $(v,t)$ is primal–dual optimal for
\[
\min_{v\in\mathbb R^p}\left\{f(v)+\sum_{k\in V}\psi_k(v_k)\right\}
=
\max_{t\in B(F)}\left\{-\sum_{k\in V}\psi_k^*(-t_k)\right\}.
\]
For each $k\in V$, let $s_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{r\le t_k}\{-\psi_k^*(-r)\}$, and set $w=v_+$ componentwise. Then $(w,s)$ is primal–dual optimal for
\[
\min_{w\in\mathbb R_+^p}\left\{f(w)+\sum_{k\in V}\psi_k(w_k)\right\}
=
\max_{s\in P(F)}\left\{-\sum_{k\in V}\psi_k^*(-s_k)\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a primal–dual optimum for the separable problem over the base polyhedron, take the componentwise positive part of the primal solution and maximize each conjugate term over the half-line ending at the corresponding dual coordinate. The resulting pair is optimal for the nonnegative primal problem dual to optimization over the submodular polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ and }(f,\psi_k)_{k\in V}\text{ satisfy the hypotheses of the underlying separable base-polyhedron duality result}
(v,t)\text{ is primal\text{–}dual optimal for the problem over }B(F)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (w,s)\text{ is primal\text{–}dual optimal for the stated problem over }\mathbb R_+^p\text{ and }P(F).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global bounds from singleton values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds every value of a finite-ground-set submodular function and gives an oracle-efficient uniform magnitude bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f:2^U\to\mathbb R$ be submodular. For every $S\subseteq U$, letting $C=\sum_{u\in U}\max\{0,f(\{u\})-f(\varnothing)\}$, one has $f(U)-C\le f(S)\le f(\varnothing)+C$. Consequently, a number $B$ satisfying $|f(S)|\le B$ for every $S\subseteq U$ can be computed in linear time using $|U|+2$ oracle calls to $f$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any submodular function on a finite ground set, every function value lies between bounds determined by the values at the empty set, the full set, and all singletons. These values yield a uniform absolute bound in linear time with exactly |U|+2 oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(U)-\sum_{u\in U}\max\{0,f(\{u\})-f(\varnothing)\}\le f(S)\le f(\varnothing)+\sum_{u\in U}\max\{0,f(\{u\})-f(\varnothing)\},\quad \exists B\ \forall S\subseteq U:\ |f(S)|\le B,\text{ computable with }|U|+2\text{ oracle calls in linear time}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tolerance and Objective-Gap Certificate for Exact Submodular Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Context-dependent approximate negative-part bounds and an exactness threshold under graph and activity conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(S\subseteq W\subseteq V\setminus T\), no arc leaves \(W\) in \(G_\varphi\), and no active triple exists, then \[z^-(V)\geq \rho(W)-n\delta,\qquad x^-(V)\geq \rho(W)-n^2\delta.\] Moreover, if \(\delta<\Delta/n^2\), where \[\Delta\leq\min\{\rho(X)-\rho(Y)\mid X,Y\subseteq V,\ \rho(X)-\rho(Y)>0\},\] then \(W\) is a minimizer of \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated containment, no-leaving-arc, and no-active-triple conditions, the negative-part values of z and x are bounded below by rho(W) minus n delta and n squared delta. If delta is below the stated positive-objective-gap threshold, W is an exact minimizer.
assumptions_latex: For the exactness conclusion, \(\delta<\Delta/n^2\) and \(\Delta\leq\min\{\rho(X)-\rho(Y)\mid X,Y\subseteq V,\ \rho(X)-\rho(Y)>0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^-(V)\geq\rho(W)-n\delta\) and \(x^-(V)\geq\rho(W)-n^2\delta\); under the stated gap threshold, \(W\in\arg\min_{X\subseteq V}\rho(X)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transfer to the Symmetric Submodular Polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A signed primal–dual transformation for a nondecreasing submodular function under the separable convex-duality hypotheses inherited from the referenced base result.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $F$ be submodular and nondecreasing. For each $k\in V$, choose $\varepsilon_k\in\{-1,1\}$ as the sign prescribed by $(\psi_k^*)'(0)$, with either sign allowed when this value is zero. Suppose $(v,t)$ is primal–dual optimal for
\[
\min_{v\in\mathbb R^p}\left\{f(v)+\sum_{k\in V}\psi_k(\varepsilon_kv_k)\right\}
=
\max_{t\in B(F)}\left\{-\sum_{k\in V}\psi_k^*(-\varepsilon_kt_k)\right\}.
\]
Set $w=\varepsilon\circ v_+$. For each $k$, choose $r_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{r\le t_k}\{-\psi_k^*(-\varepsilon_kr)\}$ and set $s_k=\varepsilon_kr_k$. Then $(w,s)$ is primal–dual optimal for
\[
\min_{w\in\mathbb R^p}\left\{f(|w|)+\sum_{k\in V}\psi_k(w_k)\right\}
=
\max_{s\in |P|(F)}\left\{-\sum_{k\in V}\psi_k^*(-s_k)\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nondecreasing submodular function, select coordinate signs from the conjugates at zero. A signed base-polyhedron optimum can then be transformed, using the positive part of the primal vector and coordinatewise half-line conjugate maximizers, into a primal–dual optimum for the problem over the symmetric submodular polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ and }(f,\psi_k)_{k\in V}\text{ satisfy the hypotheses of the underlying separable base-polyhedron duality result}
\varepsilon_k\in\{-1,1\}\text{ is the prescribed sign of }(\psi_k^*)'(0),\text{ with either sign permitted if it is zero}
(v,t)\text{ is primal\text{–}dual optimal for the stated signed problem over }B(F)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (w,s)\text{ is primal\text{–}dual optimal for the stated problem over }\mathbb R^p\text{ and }|P|(F).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Min–Max Formulas and Tight-Set Certificates for Submodular Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Base-polyhedron and nonpositive submodular-polyhedron dual representations, including equality conditions certifying primal and dual optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) be submodular with \(F(\varnothing)=0\), and define \((s_-)_{k}=\min\{s_k,0\}\). Then
\[\min_{A\subseteq V}F(A)=\max_{s\in B(F)}s_-(V)=F(V)-\min_{s\in B(F)}\lVert s\rVert_1.\]
For every \(A\subseteq V\) and \(s\in B(F)\),
\[F(A)\ge s_-(V),\]
with equality if and only if
\[\{k\in V:s_k<0\}\subseteq A\subseteq\{k\in V:s_k\le0\}\quad\text{and}\quad s(A)=F(A).\]
Also,
\[\min_{A\subseteq V}F(A)=\max_{\substack{s\in P(F)\\s\le0}}s(V).\]
For every \(A\subseteq V\) and \(s\in P(F)\) with \(s\le0\),
\[F(A)\ge s(V),\]
with equality if and only if
\[\{k\in V:s_k<0\}\subseteq A\quad\text{and}\quad s(A)=F(A).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum of a normalized submodular function equals a maximum of the summed negative coordinates over its base polyhedron, equivalently the stated minimum-l1 expression, and also equals the maximum total weight over nonpositive vectors in its submodular polyhedron. Equality in the associated weak-duality bounds is characterized by tightness of A together with the stated sign-containment conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{A\subseteq V}F(A)=\max_{s\in B(F)}s_-(V)=F(V)-\min_{s\in B(F)}\lVert s\rVert_1=\max_{\substack{s\in P(F)\\s\le0}}s(V),\text{ with the stated tightness and sign conditions characterizing equality}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional Gradient over a Submodular Base Polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General conditional-gradient method specialized to minimizing a smooth convex function over a compact submodular base polyhedron; the extracted certificate is retained with its stated sign orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $g:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}$ be convex and differentiable with $L$-Lipschitz gradient, and let $B(F)$ be a compact base polyhedron. Starting from $s_0\in B(F)$, for $t\ge1$ choose $\bar s_{t-1}\in\arg\min_{s\in B(F)}\nabla g(s_{t-1})^\top(s-s_{t-1})$ and set $s_t=\rho_{t-1}\bar s_{t-1}+(1-\rho_{t-1})s_{t-1}$. Either $\rho_{t-1}=2/(t+1)$ or a line search on the quadratic upper model induced by $L$ may be used. If $\alpha_k=F(\{k\})+F(V\setminus\{k\})-F(V)$, then $g(s_t)-\min_{s\in B(F)}g(s)\le L\sum_{k=1}^p\alpha_k^2/(t+1)$. As extracted, $\max_{s\in B(F)}\nabla g(s_t)^\top(s-s_t)$ is asserted to upper-bound the suboptimality and to converge at the same rate up to constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For smooth convex minimization over a compact submodular base polyhedron, conditional gradient repeatedly minimizes the current linearization and moves toward that minimizer. A fixed step size 2/(t+1) or line search on the Lipschitz-gradient quadratic upper model gives an O(1/t) objective bound controlled by the squared coordinate widths of the base polyhedron. The extract also asserts a computable linearization-gap certificate, although its displayed sign orientation should be verified.
assumptions_latex: B(F)\subset\mathbb{R}^p\text{ is a compact base polyhedron}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g(s_t)-\min_{s\in B(F)}g(s)\le\frac{L\sum_{k=1}^p\alpha_k^2}{t+1}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support-Function Membership and Separation Oracle Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General support-halfspace oracle conditions together with their base-polyhedron specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p be a closed convex set with 0\in K and finite attained support function h(w)=\max_{u\in K}w^\top u. Then h(w)\ge 0 and K=\bigcap_{w\in\mathbb{R}^p}\{s\in\mathbb{R}^p:s^\top w\le h(w)\}. The method assumes an efficient membership test and, for every s\notin K, an efficiently obtainable w with s^\top w>h(w). This separation can be implemented when \max_{h(w)\le1}w^\top s is efficiently computable. For K=B(F), where F is nonnegative and submodular, the source gives \max_{h(w)\le1}w^\top s=\max_{\varnothing\ne A\subseteq V}s(A)/F(A), computable efficiently when F(A)-t(A) can be minimized efficiently over A\subseteq V for arbitrary t\in\mathbb{R}^p.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex set containing the origin is described by its support halfspaces, and its support function is nonnegative. The method requires an efficient membership test that returns a violated support inequality for an exterior point. For a base polyhedron of a nonnegative submodular function, the required polar-gauge maximization reduces to maximizing s(A)/F(A), with tractability supplied by efficient minimization of F-t.
assumptions_latex: K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\text{ is closed and convex, }0\in K
h(w)=\max_{u\in K}w^\top u\text{ is finite and attained}
\text{Membership and separating-certificate operations are required to be efficient}
K=B(F)\text{ in the specialization, with }F\text{ nonnegative and submodular}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: h(w)\ge0,\quad K=\bigcap_w\{s:s^\top w\le h(w)\},\quad s\notin K\Rightarrow\exists w:\ s^\top w>h(w);\qquad K=B(F)\Rightarrow\max_{h(w)\le1}w^\top s=\max_{\varnothing\ne A\subseteq V}\frac{s(A)}{F(A)}.

knowledge_statements.title: Sign Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Base-vector signs provide a universally checkable lower bound for submodular minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in B(f)\), and write \(N(x)=\{i\in V:x_i<0\}\). For every \(T\subseteq V\), \[f(T)\ge x(T)\ge\sum_{i\in N(x)}x_i=\sum_{i\in V}\min\{x_i,0\}.\] Therefore \(x\), together with its coordinate signs, certifies the lower bound \(\sum_i\min\{x_i,0\}\) on \(\min_T f(T)\). If a set attains this bound, the certificate is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A base vector’s negative-coordinate sum is a certified lower bound on every set value; equality for a set proves that set is optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is normalized and submodular on finite \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(T)\ge\sum_{i\in V}\min\{x_i,0\}\) for every \(T\subseteq V\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Order-pivot convex decomposition for submodular base vectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The decomposition subroutine used by a strongly polynomial submodular-function minimization method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^S\to\mathbb R\) be submodular, let \(\prec\) be a total order on \(S\), and let \(s\prec t\). For \(u\in(s,t]_{\prec}\), let \(\prec^{s,u}\) be obtained by moving \(u\) immediately before \(s\). In strongly polynomial time one can find \(\delta\ge0\) and coefficients \(\mu_u\ge0\), \(\sum_u\mu_u=1\), such that \[b^{\prec}+\delta(\chi^t-\chi^s)=\sum_{u\in(s,t]_{\prec}}\mu_u b^{\prec^{s,u}}.\] After translating so that \(b^{\prec}=0\), each reordered vector satisfies \(b^{\prec^{s,u}}(v)\le0\) for \(s\preccurlyeq v\prec u\), \(b^{\prec^{s,u}}(u)\ge0\), and \(b^{\prec^{s,u}}(v)=0\) otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a submodular function and two ordered elements s before t, a strongly polynomial subroutine moves elements of the interval one at a time before s and expresses a nonnegative exchange from s to t as a convex combination of the resulting greedy base vectors. Under normalization of the original base vector to zero, every reordered vector is nonpositive between s and the moved element, nonnegative at that element, and zero elsewhere.
assumptions_latex: \prec\text{ is a total order on the finite set }S
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\delta\ge0,\ \exists(\mu_u)_{u\in(s,t]_{\prec}}:\ \mu_u\ge0,\ \sum_u\mu_u=1,\quad b^{\prec}+\delta(\chi^t-\chi^s)=\sum_u\mu_u b^{\prec^{s,u}},\text{ computably in strongly polynomial time}

children.title: Tight-Set Certificates
children.top_down_role: Optimality evidence encoded by tight subsets and tight families.

knowledge_statements.title: Tight-Set Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A tight set compatible with base-vector signs certifies global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in B(f)\) and \(S\subseteq V\). Suppose \(S\) is tight for \(x\), meaning \(x(S)=f(S)\), and suppose \[\{i:x_i<0\}\subseteq S\subseteq\{i:x_i\le0\}.\] Then \[f(S)=x(S)=\sum_{i\in V}\min\{x_i,0\}\le f(T)\qquad\text{for every }T\subseteq V.\] Hence the verifiable pair \((x,S)\) certifies that \(S\) globally minimizes \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A base-tight set containing every negative coordinate and no positive coordinate attains the base lower bound and is therefore a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{T\subseteq V}f(T)\).

notation.meaning: Tightness of S for the base vector x.
The base-vector and tight-set certificate pair.

review_flags: The certificate follows from the min–max framework, but a supporting submodular-optimization source is absent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The tightness and sign conditions correctly force equality with the negative-coordinate lower bound, and the record fits the Tight-Set Certificates leaf. It cannot pass source review without an authoritative submodular-optimization citation and specific locator.

children.title: Sign–Tightness Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural links between sign patterns and tight-set organization.

knowledge_statements.title: Sign–Tightness Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equivalence between minimizers and sign-compatible tight bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be normalized and submodular. A set \(S\subseteq V\) minimizes \(f\) if and only if there exists \(x\in B(f)\) such that \[x(S)=f(S),\qquad x_i\le0\ \text{for all }i\in S,\qquad x_i\ge0\ \text{for all }i\in V\setminus S.\] Equivalently, \(S\) is tight and contains every strictly negative coordinate of \(x\) while excluding every strictly positive coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set minimizes a normalized submodular function exactly when some base is tight on it and has nonpositive signs inside and nonnegative signs outside.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\iff\exists x\in B(f):x(S)=f(S),\ x_S\le0,\ x_{V\setminus S}\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Every coordinate indexed by S is nonpositive.

review_flags: The converse direction requires an authoritative base-polyhedron optimality theorem locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated equivalence matches the Sign-Tightness Correspondence leaf and theorem is the correct content kind. The converse existence of a sign-compatible tight base is nontrivial and requires an authoritative theorem locator.

children.title: Certificate Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where one certificate form is incomplete or nonunique.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tightness, sign compatibility, and base feasibility are each essential to the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: None of the three certificate requirements may simply be omitted. For the modular function \(f(S)=\sum_{i\in S}c_i\), its unique base is \(x=c\). If \(V=\{1,2\}\) and \(c=(-1,1)\), the tight set \(\{2\}\) is not minimizing because it violates sign compatibility, while the sign-compatible set \(\{1\}\) is certified precisely because it is tight. More generally, a vector with the desired signs but outside \(B(f)\) need not provide any valid lower bound. Thus base feasibility, tightness, and sign compatibility are jointly required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tightness alone can select a nonminimizer, signs outside the base polyhedron give no lower bound, and exact certification requires all three conditions together.
assumptions_latex: \(V=\{1,2\}\) and \(c=(-1,1)\) for the explicit tightness example.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=\{2\}\) is tight but not minimizing, demonstrating failure without sign compatibility.

notation.meaning: Coefficient vector of the modular counterexample.
Base polyhedron of the modular function.

review_flags: The explicit example is directly checkable, but a source is needed for the claimed general certificate boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit modular example correctly shows that tightness without sign compatibility does not certify minimization, and failure_boundary is the exact mathematical role. The broader assertion about the joint necessity of base feasibility, tightness, and signs has no cited source or fully specified counterexample for each omitted condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Lattice Structure of Minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of submodular minimizers under union and intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be submodular, and let \(S,T\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{U\subseteq V}f(U)\). Then \[f(S\cap T)+f(S\cup T)\le f(S)+f(T).\] Since each term on the left is at least the minimum value, equality holds and both \(S\cap T\) and \(S\cup T\) are minimizers. Consequently the minimizer family is a distributive sublattice of \(2^V\), with a unique inclusionwise minimal minimizer and a unique inclusionwise maximal minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The intersection and union of any two submodular minimizers are also minimizers, yielding unique smallest and largest minimizers on a finite ground set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S,T\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\implies S\cap T,S\cup T\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\).

notation.meaning: Family of subsets attaining the minimum of f.
Boolean lattice of subsets of V.

review_flags: Standard theorem, but no supplied locator addresses submodular minimizer lattices.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lattice theorem is standard and correctly stated for a finite ground set, but no authoritative locator is supplied. The sentences deriving equality and closure are proof text and must be removed when a sourced replacement is prepared.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Implication-digraph characterization of a lattice family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes membership in a finite lattice family from its intersection, union, and implication relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a lattice family $\mathcal C\subseteq2^E$, let $R_{\mathcal C}=\bigcap_{S\in\mathcal C}S$, $U_{\mathcal C}=\bigcup_{S\in\mathcal C}S$, and $A_{\mathcal C}=\{(i,j)\in E^2:\forall S\in\mathcal C,\ i\in S\Rightarrow j\in S\}$. Then, for every $T\subseteq E$, $$T\in\mathcal C\iff R_{\mathcal C}\subseteq T\subseteq U_{\mathcal C}\ \text{and}\ \nexists(i,j)\in A_{\mathcal C}\text{ with }i\in T,1j\notin T.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set belongs to the lattice family exactly when it contains every mandatory element, uses only elements occurring in the family, and violates no implication arc.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\in\mathcal C\iff R_{\mathcal C}\subseteq T\subseteq U_{\mathcal C}\text{ and }\forall(i,j)\in A_{\mathcal C},\ i\in T\Rightarrow j\in T

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lattice families and poset ideals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines lattice families and records their basic connection with ideals of finite posets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $E$ be finite. A nonempty family $\mathcal C\subseteq 2^E$ is a lattice (ring) family if $S,T\in\mathcal C$ implies $S\cap T,S\cup T\in\mathcal C$. If $(P,\leq)$ is a poset, an ideal is a set $I\subseteq P$ such that $x\in I$ and $y\leq x$ imply $y\in I$; the ideals form a lattice family. For a lattice family define $R_{\mathcal C}:=\bigcap_{T\in\mathcal C}T$, $U_{\mathcal C}:=\bigcup_{T\in\mathcal C}T$, and $A_{\mathcal C}:=\{(i,j)\in E^2:\forall T\in\mathcal C,\ i\in T\Rightarrow j\in T\}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lattice family is a nonempty family of subsets closed under union and intersection. Ideals of a poset form such a family. Its mandatory elements, possible elements, and membership implications are encoded by the intersection, union, and implication digraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S,T\in\mathcal C\Rightarrow S\cap T,S\cup T\in\mathcal C

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure and extension of a lattice-family submodular function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combines the induced closure operator, lattice-domain submodularity, and a penalized extension to the full power set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\mathcal C\subseteq2^E$ be a lattice family with $R_{\mathcal C}=\varnothing$ and $U_{\mathcal C}=E$. For $X\subseteq E$, define $\bar X:=\bigcap\{S\in\mathcal C:X\subseteq S\}$, the least member of $\mathcal C$ containing $X$; equivalently, $\bar X$ consists of $X$ and all vertices reachable from $X$ in the implication digraph. A function $f:\mathcal C\to\mathbb R$ is submodular when $$f(S\cap T)+f(S\cup T)\leq f(S)+f(T)\quad(S,T\in\mathcal C).$$ If $f$ is submodular and $K$ is sufficiently large, then $$\bar f(X):=f(\bar X)+K|\bar X\setminus X|\quad(X\subseteq E)$$ is submodular on $2^E$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lattice family induces a least-closed-superset operator computable by reachability in its implication digraph. Submodularity is defined using union and intersection inside the family, and a sufficiently large penalty for missing closure elements extends any such function to a submodular function on all subsets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar f(X)=f(\bar X)+K|\bar X\setminus X|\text{ defines a submodular function on }2^E

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Norm Base Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The minimum-Euclidean-norm base identifies the extremal minimizers by coordinate signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be normalized and submodular, and let \(x^*\) be the unique solution of \[\min_{x\in B(f)}\frac12\lVert x\rVert_2^2.\] Define \(S^- =\{i\in V:x_i^*<0\}\) and \(S^0=\{i\in V:x_i^*\le0\}\). Then \(S^-\) is the unique inclusionwise minimal minimizer of \(f\), and \(S^0\) is the unique inclusionwise maximal minimizer. Thus the signs of the minimum-norm base certify both extremal optimal sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly negative coordinates of the minimum-norm base give the smallest minimizer; nonpositive coordinates give the largest minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S^-=\min_{\subseteq}\operatorname*{argmin}f\) and \(S^0=\max_{\subseteq}\operatorname*{argmin}f\).

notation.meaning: Unique minimum-Euclidean-norm point of the base polyhedron.
Set of strictly negative coordinates of x*.
Set of nonpositive coordinates of x*.

review_flags: Fujishige's minimum-norm-base characterization requires an exact authoritative theorem locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strict-negative and nonpositive sign characterization is the standard minimum-norm-base result, and certificate fits this terminal container. The nontrivial extremal-minimizer characterization requires an exact authoritative theorem locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active-set algorithm for a minimum-norm point in a base polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative method operating on a simplex of extreme points of B(f).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize x^*\in\operatorname{ext}\mathrm{B}(f) and S=\{x^*\}. Use the greedy algorithm to find an x^*\text{-minimum-weight base }\widehat{x}. If \langle x^*,\widehat{x}-x^*\rangle=0, return x^*. Otherwise add \widehat{x} to S, find the minimum-norm point x_0\in\operatorname{aff}(S), and either set x^*=x_0 when x_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\operatorname{conv}S), or move along [x^*,x_0] to the relevant minimal face S' and replace S by S' before repeating.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from an extreme base and maintain an active simplex. A greedy minimum-weight base supplies the optimality test or a new active point. Project the origin onto the active affine hull; accept an interior projection or move to the appropriate boundary face and discard inactive points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \langle x^*,\widehat{x}-x^*\rangle=0\implies x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathrm{B}(f)}\|x\|_2

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Base-polyhedron path-exchange iteration for submodular minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General exact minimization procedure maintaining a short convex decomposition into greedy base vectors; this extract describes the iteration and its no-path optimality certificate but does not itself state a termination bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^S\to\mathbb R\) be submodular with \(f(\varnothing)=0\), and represent \(x\in B_f\) as \(x=\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i b^{\prec_i}\), where \(\lambda_i>0\) and \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\). Define \(A=\{(u,v):u\prec_i v\text{ for some }i\}\), \(P=\{v:x(v)>0\}\), and \(N=\{v:x(v)<0\}\). If \(D=(S,A)\) has no path from \(P\) to \(N\), let \(U\) be the vertices that can reach \(N\); then \[f(U)=x(U)\le x(W)\le f(W)\qquad(\forall W\subseteq S),\] so \(U\) minimizes \(f\). Otherwise, select \(s,t\) as prescribed from the distance labels, apply the order-pivot decomposition to one \(b^{\prec_i}\), move along \(\chi^t-\chi^s\) to the specified sign boundary, and compress the resulting convex representation to at most \(|S|\) terms before iterating.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain a base-polyhedron point as a convex combination of greedy base vectors. When the union of their order arcs contains no path from a positive coordinate to a negative one, the vertices that can reach a negative coordinate form a minimizing set. Otherwise perform the prescribed order-pivot exchange and reduce the new convex decomposition to at most |S| terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Ellipsoid Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact submodular minimization through the Lovász extension and ellipsoid separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a rational-valued submodular function \(f:2^V\to\mathbb Q\) through a value oracle and a known encoding bound. Normalize by subtracting \(f(\varnothing)\), form its Lovász extension \(\hat f\) on \([0,1]^V\), and use the greedy ordering at each query point to compute \(\hat f(z)\) and a subgradient. Apply the ellipsoid method to minimize \(\hat f\) over \([0,1]^V\), stopping once the encoding bound isolates the exact optimum. For an optimal \(z^*\), output a threshold set \(S_t=\{i:z_i^*\ge t\}\) attaining the least value among its coordinate thresholds. Then \(f(S_t)=\min_{S\subseteq V}f(S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize the Lovász extension over the unit cube by ellipsoid subgradient cuts, then return the best threshold set of an exact optimal point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is rational-valued and submodular on finite \(V\).
A value oracle and a polynomial encoding bound are available.
Exact rational arithmetic or equivalent bit-accurate separation is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{S\subseteq V}f(S)\).

notation.meaning: Lovász extension of the normalized submodular function.
An exact minimizer of the Lovász extension on the unit cube.

review_flags: The supplied network-flow locators do not support the Lovász-extension ellipsoid method.
An exact source is needed for the bit-complexity, stopping rule, and threshold-recovery formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct content kind, but the available sources do not support Lovasz-extension ellipsoid minimization. The encoding assumptions and exact stopping criterion are not quantified, and 'among its coordinate thresholds' does not explicitly include the boundary threshold sets needed in degenerate cases; an authoritative algorithm and bit-complexity source is required before the formulation can be fixed reliably.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation-Based Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional exact submodular minimization using strong separation over the base polyhedron and a lifted linear optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a normalized submodular function \(f\), the identity \(\min_{S\subseteq V}f(S)=\max_{x\in B(f)}\sum_{i\in V}\min\{x_i,0\}\) converts minimization into linear optimization over the lifted polyhedron \(Q=\{(x,z):x\in B(f),\ z_i\le x_i,\ z_i\le0\text{ for every }i\in V\}\). Given a strong separation oracle for \(B(f)\), separation for \(Q\) is immediate, so the ellipsoid method can maximize \(\sum_{i\in V}z_i\) exactly under the stated rational encoding bounds. If \(x^*\) is an optimal base, then \(S^- =\{i\in V:x_i^*<0\}\) is a minimizer of \(f\). This is a conditional separation-based method; it does not derive separation for \(B(f)\) from value-oracle access alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a strong separation oracle for the base polyhedron, a lifted linear program and the ellipsoid method recover an exact minimizing set; value-oracle access alone does not supply that separation oracle.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite and \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{Q}\) is normalized and submodular.
A strong separation oracle is available for \(B(f)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^V:x(A)\le f(A)\text{ for every }A\subseteq V,\ x(V)=f(V)\}\).
Polynomial rational encoding bounds are available for the oracle outputs and the relevant polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A set \(S^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{S\subseteq V}f(S)\) is recoverable using polynomially many strong-separation calls and bit operations.

notation.meaning: base polyhedron of the normalized submodular function

children.title: Ellipsoid–Separation Interface
children.top_down_role: Computational relationship between ellipsoid frameworks and separation oracles.

knowledge_statements.title: Ellipsoid–Separation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial oracle equivalence of strong separation and strong linear optimization for well-described rational polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty well-described rational polytope with known polynomial encoding and geometric size bounds. Given a strong separation oracle for \(P\), the ellipsoid method computes, for every \(c\in\mathbb{Q}^n\), a point \(x^*\in P\) satisfying \(c^\top x^*=\max\{c^\top x:x\in P\}\) using polynomially many oracle calls and bit operations. Conversely, a strong linear-optimization oracle for \(P\), together with the same description bounds, implements strong separation in polynomial time. Thus the two oracle problems are polynomial-time reducible to one another on this class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty well-described rational polytope, strong separation and exact linear optimization are polynomial-time equivalent through the ellipsoid framework.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty well-described rational polytope.
Polynomial bounds on the facet complexity, geometric size, and oracle-output encoding are known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong separation and strong linear optimization over \(P\) are polynomial-time oracle reducible to one another.

notation.meaning: an exact optimizer of the linear objective over the polytope

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The standard exact ellipsoid reduction for submodular minimization has running time polynomial in \(n\), the geometric encoding data, and \(L\). Consequently it is a polynomial-time algorithm in the bit model. It is not, merely from this analysis, strongly polynomial: the number or size of arithmetic operations may depend on \(L\). Any claimed strongly polynomial oracle bound must instead bound the number of value-oracle calls and arithmetic operations by a polynomial in \(n\), with intermediate encoding lengths polynomially controlled independently of the magnitudes of \(f(S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ellipsoid minimization is polynomial in input bit length, but its standard analysis does not by itself give a strongly polynomial value-oracle algorithm.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic exchange-graph framework; the precise Cunningham variant requires source disambiguation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize an extreme base \(x\in B(f)\) from an ordering of \(V\). Construct a directed exchange graph \(D_x\) whose arc \((i,j)\) represents a positive feasible transfer \(x\mapsto x+\alpha(\chi_i-\chi_j)\), with \(0<\alpha\) not exceeding the corresponding exchange capacity. Search \(D_x\) for an admissible path from a coordinate requiring decrease to one permitting increase, augment by the path bottleneck, and update the base decomposition and capacities. Repeat until no admissible improving path exists; the terminal reachability set supplies a minimizer of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method maintains a base, augments along feasible paths in its exchange graph, and extracts a minimizing set when no improving path remains.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaling-based Iwata–Fleischer–Fujishige variant with magnitude-dependent phase count.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an initial scale \(\Delta\) comparable to a positive power-of-two upper bound on \(M\). At each scale, maintain a feasible convex combination of extreme bases, form the residual exchange graph using arcs with capacity at least \(\Delta\), and perform admissible augmentations until the scale-level optimality conditions hold. Replace \(\Delta\) by \(\Delta/2\) and repeat until integrality makes the residual error zero. The number of scaling phases is \(O(\log M)\); with polynomial work per phase in \(n\), the resulting oracle bound is polynomial in \(n\) and \(\log M\), but depends on numerical magnitude.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weakly Polynomial IFF Scaling Algorithm for Submodular Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extracted exchange-and-flow delta-scaling procedure; correctness and complexity guarantees are not asserted by this algorithm block alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{Initialize }L,x,\delta,I,\varphi\text{ as prescribed. While }\delta\geq n^{-2},\text{ form }S=\{v\mid x(v)+\partial\varphi(v)\leq-\delta\},\ T=\{v\mid x(v)+\partial\varphi(v)\geq\delta\},\text{ and }W=\operatorname{Reach}_{G(\varphi)}(S).\text{ Apply Double-Exchange to active triples while applicable before reachability meets }T;\text{ when }W\cap T\neq\varnothing,\text{ augment }\varphi\text{ along a }\delta\text{-augmenting path and update }G(\varphi),S,T,W.\text{ Apply Reduce}(x,I),\text{ then set }\delta\leftarrow\delta/2\text{ and }\varphi\leftarrow\varphi/2.\text{ Return }W.

In each scaling phase, form the negative-excess set S, positive-excess set T, and the vertices W reachable from S in the residual graph. Perform double exchanges on active triples, augment the flow along a delta-augmenting path when W reaches T, update the residual structures, and apply the reduction operation. Halve delta and the flow after each phase, and return W when the scaling loop terminates.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a residual path, identify every extreme base in the convex representation of \(x\) that supports an exchange along an arc of that path. Repeat multiple exchanges until an arc saturates or a prescribed structural event occurs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strongly polynomial combinatorial submodular minimization via greedy bases and exchange operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize greedy extreme bases \(y^k\in B(f)\), weights \(\lambda_k\ge0\) with \(\sum_k\lambda_k=1\), and \(x=\sum_k\lambda_k y^k\). Repeatedly use exchange capacities, reachability, and updates of the underlying permutations to alter the decomposition while preserving \(x\in B(f)\). Each iteration either performs an improving augmentation or makes irreversible combinatorial progress in the maintained orders and reachability relation. When no improving augmentation exists, output the terminal reachable set \(S^*\); the base-polyhedron optimality conditions give \(f(S^*)=\min_{S\subseteq V}f(S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Schrijver's family maintains greedy bases and uses combinatorial exchanges and reachability until the terminal set satisfies the base-polyhedron optimality conditions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Schrijver Algorithm for Submodular Function Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extracted high-level initialization, graph construction, stopping test, and update loop; the referenced graph and update rules require the surrounding construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a linear ordering \(L_1\) and set \(I:=\{1\}\), \(\lambda_1:=1\). Repeatedly construct the graph \(G=(V,A)\) prescribed by the algorithm, form \(x=\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i y_i\), and set \(P:=\operatorname{supp}^+(x)\), \(N:=\operatorname{supp}^-(x)\). If no directed path from \(P\) to \(N\) exists, let \(W\) be the prescribed set of vertices reachable to \(N\) and stop; \(W\) is a minimizer of \(\rho\). Otherwise update \(\{(L_i,\lambda_i)\mid i\in I\}\) and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Schrijver's method maintains an ordering-based representation of a base, constructs an associated directed graph, and tests for a directed path from the positive support to the negative support. When no such path exists, it returns the prescribed set of vertices reachable to the negative support as a minimizer; otherwise it updates the representation and repeats.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Schrijver's combinatorial algorithm for submodular minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-based minimization of a normalized submodular function over all subsets of a finite ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given $U=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and an oracle for a submodular $f:2^U\to\mathbb R$ with $f(\varnothing)=0$, initialize $x=b^{\prec_1}$ for any total order and maintain $x$ as a convex combination of greedy vectors $b^{\prec_i}$. Form the digraph $D$ containing $(u,v)$ whenever $u\prec_i v$ for some maintained order, set $P=\{v:x(v)>0\}$ and $N=\{v:x(v)<0\}$, and let $X$ be the vertices not reachable from $P$. Stop when $N\subseteq X$. Otherwise select the prescribed reachable $t\in N$, predecessor $s$, and maximizing order $\prec_i$; choose $0\le\epsilon\le-x(t)$ so that $x'=x+\epsilon(\chi^t-\chi^s)$ has a convex representation by at most $n$ permitted greedy vectors, excluding $b^{\prec_i}$ when $x'(t)<0$, and repeat with $x'$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The algorithm maintains a base-polyhedron point as a convex combination of greedy vectors. It builds a precedence digraph from their orders, stops when every negative coordinate is unreachable from the positive coordinates, and otherwise transfers mass from a selected predecessor to a reachable negative vertex while recompressing the convex representation to at most n greedy vectors.
assumptions_latex: Values of $f$ are available through an oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The stopping set }X\subseteq U\text{ is the algorithm's candidate output for }\min_{Y\subseteq U}f(Y).

children.title: Orlin Strongly Polynomial Method
children.top_down_role: The strongly polynomial minimization framework associated with Orlin.

assumptions_latex: \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) is submodular and supplied by an exact evaluation oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A minimizer is computable in \(O(n^5\mathrm{EO}+n^6)\) time in the standard oracle-arithmetic accounting.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard value-oracle complexity attributed to Orlin's strongly polynomial algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Orlin's algorithm computes a set \(S^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{S\subseteq V}f(S)\) in \(O(n^5\mathrm{EO}+n^6)\) time. The algorithm combines strongly polynomial submodular-minimization primitives with contractions and a dimensional-reduction scheme: identified elements or blocks are fixed or contracted, and the remaining instance is solved recursively or by an exchange-based routine. The bound counts exact value-oracle evaluations at cost \(\mathrm{EO}\) and additional arithmetic operations separately, and neither count depends on the magnitudes or encoding lengths of the values \(f(S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orlin's exact value-oracle algorithm minimizes a submodular function in strongly polynomial time, with the standard bound O(n^5 EO + n^6).
knowledge_statements.title: Orlin Strongly Polynomial Method

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated O(n^5 EO+n^6) bound is commonly attributed to Orlin, but the record has no source or locator confirming the exact model and separation of oracle from arithmetic costs. Because the terminal names a method, the source should also establish whether the primary record should be an algorithm rather than a bare complexity bound.

children.title: Post-Orlin Refinements
children.top_down_role: Later strongly polynomial refinements, simplifications, and related frameworks.

assumptions_latex: \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) is submodular and accessed by an exact value oracle.
The refinement preserves exact minimization for unrestricted, possibly nonmonotone \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid refinement must retain magnitude-independent polynomial oracle complexity while improving a specified exponent, arithmetic term, or restricted-instance bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification criterion; the navigation label does not determine a unique post-Orlin result.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Call an algorithm a post-Orlin refinement only after specifying a bound \(T(n,\mathrm{EO})\) and a computational model in which it returns \(S^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{S\subseteq V}f(S)\). For an unrestricted strongly polynomial refinement, both the number of oracle calls and the number of arithmetic operations must be bounded by polynomials in \(n\) independent of \(\max_S|f(S)|\) and value encoding lengths. An improvement may reduce the exponent of \(n\), reduce non-oracle work, or apply to a stated restricted class; these claims are not interchangeable without their respective hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A post-Orlin refinement must state its model and exact bound, preserve exact minimization, and keep operation counts independent of function-value magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.title: Post-Orlin Refinements

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is only a criterion for labeling a future result, not a post-Orlin refinement. It states no algorithm, author, bound, restricted class, or concrete improvement and substantially duplicates the sibling mechanism and boundary containers.

children.title: Strong-Polynomiality Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Structural devices supporting strongly polynomial complexity.

assumptions_latex: An exact value-oracle model is used for \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\).
Every iteration is assigned a combinatorial progress event from a finite family polynomially bounded in \(n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If each event occurs only polynomially many times and each iteration has polynomial cost, then the algorithm is strongly polynomial.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient mechanism for strong polynomiality in exchange, contraction, and decomposition algorithms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an exact minimization algorithm performs at most \(N(n)\) iterations, where \(N\) is polynomial and does not depend on oracle-value magnitudes. Suppose further that each iteration uses polynomially many oracle calls and arithmetic operations, that intermediate numbers have polynomial encoding length, and that termination follows from irreversible combinatorial events such as arc saturation, contraction, deletion, rank reduction, or a bounded change of an ordering. Then the total oracle and arithmetic complexity is polynomial in \(n\) alone, so the algorithm is strongly polynomial in the oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong polynomiality follows when magnitude-independent combinatorial events bound the iterations and each iteration has polynomial oracle, arithmetic, and encoding cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Polynomiality Mechanisms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The general progress-event mechanism fits the container, but the record combines an arbitrary real exact oracle with bit-encoding requirements that are meaningful only after specifying a rational computation model. A source is needed to state the applicable strong-polynomiality criterion precisely.

children.title: Refinement Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Differences in access assumptions, complexity guarantees, and applicable regimes.

assumptions_latex: An algorithm exactly minimizes \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{Q}\) in the value-oracle model.
Its analysis invokes a numerical scale, tolerance, or bit-length parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without a magnitude-independent replacement for that parameter, the analysis proves at most weak polynomiality and cannot certify a strongly polynomial refinement.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between genuine strongly polynomial refinements and bit- or magnitude-dependent improvements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the iteration or operation bound contains \(L\), \(\log\max_S|f(S)|\), \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\), or another numerical magnitude parameter, then the bound is not strongly polynomial in \(n\), even when it improves an earlier bit-complexity estimate. Likewise, a faster result for symmetric, integer-valued, bounded-range, or otherwise restricted submodular functions does not automatically refine unrestricted minimization. To cross the strong-polynomiality boundary, the analysis must bound oracle calls and arithmetic operations by polynomials in \(n\) alone and control intermediate encoding lengths polynomially.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Magnitude-, precision-, or restriction-dependent speedups do not establish a strongly polynomial improvement for unrestricted exact submodular minimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Refinement Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between magnitude-dependent and strongly polynomial bounds is mathematically plausible and failure_boundary fits the leaf, but no cited source supports its application to post-Orlin submodular-minimization refinements or the listed restricted cases.

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a finite ground set and \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) is normalized and submodular.
The base polyhedron \(B(f)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^V:x(S)\le f(S)\text{ for all }S\subseteq V,\ x(V)=f(V)\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_-\) is the unique inclusion-minimal minimizer of \(f\), and \(A_0\) is the unique inclusion-maximal minimizer of \(f\).

notation.meaning: Unique Euclidean minimum-norm point of the base polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact minimum-norm-point characterization for normalized finite submodular functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute the unique point \(x^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in B(f)}\|x\|_2\). Define \(A_-=\{i\in V:x_i^*<0\}\) and \(A_0=\{i\in V:x_i^*\le0\}\). Then \(A_-\) and \(A_0\) both minimize \(f\) over \(2^V\). Moreover, every minimizer \(A\) satisfies \(A_-\subseteq A\subseteq A_0\); consequently, \(A_-\) is the unique inclusion-minimal minimizer and \(A_0\) is the unique inclusion-maximal minimizer. An exact minimum-norm-point computation therefore returns an exact minimizer through coordinate thresholding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact minimum-norm point of the base polyhedron identifies the smallest and largest minimizers through its negative and nonpositive coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Norm-Point Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimum-norm-point characterization is mathematically plausible and fits the method container, but the theorem and threshold conclusions have no cited source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Symmetric Submodular Minimization
children.top_down_role: Minimization restricted to symmetric submodular functions.

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite with \(|V|\ge2\), and \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) is submodular.
\(f\) is symmetric: \(f(S)=f(V\setminus S)\) for every \(S\subseteq V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The symmetric submodular minimization problem is \(\min\{f(S):\varnothing\ne S\subsetneq V\}\), with complementary sets having equal objective value.

notation.meaning: Complement of a set relative to the ground set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle formulation excluding the two trivial subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symmetric submodular minimization instance consists of a finite set \(V\) and a function \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(f(A)+f(B)\ge f(A\cap B)+f(A\cup B)\) and \(f(S)=f(V\setminus S)\) for all \(A,B,S\subseteq V\). Its feasible family is \(\mathcal{F}=2^V\setminus\{\varnothing,V\}\), and its value is \(\min_{S\in\mathcal{F}}f(S)\). Symmetry identifies each feasible solution with its complement, so either side of an optimal bipartition represents the same objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a symmetric submodular function over all nonempty proper subsets; either side of a bipartition has the same value.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Submodular Minimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the symmetric-minimization container and is internally precise, but no source supports the stated formulation and exclusion of the trivial subsets.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Legal order used in symmetric submodular minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy ordering primitive appearing in the recursive symmetric-minimization procedure; the definition and construction themselves require only value-oracle access to the set function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An ordering \((s_1,\ldots,s_n)\) of \(S\) is legal for \(f\) if, for each \(i=1,\ldots,n\), \(x=s_i\) minimizes \[f(\{s_1,\ldots,s_{i-1},x\})-f(\{x\})\] over \(x\in S\setminus\{s_1,\ldots,s_{i-1}\}\). Such an order can be found using \(O(|S|^2)\) calls to a value oracle for \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A legal order chooses each next element to minimize the stated expression relative to the current prefix. Greedy selection constructs one using quadratically many value-oracle calls.
assumptions_latex: f:2^S\to\mathbb R\text{ is accessible through a value oracle}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ a legal order of }S\text{ constructible using }O(|S|^2)\text{ value-oracle calls}
