intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selected algorithm role fits the leaf, but no citation supports this particular top-k random-greedy variant, its dummy-element convention, or the broader family claim.

children.title: Sampling-Based Families
children.top_down_role: Methods using sampled candidates or sampled objective information.

assumptions_latex: \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\) is monotone submodular, \(|V|=n\), and only a value oracle is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output uses at most \(k\lceil(n/k)\log(1/\varepsilon)\rceil\) marginal evaluations and is the standard stochastic-greedy sampling scheme.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform subsampling variant for monotone cardinality-constrained maximization in the value-oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(S_0=\varnothing\) and \(s=\min\{n,\lceil(n/k)\log(1/\varepsilon)\rceil\}\). For \(i=1,\ldots,k\), sample a subset \(R_i\subseteq V\setminus S_{i-1}\) uniformly without replacement with \(|R_i|=\min\{s,|V\setminus S_{i-1}|\}\). Select \(u_i\in\arg\max_{u\in R_i} f(u\mid S_{i-1})\), set \(S_i=S_{i-1}\cup\{u_i\}\), and return \(S_k\). Thus the method evaluates at most \(ks\le k\lceil(n/k)\log(1/\varepsilon)\rceil\) sampled marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic greedy samples about (n/k) log(1/epsilon) candidates per round and adds the sampled element with greatest marginal gain.
knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Based Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is plausible and locally appropriate, but the precise sample size, without-replacement convention, and oracle-count formulation have no inspectable source.

children.title: Sampling-Quality Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Interactions between sampling intensity, runtime, and solution quality.

assumptions_latex: \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\) is monotone submodular and accessed by a value oracle.
The constraint is \(|S|\le k\), with \(1\le k\le n=|V|\) and \(0<\varepsilon<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sampling \(s=\lceil(n/k)\log(1/\varepsilon)\rceil\) elements per round yields expected ratio at least \(1-1/e-\varepsilon\) using \(O(n\log(1/\varepsilon))\) oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard stochastic-greedy approximation versus value-oracle complexity tradeoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the stochastic-greedy scheme using \(s=\min\{n,\lceil(n/k)\log(1/\varepsilon)\rceil\}\) samples in each of \(k\) rounds, the expected objective value obeys \[\mathbb{E}[f(S_k)]\ge (1-1/e-\varepsilon)f(O).\] The total number of value-oracle evaluations is at most \(ks\), hence \(O(n\log(1/\varepsilon))\). Increasing \(s\) decreases the additive approximation loss while increasing oracle work linearly; the bound is independent of \(k\) after simplification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampling about (n/k) log(1/epsilon) elements per round achieves expected ratio 1-1/e-epsilon with O(n log(1/epsilon)) value queries.
knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Quality Tradeoffs

assumptions_latex: \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\) is monotone submodular with multilinear extension \(F\).
\(P\subseteq[0,1]^V\) is a down-closed solvable polytope and linear optimization over \(P\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trajectory remains in \(P\), and its endpoint satisfies \(F(x(1))\ge(1-1/e)\max_{y\in P}F(y)\) under exact continuous dynamics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact continuous-time form for monotone submodular maximization over a down-closed solvable polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x(0)=0\). For almost every \(t\in[0,1]\), choose \[v(t)\in\arg\max_{v\in P} v\cdot\nabla F(x(t))\] and evolve according to \(\dot{x}(t)=v(t)\). Output \(x(1)\), followed by an appropriate rounding method when an integral solution is required. Convexity of \(P\) gives \(x(t)=\int_0^t v(\tau)\,d\tau\in tP\subseteq P\), and the continuous-greedy guarantee is \[F(x(1))\ge(1-e^{-1})\mathrm{OPT}_F.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous greedy follows the feasible direction maximizing the multilinear gradient and attains a 1-1/e fractional approximation for monotone objectives.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Greedy Family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The continuous-greedy algorithm fits the node, but the exact dynamics and the stated guarantee over a general down-closed solvable polytope require authoritative support.

assumptions_latex: \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\) is submodular, not necessarily monotone, with multilinear extension \(F\).
\(P\subseteq[0,1]^V\) is down-closed and admits linear optimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update attenuates coordinate growth by residual capacity \(1-x(t)\), so \(0\le x(t)\le\mathbf{1}\) throughout the trajectory.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core measured dynamics; approximation constants depend on the monotonicity, horizon, and constraint variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x(0)=0\). At time \(t\), choose a direction \[v(t)\in\arg\max_{v\in P} v\cdot\bigl((\mathbf{1}-x(t))\odot\nabla F(x(t))\bigr)\] and evolve by \[\dot{x}(t)=v(t)\odot(\mathbf{1}-x(t)).\] Stop at the horizon prescribed by the approximation variant and output the endpoint for rounding. Equivalently, each coordinate grows at a rate scaled by its unused capacity, distinguishing measured continuous greedy from the unattenuated dynamics \(\dot{x}(t)=v(t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measured continuous greedy scales each chosen direction by the coordinatewise unused capacity, enabling multilinear optimization for nonmonotone submodular objectives.
knowledge_statements.title: Measured Continuous-Greedy Family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The measured dynamics are locally appropriate, but the horizon and approximation variant are deliberately unspecified, and no source establishes the precise direction-selection formulation.

assumptions_latex: \(M=(V,\mathcal I)\) is a matroid and \(x\) lies in its base polytope.
\(F\) is the multilinear extension of a submodular set function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The process terminates at an incidence vector \(\mathbf{1}_B\) of a base \(B\), with deterministic choices satisfying \(F(\mathbf{1}_B)\ge F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic pipage rounding on a matroid base polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: While \(x\) is fractional, choose distinct fractional coordinates \(i,j\) and the maximal interval \([\alpha_-,\alpha_+]\) containing \(0\) such that \(x+\alpha(e_i-e_j)\) remains in the base polytope. Submodularity makes \(g(\alpha)=F(x+\alpha(e_i-e_j))\) convex on this interval. Replace \(x\) by whichever endpoint \(x+\alpha_-(e_i-e_j)\) or \(x+\alpha_+(e_i-e_j)\) has larger \(F\)-value. Repeat until \(x=\mathbf{1}_B\) for a matroid base \(B\), and output \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pipage rounding shifts mass between two fractional coordinates to a feasible endpoint without decreasing the multilinear objective, eventually producing a matroid base.
knowledge_statements.title: Pipage-Rounding Family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but an arbitrary pair of fractional coordinates need not give a nondegenerate feasible pipage move. A source is needed to specify the valid pair-selection rule and support termination and nondecrease.

children.title: Swap-Rounding Families
children.top_down_role: Correlated rounding based on exchanges between fractional structures.

assumptions_latex: \(M=(V,\mathcal I)\) is a matroid, and \(x=\sum_{r=1}^m\lambda_r\mathbf{1}_{B_r}\) is a convex combination of base-incidence vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a random base \(B\) satisfying \(\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{1}_B]=x\) and \(\mathbb{E}[f(B)]\ge F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Swap rounding from an explicit convex decomposition in a matroid base polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Repeatedly merge two weighted bases. If current bases \(B_1,B_2\) differ, choose \(i\in B_1\setminus B_2\) and \(j\in B_2\setminus B_1\) such that both \(B_1-i+j\) and \(B_2-j+i\) are bases. Perform one of these exchanges with probabilities chosen to preserve the weighted average of their incidence vectors. Continue until the two bases coincide, replace them by that base with their combined weight, and repeat until one random base \(B\) remains. Then \(\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{1}_B]=x\) and \(\mathbb{E}[f(B)]\ge F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Swap rounding merges bases through randomized symmetric exchanges, preserving marginals and retaining at least the multilinear value in expectation.
knowledge_statements.title: Swap-Rounding Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The swap-rounding algorithm matches the leaf, but the exchange probabilities and the guarantees preserving marginals and multilinear value require an exact cited theorem.

children.title: Dependent-Rounding Families
children.top_down_role: Rounding schemes that preserve selected marginal or feasibility dependencies.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in[0,1]^V\) satisfies the linear constraints preserved by the selected dependent-rounding scheme.
Each update acts on at least two fractional coordinates and preserves their designated linear sum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The terminal vector \(X\in\{0,1\}^V\) preserves the prescribed constraints and satisfies \(\mathbb{E}[X_i]=x_i\) for every \(i\in V\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic pairwise dependent-rounding template; feasibility details depend on the underlying constraint system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(Y=x\). While at least two coordinates \(Y_i,Y_j\) are fractional, determine the maximal positive step lengths \(a,b\) for which both candidates \(Y+a(e_i-e_j)\) and \(Y-b(e_i-e_j)\) remain feasible in \([0,1]^V\) and preserve the required linear constraints. Replace \(Y\) by the first candidate with probability \(b/(a+b)\) and by the second with probability \(a/(a+b)\). Resolve any final coordinate according to the scheme's feasibility rule and output \(X=Y\). The conditional expectation of every update equals its input.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori upper-bound certificate from the largest available greedy marginal under a cardinality constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(i\), define \(\Delta_i=\max_{u\in V\setminus S_{i-1}} f(u\mid S_{i-1})\) and \(U_i=f(S_{i-1})+k\Delta_i\). knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Model Hardness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-theoretic hardness under value-oracle access.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\varepsilon>0\). In the value-oracle model, there are families of nonnegative monotone submodular functions on \(n\) elements with a cardinality constraint \(|S|\le k\) such that any randomized algorithm guaranteeing \[\mathbb E[f(S)]>(1-1/e+\varepsilon)\max_{|T|\le k}f(T)\] on every instance must make exponentially many oracle queries in \(n\). This obstruction is information-theoretic and does not assume that the function has a polynomial-size explicit encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Beating 1−1/e for monotone cardinality-constrained maximization requires exponentially many value queries, independently of computational complexity assumptions.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm learns \(f\) only through value queries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A \((1-1/e+\varepsilon)\)-approximation has exponential worst-case value-query complexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit-Representation Hardness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: NP-hardness frontier inherited from explicitly represented maximum coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maximum coverage is an explicitly represented special case of monotone submodular maximization: given sets \(A_1,\ldots,A_n\) and budget \(k\), define \(f(S)=|\bigcup_{i\in S}A_i|\). Unless \(P=NP\), for every constant \(\varepsilon>0\) no polynomial-time algorithm can always return \(|S|\le k\) with \[f(S)>(1-1/e+\varepsilon)\max_{|T|\le k}f(T).\] Hence the \(1-1/e\) barrier persists even when the objective is supplied by a polynomial-size incidence representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit maximum coverage is submodular and NP-hard to approximate beyond 1−1/e, so explicit access does not remove the frontier.
assumptions_latex: The set-system incidence relation is given explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No polynomial-time \((1-1/e+\varepsilon)\)-approximation exists for this explicitly represented subclass.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation-Sensitive Separations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes information-theoretic oracle barriers from encoding-dependent computational hardness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An approximation lower bound must specify how \(f\) is represented. A value-oracle lower bound states that many evaluations are necessary even with unlimited computation between queries; an explicit-representation lower bound states that polynomial-time computation is impossible under a complexity assumption. Neither statement implies the other without a reduction preserving feasibility, objective values, approximation ratio, and polynomial instance size. In particular, a succinct formula may expose structure hidden by an oracle, whereas a general explicit encoding may itself make evaluation or optimization computationally hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle-query hardness and explicit-input NP-hardness are different claims; transferring either requires a representation-preserving reduction.
assumptions_latex: The oracle and explicit models encode the same optimization objective only when an explicit reduction establishes this correspondence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Hardness frontiers from distinct representation models cannot be identified solely because both concern submodular maximization.

notation.meaning: Set-function objective whose access model is being specified.

children.title: Lazy Greedy Implementations
children.top_down_role: Priority-based implementations that avoid unnecessary marginal evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Lazy Greedy Implementations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact priority-queue implementation of cardinality greedy using diminishing returns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given monotone submodular \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) and budget \(k\), initialize \(S=\varnothing\) and store for each \(e\in V\) an upper bound \(u_e=f(\{e\})-f(\varnothing)\) in a max-priority queue. Repeatedly extract an element \(e\) of largest key, recompute \(\Delta(e\mid S)=f(S\cup\{e\})-f(S)\), and reinsert it unless its recomputed value is at least every remaining key. In the latter case add \(e\) to \(S\). Stop when \(|S|=k\) or no positive marginal remains. The output equals a valid execution of ordinary greedy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lazy greedy caches marginal upper bounds and reevaluates only competitive elements while producing the same choices as ordinary greedy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned set is an ordinary greedy solution, although the number of value evaluations is instance-dependent.

notation.meaning: Marginal gain of adding e to S.

children.title: Stochastic Greedy Implementations

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Greedy Implementations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random-sampling implementation for monotone cardinality-constrained maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a finite ground set with \(n=|V|\), let \(1\le k\le n\) be an integer, and let \(0<\varepsilon<1\). Given a normalized, monotone, submodular function \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\), initialize \(S=\varnothing\). At each of \(k\) iterations, sample uniformly without replacement a subset \(R\subseteq V\setminus S\) of size \(s=\min\{|V\setminus S|,\lceil(n/k)\log(1/\varepsilon)\rceil\}\), evaluate \(\Delta(e\mid S)=f(S\cup\{e\})-f(S)\) for every \(e\in R\), and add an element of maximum sampled marginal gain. The output satisfies \[\mathbb E[f(S)]\ge(1-1/e-\varepsilon)\max_{T\subseteq V,\,|T|\le k}f(T).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic greedy samples about (n/k) log(1/ε) candidates per round and achieves an expected approximation factor of 1−1/e−ε.
assumptions_latex: \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) is normalized, monotone, and submodular.
\(0<\varepsilon<1\), and sampling is uniform without replacement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm performs at most \(n\log(1/\varepsilon)+k\) sampled marginal evaluations and satisfies \(\mathbb E[f(S)]\ge(1-1/e-\varepsilon)\mathrm{OPT}\).

notation.meaning: Random candidate sample in one iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: Evaluation-Savings Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluation complexity comparison for exact lazy and sampled greedy implementations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For cardinality budget \(k\) on a ground set of size \(n\), ordinary greedy may perform \(\Theta(nk)\) marginal evaluations. Stochastic greedy with accuracy parameter \(\varepsilon\) performs at most \(O(n\log(1/\varepsilon))\) sampled marginal evaluations and achieves expected ratio \(1-1/e-\varepsilon\). Lazy greedy preserves the ordinary-greedy solution and often saves evaluations, but submodularity alone gives no uniform improvement over its \(O(nk)\) worst-case evaluation bound. Thus stochastic savings are worst-case quantitative, whereas lazy savings are data-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic greedy has a provable near-linear evaluation bound; lazy greedy is exact but its evaluation savings are instance-dependent.
assumptions_latex: The objective is monotone and submodular.
Each marginal evaluation has unit oracle cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stochastic greedy uses \(O(n\log(1/\varepsilon))\) evaluations, while lazy greedy retains an \(O(nk)\) worst case.

knowledge_statements.title: Streaming Maximization Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Streaming model for submodular maximization under bounded retained state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A \(p\)-pass streaming maximization method receives elements of a finite ground set \(V\) in a fixed sequence and scans that sequence at most \(p\) times. After each arrival it may query objective values involving the arriving element and its retained state, then update a state occupying at most \(M\) machine words. It cannot randomly access discarded elements. After the final pass it outputs a feasible set \(S\) contained in its retained state. Its guarantees are measured by approximation ratio, number of passes, memory \(M\), and oracle evaluations.

assumptions_latex: Discarded elements cannot later be accessed except during another permitted pass.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Pass Maximization Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sieve-style single-pass algorithm for monotone cardinality-constrained maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) be normalized, monotone, and submodular, with budget \(k\). Maintain parallel candidate sets for a geometric collection of guesses \(v\) for \(\mathrm{OPT}\). Upon arrival of \(e\), add \(e\) to candidate \(S_v\) when \(|S_v|<k\) and \[\Delta(e\mid S_v)\ge\frac{v/2-f(S_v)}{k-|S_v|}.\] Discard obsolete guesses as the largest singleton value grows, and output the candidate of greatest value. With suitable \((1+	heta)\)-spaced guesses, the method makes one pass, uses \(O(k\log k/\theta)\) stored elements, and achieves factor \(1/2-O(\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sieve-style thresholding obtains an approximately 1/2 solution in one pass using memory near linear in the cardinality budget.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is normalized, nonnegative, monotone, and submodular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One pass suffices for a \((1/2-O(\theta))\)-approximation using \(O(k\log k/\theta)\) stored elements.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Pass Streaming Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated threshold scans trading additional passes for finer greedy selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given normalized monotone submodular \(f\), budget \(k\), and thresholds \(\tau_1>\cdots>\tau_p\ge0\), initialize \(S=\varnothing\). During pass \(j\), scan the stream and accept an arriving element \(e\notin S\) whenever \(|S|<k\) and \(\Delta(e\mid S)\ge\tau_j\). Retain accepted elements between passes and output \(S\) after pass \(p\). Choosing thresholds from valid upper and lower bounds on \(\mathrm{OPT}\) produces multi-pass threshold-greedy variants; their approximation and memory bounds depend on the threshold schedule and stream-order model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multi-pass threshold greedy rescans discarded elements at decreasing thresholds, allowing later acceptance as the selection criterion is refined.
assumptions_latex: The stream can be replayed in the same order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure uses \(p\) passes, retains at most \(k\) selected elements, and returns a feasible set.

notation.meaning: Acceptance threshold used in pass j.

children.title: Memory-Pass Tradeoffs

knowledge_statements.title: Memory-Pass Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model boundary for claims relating streaming memory, passes, and approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a streaming algorithm use \(p\) passes and at most \(M\) words of retained state. These two parameters alone do not determine an approximation ratio: the attainable ratio also depends on the constraint family, monotonicity, stream order, randomization, oracle access, and whether output elements count toward memory. Any claimed memory-pass frontier must therefore fix those conventions and state a bound of the form \(M\ge L(n,k,p,\alpha)\) or provide an algorithm with \(M\le U(n,k,p,\alpha)\) for approximation factor \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: There is no representation-free memory-pass frontier; meaningful tradeoffs must fix the streaming, oracle, feasibility, and approximation models.
assumptions_latex: Memory is measured in machine words.
The algorithm makes at most \(p\) complete stream passes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A memory-pass claim is incomplete unless it quantifies \(M\), \(p\), and \(\alpha\) under a fully specified streaming model.

notation.meaning: Batch of value-oracle queries issued in parallel during round r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-oracle parallelism for monotone cardinality-constrained maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A parallel maximization method proceeds in rounds \(r=1,\ldots,R\). In round \(r\), it constructs a query batch \(Q_r\subseteq 2^V\) using only its internal randomness and answers from \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_{r-1}\), and all values \(\{f(T):T\in Q_r\}\) are returned simultaneously. After round \(R\), it outputs \(S\in\mathcal F\). Its adaptivity is \(R\), its query complexity is \(q=\sum_{r=1}^{R}|Q_r|\), and it is an \(\alpha\)-approximation if \(\mathbb E[f(S)]\ge\alpha\max_{T\in\mathcal F}f(T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel methods batch independent value queries into sequential rounds; adaptivity counts rounds, while approximation compares expected output value with the feasible optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Maximization Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The parallel value-oracle model and its definition-level content kind are mathematically coherent, but no inspectable citation supports the model or terminology.

children.title: Distributed Maximization Methods
children.top_down_role: Methods partitioning data or computation across multiple workers.

assumptions_latex: \(V=V_1\dot\cup\cdots\dot\cup V_m\) is a partition held by \(m\) machines.
\(f:2^V\to\mathbb R_+\) is normalized, monotone, and submodular, with feasibility \(|S|\le k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The protocol is an \(\alpha\)-approximation when \(\mathbb E[f(S)]\ge\alpha\max_{|T|\le k}f(T)\), with communication measured by the transmitted summaries and synchronization rounds.

notation.meaning: Data block stored on machine i
Summary sent by machine i in communication round t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous distributed value-oracle model with partitioned ground data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize each machine with \(V_i\) and no information about other blocks. In communication round \(t\), machine \(i\) computes a summary \(C_i^{(t)}\) from \(V_i\), shared randomness, and previously received messages. A coordinator aggregates the summaries, may broadcast a new state, and after \(T\) rounds returns \(S\subseteq V\) with \(|S|\le k\). Communication is \(\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{m}|C_i^{(t)}|\) under a specified encoding. The protocol has factor \(\alpha\) if \(\mathbb E[f(S)]\ge\alpha\max_{|T'|\le k}f(T')\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Machines summarize disjoint data blocks, exchange summaries through a coordinator, and jointly return a feasible set with a stated expected approximation guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Maximization Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract distributed protocol is consistent with the leaf, but it has no source establishing this particular partition, coordinator, communication, and approximation model.

children.title: Low-Adaptivity Maximization Methods
children.top_down_role: Methods limiting sequential dependence among oracle-query rounds.

assumptions_latex: A value-oracle algorithm accesses \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) only through queried set values.
Queries within one batch may be issued simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The adaptivity is the smallest \(R\) admitting such a batch decomposition; low adaptivity means \(R\) is polylogarithmic or otherwise asymptotically smaller than the query count.

notation.meaning: Queries issued in adaptive round r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive-round complexity in the value-oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An oracle algorithm has adaptivity at most \(R\) if its queries can be partitioned into batches \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_R\) such that every query in \(Q_r\) is determined by the algorithm's randomness and the oracle answers to \(Q_1\cup\cdots\cup Q_{r-1}\), but not by answers to other queries in \(Q_r\). Its total query complexity is \(q=\sum_{r=1}^{R}|Q_r|\). A low-adaptivity maximization method simultaneously specifies a feasible output rule and an approximation guarantee while making \(R\) asymptotically smaller than \(q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptivity counts sequential oracle batches, allowing unlimited parallel queries inside each batch; low-adaptivity methods retain approximation quality with few sequential batches.
knowledge_statements.title: Low-Adaptivity Maximization Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The adaptive-batch definition is precise and appropriate, but the record supplies no authoritative source or locator for the adopted definition of low adaptivity.

children.title: Round-Communication Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Interactions among adaptive rounds, synchronization, and communication cost.

assumptions_latex: Round \(r\) contains \(q_r\) oracle queries executed on at most \(p\) processors.
Communication volume \(C_r\) is measured in a fixed common encoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The query-batch time is \(T_p=\sum_{r=1}^{R}\lceil q_r/p\rceil\), hence \(T_p\ge\max\{R,\lceil q/p\rceil\}\), while total communication is \(C=\sum_{r=1}^{R}C_r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource accounting, not an approximation lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose adaptive round \(r\) issues \(q_r\ge1\) unit-time oracle queries and uses at most \(p\) processors. Its query-batch time is at least \(\lceil q_r/p\rceil\), and the ideal balanced schedule attains this value. Therefore \(T_p=\sum_{r=1}^{R}\lceil q_r/p\rceil\) and, for \(q=\sum_{r=1}^{R}q_r\), \(T_p\ge\max\{R,\lceil q/p\rceil\}\). If round \(r\) communicates \(C_r\) encoded units, total communication is \(C=\sum_{r=1}^{R}C_r\); reducing \(R\) need not reduce \(C\) or \(q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With bounded processors, elapsed query time depends on both adaptive rounds and batch sizes; fewer rounds need not mean fewer queries or less communication.
knowledge_statements.title: Round-Communication Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound is correct for the explicitly idealized unit-time, zero-overhead batch schedule, but no source supports this cost model or its placement as a round-communication tradeoff.

children.title: Robust Maximization
children.top_down_role: Maximization against structured perturbations or adverse scenarios.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Maximization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-ground-set max-inf robust submodular maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite set \(V\), a nonempty feasible family \(\mathcal F\subseteq 2^V\), a nonempty scenario set \(\Theta\), and objectives \(f_\theta:2^V\to\mathbb R\), define \(F_{\rm rob}(S)=\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}f_\theta(S)\). The robust maximization problem is \(\max_{S\in\mathcal F}F_{\rm rob}(S)\), and a robust optimizer is any \(S^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{S\in\mathcal F}\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}f_\theta(S)\). If \(\Theta\) is finite, the infimum over scenarios is a minimum. Even when every \(f_\theta\) is submodular, \(F_{\rm rob}\) need not be submodular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust maximization selects a feasible set maximizing its worst-case scenario value, expressed as an infimum unless scenario attainment is guaranteed; the resulting worst-case objective need not be submodular.
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\ne\varnothing\), and \(f_\theta:2^V\to\mathbb R\) is submodular for every \(\theta\in\Theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A robust optimizer is any \(S^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{S\in\mathcal F}\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}f_\theta(S)\), with robust value \(\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}f_\theta(S^\star)\); when \(\Theta\) is finite, each infimum may be written as a minimum.

children.title: Noisy Maximization
children.top_down_role: Maximization with corrupted or stochastic objective evaluations.

assumptions_latex: Each oracle call may use fresh randomness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle is unbiased when \(\mathbb E[Z(S)\mid S]=f(S)\); it is \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian when \(\mathbb E[e^{\lambda(Z(S)-f(S))}\mid S]\le e^{\lambda^2\sigma^2/2}\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\).

notation.meaning: Random response to a query at S

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbiased sub-Gaussian value-oracle noise model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A noisy value oracle queried at \(S\subseteq V\) returns a random variable \(Z(S)\) rather than \(f(S)\). It is unbiased if \(\mathbb E[Z(S)\mid S]=f(S)\). It has conditionally \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian noise if, for every \(S\subseteq V\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), \(\mathbb E[\exp(\lambda(Z(S)-f(S)))\mid S]\le\exp(\lambda^2\sigma^2/2)\). An algorithm must state whether repeated responses are conditionally independent and whether its approximation guarantee holds in expectation or with specified probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A noisy oracle returns random estimates of set values; unbiasedness, tail behavior, independence, and the probability form of guarantees must be specified.
knowledge_statements.title: Noisy Maximization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unbiased conditionally sub-Gaussian oracle definition is internally consistent and fits the leaf, but no source or locator supports the selected noise model.

children.title: Adversarial-Uncertainty Regimes
children.top_down_role: Robustness settings governed by worst-case uncertainty.

assumptions_latex: Oracle answers may incur adversarial additive error at most \(\eta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(0<\delta\le2\eta\), identical admissible answers can represent objectives with opposite unique optima, so no deterministic one-query-per-set rule always identifies the optimum.

notation.meaning: Gap between the best and second-best singleton

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-element indistinguishability under bounded additive adversarial noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<\delta\le2\eta\). Define modular objectives by \(f_1(\{a\})=1\), \(f_1(\{b\})=1-\delta\), and \(f_2(\{a\})=1-\delta\), \(f_2(\{b\})=1\), with value zero at the empty set and additive extension. The response \(y(\{a\})=y(\{b\})=1-\delta/2\) differs from each true singleton value by at most \(\eta\) under both objectives. Thus the transcript is identical although the unique optimal singleton is \(\{a\}\) for \(f_1\) and \(\{b\}\) for \(f_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When adversarial error reaches half the optimality gap, even two modular objectives with opposite optima can produce exactly the same observations.
knowledge_statements.title: Adversarial-Uncertainty Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-objective indistinguishability construction is mathematically sound and correctly classified as a failure boundary, but it has no cited lower-bound source.

children.title: Statistical-Uncertainty Regimes
children.top_down_role: Noise settings governed by probabilistic observation models.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\subseteq2^V\) is finite and \(f(S,\xi)\in[0,1]\) for all \(S\in\mathcal F\).
Samples \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\) are independent and identically distributed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(N\ge(2\varepsilon^2)^{-1}\log(2|\mathcal F|/\delta)\), then \(\Pr\{\sup_{S\in\mathcal F}|\widehat F_N(S)-F(S)|\le\varepsilon\}\ge1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-class uniform convergence for bounded stochastic objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(F(S)=\mathbb E[f(S,\xi)]\) and \(\widehat F_N(S)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{N}f(S,\xi_i)\). For \(0<\varepsilon<1\) and \(0<\delta<1\), if \(N\ge(2\varepsilon^2)^{-1}\log(2|\mathcal F|/\delta)\), then with probability at least \(1-\delta\), \(\sup_{S\in\mathcal F}|\widehat F_N(S)-F(S)|\le\varepsilon\). Consequently, any exact maximizer \(\widehat S\) of \(\widehat F_N\) satisfies \(F(\widehat S)\ge\max_{S\in\mathcal F}F(S)-2\varepsilon\) on the same event.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enough independent bounded samples uniformly approximate every feasible set's expectation, and an empirical maximizer is within twice the uniform error of optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Statistical-Uncertainty Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Hoeffding-union-bound sample threshold and the resulting two-epsilon empirical-optimization guarantee are correct for a finite feasible class, but no source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Total Dual Integrality of Two-Polymatroid Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: TDI property for the common nonnegative region bounded by two submodular functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let E be finite and let f,g:2^E\to\mathbb{R}_+ be submodular. The system
\[
x_e\ge0\quad(e\in E),\qquad \sum_{e\in A}x_e\le f(A)\quad(A\subseteq E),\qquad \sum_{e\in A}x_e\le g(A)\quad(A\subseteq E)
\]
is totally dual integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any two nonnegative submodular functions on a finite ground set, the nonnegativity constraints together with both families of subset-sum upper bounds form a totally dual integral system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x\ge0:\ x(A)\le f(A),\ x(A)\le g(A)\ \forall A\subseteq E\}\text{ has a TDI defining system}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polymatroid Function, Polymatroid, and Polymatroidal Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Foundational polymatroid definitions, with integrality assumed unless explicitly stated otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function $b:2^S\to\mathbb Z$ is a polymatroid function if $b(\varnothing)=0$, $b$ is nondecreasing, and $b$ is submodular. Its polymatroid is $P(b):=\{x\in\mathbb R^S:x\ge0,\ x(X)\le b(X)\ \forall X\subseteq S\}$. A polymatroidal set is the set $P(b)\cap\mathbb Z^S$ for an integral polymatroid. If $b$ is a matroid rank function, then $P(b)$ is the matroid independence polyhedron and its integral points are exactly the incidence vectors of independent sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integer-valued, normalized, nondecreasing submodular set function defines a polymatroid through nonnegativity and all subset upper bounds. The integral points of an integral polymatroid form its polymatroidal set. Matroid independence polyhedra arise as the rank-function special case.
assumptions_latex: b(X)+b(Y)\ge b(X\cap Y)+b(X\cup Y)\quad\forall X,Y\subseteq S
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P(b)=\{x\in\mathbb R^S:x\ge0,\ x(X)\le b(X)\ \forall X\subseteq S\},\quad\text{with polymatroidal set }P(b)\cap\mathbb Z^S.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polymatroid and extended polymatroid associated with a set function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines both inequality systems, states their exact nonemptiness conditions, and records boundedness of the ordinary polymatroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be finite and let \(f:\mathcal P(S)\to\mathbb R\). Define \[P_f:=\{x\in\mathbb R^S:x\ge0,\ x(U)\le f(U)\text{ for every }U\subseteq S\},\] \[EP_f:=\{x\in\mathbb R^S:x(U)\le f(U)\text{ for every }U\subseteq S\}.\] Then \(P_f\ne\varnothing\) if and only if \(f(U)\ge0\) for every \(U\subseteq S\), and \(EP_f\ne\varnothing\) if and only if \(f(\varnothing)\ge0\). If \(f\) is submodular, \(P_f\) and \(EP_f\) are called its polymatroid and extended polymatroid, respectively. Moreover, \(P_f\) is bounded because \(0\le x_s\le f(\{s\})\) for every \(s\in S\), and hence is a polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ordinary polymatroid adds nonnegative-coordinate constraints to the subset-sum inequalities, while the extended polymatroid does not. Their nonemptiness conditions are, respectively, nonnegativity of the set function on every subset and nonnegativity at the empty set. When generated by a submodular function, the ordinary polymatroid is bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_f\ne\varnothing\iff \forall U\subseteq S,\ f(U)\ge0,\qquad EP_f\ne\varnothing\iff f(\varnothing)\ge0;\qquad f\text{ submodular}\implies P_f\text{ is a bounded polymatroid polytope and }EP_f\text{ is an extended polymatroid}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear 2-Polymatroid Matching Minimax Formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimax characterization of the matching number of a linear 2-polymatroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $(S,f)$ be a linear 2-polymatroid. Then
\[
\nu(S,f)=\min_{g,\,\{S_1,\ldots,S_k\}}\left(f(S)-g(S)+\sum_{i=1}^{k}\left\lfloor\frac{g(S_i)}{2}\right\rfloor\right),
\]
where the minimum ranges over all linear projections $(S,g)$ of $(S,f)$ and all partitions $\{S_1,\ldots,S_k\}$ of $S$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a linear 2-polymatroid, the matching number equals the minimum of the stated projection-and-partition expression over all linear projections and all partitions of the ground set.

Let E be finite and let ho:2^E	o\mathbf R satisfy ho(\varnothing)=0, monotonicity, and submodularity. The polymatroid (E,ho) has independence polyhedron P_+(ho)=\{x\in\mathbf R^E:x\geq0,\ x(X)\leqho(X)\  orall X\subseteq E\} and base polyhedron B(ho)=\{x\in P_+(ho):x(E)=ho(E)\}. For e\in\operatorname{sat}(x), their minimal member containing e is \operatorname{dep}(x,e), while \operatorname{dep}(x,e)=\varnothing for e

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Downward Closure of an Extended-Polymatroid Optimal Face
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combines the structural representation with its value-oracle evaluation guarantee.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility criterion for simultaneous box and plank intersection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes nonemptiness using four subset inequalities, including the cases of unbounded plank endpoints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Chain-Marginal Domination Proposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A subset-inequality certificate used to establish feasibility of chain-marginal greedy vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let E=\{e_1,\ldots,e_n\}, let f:2^E\to\mathbb{R} be submodular with f(\varnothing)\geq0, and let b:E\to\mathbb{R}. If
\[
b(e_1)\leq f(\{e_1\}),\qquad b(e_i)\leq f(\{e_1,\ldots,e_i\})-f(\{e_1,\ldots,e_{i-1}\})\quad(2\leq i\leq n),
\]

\[
\sum_{a\in A}b(a)\leq f(A)\qquad\text{for every }A\subseteq E.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If each value b(e_i) is bounded by the corresponding marginal increment of a submodular function along a fixed ordering, then b(A) is at most f(A) for every subset A.

knowledge_statements.title: Polymatroid Greedy Principle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Edmonds greedy theorem for nonnegative linear objectives over a polymatroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a permutation \(\pi\) of \(V\) satisfying \(w_{\pi(1)}\ge\cdots\ge w_{\pi(n)}\), set \(S_0=\varnothing\), and let \(S_i=\{\pi(1),\ldots,\pi(i)\}\). Define \(x_{\pi(i)}=r(S_i)-r(S_{i-1})\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\). Then \(x\in P(r)\) and \(w^\top x=\max\{w^\top y:y\in P(r)\}\). Equal-weight elements may be ordered arbitrarily; each compatible ordering yields an optimal greedy vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sort nonnegative weights downward and assign successive rank increments; the resulting feasible polymatroid vector maximizes the linear objective.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite, and \(r:2^V\to\mathbb R_+\) is normalized, monotone, and submodular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The greedy vector \(x_{\pi(i)}=r(S_i)-r(S_{i-1})\) belongs to \(P(r)\) and maximizes \(w^\top x\) over \(P(r)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinate-ordered greedy rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the sequential coordinate maximization rule and when it works for a nonnegative rational objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n and c\in\mathbb{Q}_+^n. For any coordinate ordering satisfying c_1\ge\cdots\ge c_n, recursively set
\[
x_i^*:=\max\{x_i:x\in X,\ x_j=x_j^*\text{ for every }j<i\},\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.
\]
The greedy algorithm works for c if, for every such ordering, all maxima exist and the resulting x^* belongs to X and satisfies
\[
c^Tx^*=\max_{x\in X}c^Tx.
\]

The rule works for the objective if every compatible ordering produces existing maxima and an optimal feasible point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polymatroid Greedy Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear optimization over an integral polymatroid; negative objective coefficients may first be removed and assigned zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $b:2^S\to\mathbb Z$ be a polymatroid function and let $c\in\mathbb R^S$. Components with $c(s)<0$ may be deleted, since some optimum has value zero in those coordinates. Order the remaining elements so that $c(s_1)\ge\cdots\ge c(s_n)\ge0$, set $S_i=\{s_1,\ldots,s_i\}$, and define $x_{\mathrm{alg}}(s_1)=b(\{s_1\})$ and $x_{\mathrm{alg}}(s_i)=b(S_i)-b(S_{i-1})$ for $i\ge2$. Then $\widetilde x_{\mathrm{alg}}(S_i)=b(S_i)$ for every $i$, and $x_{\mathrm{alg}}$ is integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After discarding negative-weight coordinates, sort the elements by nonincreasing weight and assign each coordinate the corresponding marginal increase of the polymatroid function. Every prefix constraint is tight, and an integer-valued polymatroid function yields an integral vector.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{\mathrm{alg}}(s_i)=b(S_i)-b(S_{i-1}),\quad \widetilde x_{\mathrm{alg}}(S_i)=b(S_i)\ \forall i,\quad x_{\mathrm{alg}}\in\mathbb Z^S

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Correctness and Integrality of the Polymatroid Greedy Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality of the chain-marginal greedy construction, with integrality when the set function is integer-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let E be finite, let f:2^E\to\mathbb{R}_+ be monotone and submodular with f(\varnothing)\geq0, and let c\in\mathbb{R}^E. Let x be produced by the polymatroid greedy algorithm: order the elements by nonincreasing c-value, assign successive f-marginals to the elements having positive coefficients, and set the remaining coordinates to zero. Then
\[
x\in P(f),\qquad c^\top x=\max\{c^\top y:y\in P(f)\}.
\]
If f(A)\in\mathbb{Z} for every A\subseteq E, then x\in\mathbb{Z}^E.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polymatroid greedy algorithm returns a feasible maximizer of the given linear objective. If the submodular function is integer-valued, its returned vector is integral.
assumptions_latex: x\text{ is produced by the polymatroid greedy algorithm}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{y\in P(f)}c^\top y,\qquad \bigl(f(A)\in\mathbb{Z}\ \forall A\subseteq E\bigr)\Rightarrow x\in\mathbb{Z}^E

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polymatroid Greedy Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy maximization of an arbitrary linear objective over a polymatroid given by a value oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given finite E, a monotone submodular f:2^E\to\mathbb{R}_+ with f(\varnothing)\ge0, and c\in\mathbb{R}^E, order E=\{e_1,\ldots,e_n\} so that c(e_1)\ge\cdots\ge c(e_k)>0\ge c(e_{k+1})\ge\cdots\ge c(e_n). Set
\[
x_{e_1}=f(\{e_1\}),\qquad x_{e_i}=f(\{e_1,\ldots,e_i\})-f(\{e_1,\ldots,e_{i-1}\})\ (2\le i\le k),
\]
and x_{e_i}=0 for i>k; if k=0, set x=0. The intended output is an x\in P(f) maximizing c^\top x.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sort elements by decreasing objective coefficient, assign successive submodular marginal increments to the positively weighted elements, and assign zero to all remaining elements. If no coefficient is positive, return the zero vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in P(f)\quad\text{and the algorithm seeks }\max\{c^\top y:y\in P(f)\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Exchange Characterization of a Maximum-Weight Matroid Base
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global maximum-weight optimality is equivalent to dominance over every base differing by one element.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(S,\mathcal I)\) be a matroid, let \(B\) be a base of \(M\), and let \(w:S\to\mathbb R\). Then
\[
B\text{ is a maximum-weight base}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad w(B')\leq w(B)
\]
for every base \(B'\) such that \(|B'\setminus B|=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid base has maximum total weight if and only if no base obtained by a one-element replacement has greater weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B\text{ is a maximum-weight base}\iff \forall B'\text{ base with }|B'\setminus B|=1,\;w(B')\leq w(B).

children.title: Optimal-Ordering Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relations between objective orderings and optimal base faces.

assumptions_latex: \(r:2^V\to\mathbb R\) is normalized and submodular, with nonempty \(B(r)\).
\(c\in\mathbb R^V\), and \(\Pi(c)\) is the set of permutations nonincreasing in \(c\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal exposed faces and cost-compatible permutations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Pi(c)=\{\pi:c_{\pi(1)}\ge\cdots\ge c_{\pi(n)}\}\), and let \(x^\pi\) be the greedy base of \(\pi\). The face exposed by \(c\) is \(F_c=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in B(r)}c^\top x=\operatorname{conv}\{x^\pi:\pi\in\Pi(c)\}\). Thus every ordering compatible with the weak cost order produces an optimal base, and every optimal point is a convex combination of such bases. If all coordinates of \(c\) are distinct, \(\Pi(c)\) contains one permutation and \(F_c=\{x^\pi\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cost-compatible orderings generate exactly the exposed optimal face; with distinct costs, the unique ordering produces a single optimal greedy base.

knowledge_statements.title: Box-Constrained Polymatroid Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of a box-constrained polymatroid to a translated polymatroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be finite, let \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R_+\) be normalized, nondecreasing, and submodular, and let \(l,u\in\mathbb R^E\) satisfy \(0\le l\le u\) and \(l(A)\le f(A)\) for every \(A\subseteq E\). Define \(c=u-l\),
\[
h(S)=\min_{A:\,S\subseteq A\subseteq E}\bigl(f(A)-l(A)\bigr),
\qquad
g(S)=\min_{T\subseteq S}\bigl(h(T)+c(S\setminus T)\bigr).
\]
Then \(g\) is a polymatroid rank function and
\[
P(f)\cap[l,u]=l+P(g),
\qquad P(f)=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^E:x(S)\le f(S)\text{ for every }S\subseteq E\}.
\]
Consequently, linear optimization over the box intersection reduces to polymatroid greedy optimization over \(P(g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After shifting by a feasible nonnegative lower bound, monotone closure and upper-cap truncation transform a box-constrained polymatroid into a translated polymatroid, permitting greedy linear optimization.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le l\le u\) and \(l(A)\le f(A)\) for every \(A\subseteq E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(f)\cap[l,u]=l+P(g)\).

notation.meaning: Polymatroid defined by the rank inequalities of f.
Sum of the coordinates of l indexed by S.
Monotone closure of the shifted submodular upper function.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional perturbation property for good-pair decompositions used in polymatroid-intersection algorithms; the term good pair is inherited from the surrounding source context.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: M-natural convex intersection theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes a minimizer of a sum through opposing linear tilts, equivalent elementary-exchange tests, an argmin-intersection identity, and an integral-price refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two M-natural-convex functions and a point in both integer domains, the point minimizes their sum exactly when a real price vector makes it minimize the first function tilted by the negative price and the second tilted by the positive price. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid and Rank Formulas from an Intersecting-Submodular Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General subpartition rank formula and its monotone, fully submodular, and polymatroid reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $b:2^S\to\mathbb{R}$ be nonnegative and intersecting submodular. Then $\mathcal I(b)$ satisfies the matroid independence axioms. For every $Z\subseteq S$,
\[
r_b(Z)=\min\left\{\sum_{i=1}^t b(X_i)+\left|Z\setminus\bigcup_{i=1}^tX_i\right|:\{X_1,\ldots,X_t\}\text{ is a subpartition of }S\right\}.
\]
If $b$ is also nondecreasing, the minimum may be restricted to subpartitions of $Z$. If $b$ is fully submodular, then
\[
r_b(Z)=\min_{X\subseteq S}\{b(X)+|Z\setminus X|\}.
\]
If $b$ is a polymatroid function, then
\[
r_b(Z)=\min_{X\subseteq Z}\{b(X)+|Z\setminus X|\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonnegative intersecting-submodular function induces a matroid. Its rank is obtained by minimizing the sum of b over a subpartition plus the number of uncovered elements of Z. Monotonicity restricts the subpartition to Z; full submodularity reduces it to one subset of S; and the polymatroid case restricts that subset to Z.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal I(b)\text{ satisfies the matroid independence axioms, with the stated rank formulas and specializations.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polymatroid Intersection Min–Max Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Min–max characterization and integral attainment for the intersection of two polymatroids.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Edmonds Submodular-Polyhedron Intersection Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the intersection min–max identity and its integral strengthening for integer-valued submodular functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho_1,\rho_2:2^V\to\mathbf R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be submodular with \(\rho_1(\varnothing)=\rho_2(\varnothing)=0\) and \(\rho_1(V),\rho_2(V)<+\infty\). Then \[\max\{x(V)\mid x\in\mathbf P(\rho_1)\cap\mathbf P(\rho_2)\}=\min_{X\subseteq V}\{\rho_1(X)+\rho_2(V\setminus X)\}.\] If both functions are integer valued, then \(\mathbf P(\rho_1)\cap\mathbf P(\rho_2)=\overline{\mathbf P(\rho_1)\cap\mathbf P(\rho_2)\cap\mathbf Z^V}\), and an integer-valued vector attains the maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum total coordinate sum over the intersection of two normalized submodular polyhedra equals the minimum complementary-set sum of their defining functions. For integer-valued functions, the intersection is integral and an integer vector attains the maximum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{x\in\mathbf P(\rho_1)\cap\mathbf P(\rho_2)}x(V)=\min_{X\subseteq V}\bigl(\rho_1(X)+\rho_2(V\setminus X)\bigr),\text{ and if }\rho_1,\rho_2\text{ are integer valued, the intersection is the closure of its integer points and an integer vector attains the maximum.}

knowledge_statements.title: Augmenting Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality matroid-intersection augmentation by shortest exchange paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given matroids \(M_1=(E,\mathcal I_1)\), \(M_2=(E,\mathcal I_2)\), initialize \(I=\varnothing\). For the current common independent set, form the directed exchange graph, add a source adjacent to every \(v\notin I\) with \(I+v\in\mathcal I_1\), and add arcs from every \(v\notin I\) with \(I+v\in\mathcal I_2\) to a sink. If no source–sink path exists, output \(I\). Otherwise choose a shortest path \(P\), replace \(I\) by \(I\triangle V(P)\), and repeat; each iteration increases \(|I|\) by one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly flip membership along a shortest exchange path. Each augmentation enlarges the common independent set by one, and absence of a path certifies optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) are matroids on the same finite ground set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned set \(I\) has maximum cardinality in \(\mathcal I_1\cap\mathcal I_2\).

notation.meaning: Symmetric difference of I with the nonterminal vertices of P.

knowledge_statements.title: Exchange-Graph Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed exchange graph for two matroids at a common independent set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For matroids \(M_i=(E,\mathcal I_i)\) and \(I\in\mathcal I_1\cap\mathcal I_2\), define a directed bipartite graph on \(E\). For \(v\in E\setminus I\) and \(e\in I\), include \(v\to e\) when \(I-e+v\in\mathcal I_1\), and include \(e\to v\) when \(I-e+v\in\mathcal I_2\). Define
\[
S_I=\{v\notin I:I+v\in\mathcal I_1\},\qquad
T_I=\{v\notin I:I+v\in\mathcal I_2\}.
\]
Directed paths from \(S_I\) to \(T_I\) encode alternating feasible exchanges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exchange graph records swaps feasible in each matroid with opposite arc directions; paths between addable elements encode alternating augmentations.
assumptions_latex: \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) are matroids on a common finite ground set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A directed \(S_I\)-to-\(T_I\) path represents an alternating exchange sequence.

notation.meaning: The set obtained by deleting e and adding v.
Elements directly addable in the first and second matroid, respectively.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmentation-Graph Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality correspondence for the matroid-intersection exchange graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_1,M_2\) be matroids on \(E\), let \(I\) be common independent, and construct its exchange graph with terminal sets \(S_I\) and \(T_I\). Then \(I\) is not maximum-cardinality common independent if and only if the graph contains a directed path from \(S_I\) to \(T_I\). For a shortest such path \(P\), the symmetric-difference update \(I'=I\triangle V(P)\) is independent in both matroids and satisfies \(|I'|=|I|+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common independent set is improvable exactly when its exchange graph has an augmenting path; flipping a shortest path produces a common set one element larger.
assumptions_latex: \(M_1,M_2\) are matroids on the same finite ground set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\) is maximum if and only if no directed \(S_I\)-to-\(T_I\) path exists.

knowledge_statements.title: Exchange-Graph Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of exchange-path optimality for arbitrary hereditary systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E=\{a,b,c\}\) and let both hereditary systems have independent family
\[
\mathcal I=\{\varnothing,\{a\},\{b\},\{c\},\{b,c\}\}.
\]
At the common independent set \(I=\{a\}\), neither \(b\) nor \(c\) can be added, so the usual exchange graph has no source and hence no augmenting path. Nevertheless \(\{b,c\}\) is common independent and has cardinality two. Thus the no-augmenting-path certificate fails when hereditary systems lack the matroid exchange axiom.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without matroid exchange, an exchange graph may have no augmenting path at a nonoptimal common independent set.
assumptions_latex: The feasible families are merely hereditary, not matroids.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absence of an augmenting path does not imply maximum cardinality outside the matroid-exchange regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Separation Theory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subset certificate separating a target cardinality from a polymatroid intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_1,f_2\) be normalized, nondecreasing submodular functions on finite \(E\), and let \(k\ge0\). Exactly one of the following holds: there exists \(x\in P(f_1)\cap P(f_2)\) with \(x(E)\ge k\); or there exists \(A\subseteq E\) such that
\[
f_1(A)+f_2(E\setminus A)<k.
\]
The displayed subset is a verifiable discrete separation certificate, since every common point satisfies \(x(E)=x(A)+x(E\setminus A)\le f_1(A)+f_2(E\setminus A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Either a common polymatroid point reaches the target size, or a subset and its complement provide a rank-sum certificate excluding that target.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility of \(x(E)\ge k\) is equivalent to \(f_1(A)+f_2(E\setminus A)\ge k\) for every \(A\subseteq E\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Discrete Sandwich Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise modular separation of a supermodular function from a dominating submodular function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^S\to\mathbb{R}\) be submodular and \(g:2^S\to\mathbb{R}\) be supermodular, with \(g(X)\leq f(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq S\). knowledge_statements.title: Common-Base Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence criterion for a common base of two polymatroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_1,f_2:2^E\to\mathbb R_+\) be normalized, nondecreasing, submodular functions and suppose \(f_1(E)=f_2(E)=r\). Their base polytopes
\[
B(f_i)=\{x\in P(f_i):x(E)=r\}
\]
have a common point if and only if
\[
f_1(A)+f_2(E\setminus A)\ge r
\quad\text{for every }A\subseteq E.
\]
For integer-valued rank functions, a nonempty intersection contains an integral common base.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two equal-rank polymatroids have a common base exactly when every subset-complement pair has combined rank at least the common total rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B(f_1)\cap B(f_2)\ne\varnothing\) if and only if \(f_1(A)+f_2(E\setminus A)\ge r\) for all \(A\subseteq E\).

knowledge_statements.title: Paramodular Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized polymatroid defined by a paramodular lower–upper pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p,b:2^E\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(p(\varnothing)=b(\varnothing)=0\). The pair \((p,b)\) is paramodular when \(p\) is supermodular, \(b\) is submodular, and
\[
b(A)-p(B)\ge b(A\setminus B)-p(B\setminus A)
\quad\text{for all }A,B\subseteq E.
\]
Its paramodular polyhedron, also called a generalized polymatroid, is
\[
Q(p,b)=\{x\in\mathbb R^E:p(S)\le x(S)\le b(S)\text{ for every }S\subseteq E\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A paramodular polyhedron consists of vectors simultaneously bounded by a supermodular lower function and submodular upper function satisfying the cross inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(p,b)=\{x:p(S)\le x(S)\le b(S)\text{ for all }S\subseteq E\}\).

notation.meaning: Paramodular polyhedron determined by p and b.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partition Criterion for Crossing Base-Polyhedron Nonemptiness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers the mutually dual crossing-submodular and crossing-supermodular statements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(b\) be crossing submodular with finite \(b(S)\). Then \(B(b)\ne\varnothing\) if and only if, for every partition \(\{S_1,\ldots,S_t\}\) of \(S\), \(\sum_i b(S_i)\ge b(S)\) and \(\sum_i b(S\setminus S_i)\ge (t-1)b(S)\), equivalently \(\sum_i\bar b(S_i)\ge b(S)\). Dually, if \(p\) is crossing supermodular with finite \(p(S)\), then \(B'(p)\ne\varnothing\) if and only if every such partition satisfies \(\sum_i p(S_i)\le p(S)\) and \(\sum_i p(S\setminus S_i)\le (t-1)p(S)\), equivalently \(\sum_i\bar p(S_i)\le p(S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A base polyhedron of a crossing submodular function with finite value on S is nonempty exactly when two stated partition inequalities hold for every partition of S. Dually, the base polyhedron of a crossing supermodular function is nonempty exactly when the reversed partition inequalities hold.
assumptions_latex: \(b\) is crossing submodular and \(b(S)\) is finite.
\(p\) is crossing supermodular and \(p(S)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B(b)\ne\varnothing\iff[\sum_i b(S_i)\ge b(S)\ \land\ \sum_i b(S\setminus S_i)\ge(t-1)b(S)]\), and dually \(B'(p)\ne\varnothing\iff[\sum_i p(S_i)\le p(S)\ \land\ \sum_i p(S\setminus S_i)\le(t-1)p(S)]\), for every partition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Base-polyhedron representation of a paramodular polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-element lifted representation and submodularity characterization for generalized polymatroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For $S^*=S\cup\{s^*\}$ and the extensions $b^*,p^*$ defined by
\[
b^*(X)=\begin{cases}b(X),&X\subseteq S,\\-p(S-X),&s^*\in X,
\end{cases}\quad
p^*(X)=\begin{cases}p(X),&X\subseteq S,\\-b(S-X),&s^*\in X,
\end{cases}
\]
one has $b^*(S^*)=p^*(S^*)=0$ and
\[
B(b^*)=B'(p^*)=Q(p^*,b^*).
\]
Moreover, $Q(p,b)$ is the projection of $B(b^*)$ obtained by deleting the $s^*$ coordinate, and $b^*$ is submodular if and only if $(p,b)$ is paramodular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The one-element extensions have total-set value zero, and their upper-base, lower-base, and generalized-polymatroid descriptions coincide. Projecting this base polyhedron away from the new coordinate gives the original generalized polymatroid. The extended upper function is submodular exactly when the original pair is paramodular.
assumptions_latex: b^*\text{ and }p^*\text{ are defined by the displayed extension formulas}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b^*(S^*)=p^*(S^*)=0,\quad B(b^*)=B'(p^*)=Q(p^*,b^*),\quad \operatorname{proj}_S B(b^*)=Q(p,b),\quad b^*\text{ submodular}\iff(p,b)\text{ paramodular}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Submodular, supermodular, base, and generalized-polymatroid polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the principal polyhedra and their 0–1 set systems; total-set finiteness is required for base-polyhedron equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For set functions b:2^S\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\} and p:2^S\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}, write x(A)=\sum_{s\in A}x_s. Define P(b)=\{x\in\mathbb R^S:x\ge0,\ x(A)\le b(A)\ \forall A\subseteq S\}, S(b)=\{x:x(A)\le b(A)\ \forall A\subseteq S\}, and, when b(S) is finite, B(b)=\{x\in S(b):x(S)=b(S)\}. Dually define C(p)=\{x\ge0:x(A)\ge p(A)\ \forall A\subseteq S\}, S'(p)=\{x:x(A)\ge p(A)\ \forall A\subseteq S\}, and, when p(S) is finite, B'(p)=\{x\in S'(p):x(S)=p(S)\}. The two-sided system is Q(p,b)=\{x:p(A)\le x(A)\le b(A)\ \forall A\subseteq S\}. Their 0–1 vectors correspond respectively to subsets satisfying the same cardinality inequalities, with total-cardinality equality for B(b) and B'(p). If b is submodular, S(b) is a submodular polyhedron and B(b) a base polyhedron; if p is supermodular, S'(p) is a supermodular polyhedron and B'(p)=B(\bar p). If p is nonnegative and supermodular, S'(p)=C(p), a contra-polymatroid. Moreover S(b)=-S'(-b), with the analogous reflection for base polyhedra. If (p,b) is paramodular, Q(p,b) is a generalized polymatroid with border pair (p,b). If the pair is integral, p is nonnegative, and b(A)\le |A| for every A\subseteq S, its feasible 0–1 sets form a generalized matroid. Every nonempty generalized polymatroid uniquely determines its paramodular border pair, although other nonparamodular representations may exist; by convention the empty polyhedron is also called a generalized polymatroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Upper, lower, base, and two-sided set-function inequality systems define polymatroid-related polyhedra, and their binary points encode the corresponding cardinality-constrained set systems. Submodular upper borders define submodular and base polyhedra; supermodular lower borders define their dual forms, with complement and reflection correspondences. A paramodular lower–upper pair defines a generalized polymatroid. Under integrality, nonnegative lower bounds, and subcardinal upper bounds, its binary feasible sets form a generalized matroid. Nonempty generalized polymatroids have unique paramodular border pairs, while the empty case is included only by convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q(p,b)=\{x\in\mathbb R^S: p(A)\le x(A)\le b(A)\ \forall A\subseteq S\}\text{ is a generalized polymatroid whenever }(p,b)\text{ is paramodular}.

knowledge_statements.title: Semimodular Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted base-polyhedral representation of lower–upper set-function inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E^+=E\cup\{0\}\), choose \(C\in\mathbb R\), and let \(F:2^{E^+}\to\mathbb R\) be normalized and submodular with \(F(E^+)=C\). Its base polyhedron is
\[
B(F)=\{z\in\mathbb R^{E^+}:z(U)\le F(U)\text{ for all }U\subseteq E^+,\ z(E^+)=C\}.
\]
Eliminating \(z_0=C-z(E)\) yields a polyhedron on \(E\) having upper bounds \(z(S)\le F(S)\) and lower bounds \(z(S)\ge C-F((E\setminus S)\cup\{0\})\). This lifted base form is the semimodular representation used for generalized-polymatroid inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A submodular base polyhedron on a ground set with one added element projects to paired upper and lower subset inequalities on the original set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection of \(B(F)\) onto \(E\) has paired submodular upper and complementary lower bounds.

notation.meaning: Ground set E with one added element 0.

knowledge_statements.title: Paramodular-Semimodular Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-element lifting equivalence between paramodular and base-polyhedral descriptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((p,b)\) be paramodular on \(E\), choose \(C\in\mathbb R\), and define \(F\) on \(E^+=E\cup\{0\}\) by
\[
F(S)=b(S)\quad(S\subseteq E),\qquad
F(S\cup\{0\})=C-p(E\setminus S)\quad(S\subseteq E).
\]
Then \(F\) is submodular, \(F(E^+)=C\), and
\[
Q(p,b)=\{z|_E:z\in B(F)\}.
\]
Conversely, every normalized submodular \(F\) with total \(C\) induces \(b(S)=F(S)\) and \(p(S)=C-F((E\setminus S)\cup\{0\})\), producing the same projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A paramodular lower–upper pair has an equivalent submodular base-polyhedron representation after adjoining one element, and either representation reconstructs the other.
assumptions_latex: \((p,b)\) is a normalized paramodular pair on finite \(E\).
\(C\) is a real total assigned to the lifted ground set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(p,b)=\{z|_E:z\in B(F)\}\), with the displayed transformations mutually inverse.

notation.meaning: Restriction of z to coordinates indexed by E.
Total value of the lifted base polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.title: Box Intersections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of generalized polymatroids under intersection with coordinate boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q(p,b)\) be a generalized polymatroid and let \(l,u\in\mathbb R^E\) satisfy \(l\le u\). Define
\[
p_l(S)=\max_{T\subseteq S}\bigl(p(T)+l(S\setminus T)\bigr),
\qquad
b_u(S)=\min_{T\subseteq S}\bigl(b(T)+u(S\setminus T)\bigr).
\]
Whenever the box intersection is nonempty, \((p_l,b_u)\) is a paramodular pair and
\[
Q(p,b)\cap[l,u]=Q(p_l,b_u).
\]
Thus coordinate lower and upper bounds preserve the generalized-polymatroid form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting a generalized polymatroid with a nonempty coordinate box produces another generalized polymatroid whose bounds are explicit max- and min-convolutions.
assumptions_latex: \((p,b)\) is a paramodular pair on finite \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(p,b)\cap[l,u]=Q(p_l,b_u)\).

notation.meaning: Lower-bound max-convolution of p with l.
Upper-bound min-convolution of b with u.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Box intersection of a generalized polymatroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives closure, explicit border-pair formulas, and the integer-data integrality conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $Q=Q(p,b)$ be a generalized polymatroid on $S$ and let $T(f,g)$ be a box. Then $M:=Q\cap T(f,g)$ is a generalized polymatroid. If $M\ne\varnothing$, its border pair $(p',b')$ is given, for every $Z\subseteq S$, by $p'(Z)=\max_{X\subseteq S}\{p(X)-\widetilde g(X-Z)+\widetilde f(Z-X)\}$ and $b'(Z)=\min_{X\subseteq S}\{b(X)-\widetilde f(X-Z)+\widetilde g(Z-X)\}$. If $p,b,f,g$ are integer-valued, then $M$ is integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The intersection of a generalized polymatroid with coordinate-wise lower and upper bounds remains a generalized polymatroid. When nonempty, its border pair has explicit max–min formulas, and integer-valued input data make the intersection integral.
assumptions_latex: M=Q\cap T(f,g)\ne\varnothing\text{ for the border-pair formulas}
p,b,f,g\text{ are integer-valued for the integrality conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is a generalized polymatroid};\quad p'(Z)=\max_{X\subseteq S}\{p(X)-\widetilde g(X-Z)+\widetilde f(Z-X)\};\quad b'(Z)=\min_{X\subseteq S}\{b(X)-\widetilde f(X-Z)+\widetilde g(Z-X)\};\quad M\text{ is integral for integer-valued data}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boxes and planks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines coordinate-bound and total-sum-bound polyhedra, including their unbounded and degenerate cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:S\to\mathbb Z\cup\{-\infty\} and g:S\to\mathbb Z\cup\{+\infty\} satisfy f\le g. The box is T(f,g)=\{x\in\mathbb R^S:f(s)\le x_s\le g(s)\ \forall s\in S\}. If g\equiv+\infty or f\equiv-\infty, this is respectively an upper or lower orthant; T(0,1) is the unit cube U_S. For -\infty\le\alpha\le\beta\le+\infty, the plank is K(\alpha,\beta)=\{x\in\mathbb R^S:\alpha\le\sum_{s\in S}x_s\le\beta\}. If \alpha=\beta, it is the hyperplane K(=\alpha); if exactly one endpoint is infinite, it is the corresponding halfspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A box imposes coordinate-wise lower and upper bounds, allowing infinite endpoints; its special cases include orthants and the unit cube. A plank bounds the sum of all coordinates between two endpoints; equal finite endpoints give a hyperplane, and one infinite endpoint gives a halfspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T(f,g)=\{x:f\le x\le g\},\qquad K(\alpha,\beta)=\left\{x:\alpha\le\sum_{s\in S}x_s\le\beta\right\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Linking Property with Aggregate Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combines componentwise box bounds with lower and upper bounds on the total coordinate sum inside a generalized polymatroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $Q=Q(p,b)$ be a generalized polymatroid on $S$. Suppose there exists $x'\in Q$ with $x'\geq f$ and $\widetilde{x'}(S)\leq\beta$, and there exists $x''\in Q$ with $x''\leq g$ and $\widetilde{x''}(S)\geq\alpha$. Then there exists $x\in Q$ such that $f\leq x\leq g$ and $\alpha\leq\widetilde x(S)\leq\beta$. If $p,b,f,g,\alpha,\beta$ are integral, $x$ may be chosen integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a generalized polymatroid separately contains a point meeting the lower coordinate bounds and total-sum upper bound, and a point meeting the upper coordinate bounds and total-sum lower bound, then it contains a point meeting all those bounds simultaneously. Integral data permit an integral point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Box-and-Plank Feasibility Criteria for Submodular and Supermodular Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives two quantified nonemptiness characterizations for intersections involving componentwise bounds and a plank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $S$ be the ground set. The intersection $S(b)\cap T(f,g)\cap K(\alpha,\beta)$ is nonempty if and only if $\widetilde f(S)\leq\beta$, $\widetilde f(X)\leq b(X)$ for every $X\subseteq S$, and $\widetilde g(X)\geq\alpha-b(S\setminus X)$ for every $X\subseteq S$. Dually, $S'(p)\cap T(f,g)\cap K(\alpha,\beta)$ is nonempty if and only if $\widetilde g(S)\geq\alpha$, $\widetilde g(X)\geq p(X)$ for every $X\subseteq S$, and $\widetilde f(X)\leq\beta-p(S\setminus X)$ for every $X\subseteq S$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A submodular-polyhedron intersection with a coordinate box and a plank is nonempty exactly under the stated upper-box and complementary lower-plank inequalities for every subset. The dual supermodular-polyhedron intersection is nonempty exactly under the corresponding lower-box and complementary upper-plank inequalities.
assumptions_latex: S(b),\ S'(p),\ T(f,g),\text{ and }K(\alpha,\beta)\text{ are the stated submodular/supermodular, box, and plank sets}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}S(b)\cap T(f,g)\cap K(\alpha,\beta)\neq\varnothing&\iff \widetilde f(S)\leq\beta,\ \forall X\subseteq S:\ \widetilde f(X)\leq b(X),\ \widetilde g(X)\geq\alpha-b(S\setminus X);\\ S'(p)\cap T(f,g)\cap K(\alpha,\beta)\neq\varnothing&\iff \widetilde g(S)\geq\alpha,\ \forall X\subseteq S:\ \widetilde g(X)\geq p(X),\ \widetilde f(X)\leq\beta-p(S\setminus X).\end{aligned}
