children.title: Submodular Flow Representation
children.top_down_role: The submodular-system side of the equivalence.

knowledge_statements.title: Submodular Flow Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Base-polyhedral representation of feasible network divergences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite directed graph \(D=(V,A)\), arc bounds \(\ell\le u\), and submodular \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) with \(f(\varnothing)=f(V)=0\), the submodular-flow feasible set is represented by
\[
\mathcal F_f=\{x\in\mathbb R^A:\ell\le x\le u,\ b_x\in B(f)\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(x\in\mathcal F_f\) precisely when its divergence satisfies \(b_x(S)\le f(S)\) for every \(S\subseteq V\); the equality \(b_x(V)=f(V)=0\) is automatic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A submodular flow is an arc-bounded network flow whose divergence vector belongs to a specified submodular base polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F_f=\{x:\ell\le x\le u,\ b_x(S)\le f(S)\ \forall S\subseteq V\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The base-polyhedral formula is internally consistent and representation is the correct role, but no source supports the claimed submodular-flow representation within the named neoflow equivalence container.

children.title: Independent Flow Representation
children.top_down_role: The independence-system side of the equivalence.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Flow Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine polymatroid-base representation of the same boundary vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q\in\mathbb R^V\) be modular and define \(r(S)=f(S)+q(S)\). Suppose \(r\) is normalized and nondecreasing. For every arc vector \(x\), put \(y=b_x+q\). Then the independent-flow representation of the submodular boundary condition is
\[
y\in P(r),\qquad y(V)=r(V).
\]
Indeed, this maximal-sum face of the independence polytope is \(B(r)\), and translation by \(q\) gives \(y\in B(r)\) exactly when \(b_x\in B(f)\). Arc bounds remain unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a modular translation, a submodular divergence condition becomes membership in the maximal-sum face of a polymatroid independence polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_x\in B(f)\iff b_x+q\in P(r)\text{ and }(b_x+q)(V)=r(V)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The modular-translation identity is mathematically plausible, but no source establishes that this maximal-sum polymatroid face is the intended “Independent Flow Representation” in the immutable equivalence context.

children.title: Submodular-to-Independent Conversion
children.top_down_role: Structural translation from submodular flows to independent flows.

knowledge_statements.title: Submodular-to-Independent Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Modular translation from a submodular base constraint to a polymatroid-base face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a finite ground set \(V\), a submodular function \(f\) with \(f(\varnothing)=0\), and a boundary vector \(b\). For each \(v\in V\), choose
\[
q_v\ge \max_{S\subseteq V\setminus\{v\}}\bigl(f(S)-f(S\cup\{v\})\bigr).
\]
Initialize \(r(\varnothing)=0\), set \(q(S)=\sum_{v\in S}q_v\), and define \(r(S)=f(S)+q(S)\) and \(y=b+q\). Output the independent constraints \(y\in P(r)\) and \(y(V)=r(V)\). The construction preserves feasibility because \(y\in B(r)\) exactly when \(b\in B(f)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add sufficiently large modular weights to make the submodular function monotone, then translate the boundary vector and impose the corresponding polymatroid base-face constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b\in B(f)\iff y=b+q\in P(r)\text{ and }y(V)=r(V)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed modular correction does make the translated submodular function nondecreasing, and algorithm is suitable for a conversion leaf. However, no source confirms that this construction is the intended named neoflow conversion.

children.title: Independent-to-Submodular Conversion
children.top_down_role: Structural translation from independent flows to submodular flows.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent-to-Submodular Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse translation from a polymatroid base face to submodular boundary inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a polymatroid rank function \(r:2^V\to\mathbb R_+\), a modular vector \(q\in\mathbb R^V\), and an independent boundary vector \(y\) constrained by \(y\in P(r)\) and \(y(V)=r(V)\). Initialize \(f(\varnothing)=0\), define \(f(S)=r(S)-q(S)\), and set \(b=y-q\). Output the submodular boundary system
\[
b(S)\le f(S)\quad(S\subseteq V),\qquad b(V)=f(V).
\]
Subtracting a modular function preserves submodularity, and the output satisfies \(b\in B(f)\) exactly when the input lies on the base face of \(P(r)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtract the modular translation from both the rank function and boundary vector to recover an equivalent submodular base system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\in B(r)\iff y-q\in B(r-q)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Subtracting the same modular function from the rank function and boundary vector gives the stated base-polyhedron translation, but the record lacks a source tying this operation to the named neoflow conversion.

children.title: Independent Flow Representation
children.top_down_role: The independence-system side of the equivalence.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Flow Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent-polytope constraints applied to incident flow vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=(V,A)\) carry a nonnegative flow \(x\). For each vertex \(v\), let \(r_v^-\) and \(r_v^+\) be polymatroid rank functions on \(\delta^-(v)\) and \(\delta^+(v)\), respectively. The independent-flow representation imposes
\[
x|_{\delta^-(v)}\in P(r_v^-),\qquad x|_{\delta^+(v)}\in P(r_v^+)
\]
for every \(v\), together with the required conservation equations. Thus each local incident-flow vector is independently feasible in its designated polymatroid, while shared arc coordinates couple adjacent vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each incoming and outgoing incident-flow vector must lie in a designated polymatroid independence polytope, with shared arcs and conservation coupling the local systems.
assumptions_latex: Each local rank function is normalized, nondecreasing, and submodular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x|_{\delta^-(v)}\in P(r_v^-)\) and \(x|_{\delta^+(v)}\in P(r_v^+)\) for all \(v\).

notation.meaning: Restriction of x to coordinates in F.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local independence-polytope constraints are coherent, but no source confirms that they constitute the intended independent-flow representation rather than merely a restatement of polymatroidal capacities.

children.title: Polymatroidal Flow Representation
children.top_down_role: The polymatroidal-boundary side of the equivalence.

knowledge_statements.title: Polymatroidal Flow Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subset-inequality expansion of local independent-polytope membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the local rank functions \(r_v^-\) and \(r_v^+\), polymatroidal feasibility has the explicit representation
\[
x(F)\le r_v^-(F)\quad\text{for all }F\subseteq\delta^-(v),\qquad
x(F)\le r_v^+(F)\quad\text{for all }F\subseteq\delta^+(v),
\]
for every vertex \(v\), together with \(x\ge0\) and the specified conservation equations. These subset inequalities are exactly the defining inequalities of the local independence polytopes, so this representation and the local independent-flow representation have identical feasible arc vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expanding each local independence-polytope membership condition yields the subset capacity inequalities defining a polymatroidal flow.
assumptions_latex: Each local rank function is a polymatroid rank function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x|_{\delta^\pm(v)}\in P(r_v^\pm)\iff x(F)\le r_v^\pm(F)\) for every corresponding subset \(F\).

notation.meaning: Either the incoming or outgoing arc set at v.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Expanding local independence-polytope membership into subset inequalities is mathematically standard and representation is the correct kind, but the named equivalence and its local taxonomy sense have no cited support.

children.title: Independent-to-Polymatroidal Conversion
children.top_down_role: Structural translation from independent flows to polymatroidal flows.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent-to-Polymatroidal Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expansion of local polytope membership into submodular subset capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a directed graph \(D=(V,A)\), local rank functions \(r_v^-\) and \(r_v^+\), and independent constraints \(x|_{\delta^-(v)}\in P(r_v^-)\) and \(x|_{\delta^+(v)}\in P(r_v^+)\). For each vertex \(v\), initialize the same incident arc sets and replace each membership constraint by all inequalities
\[
x(F)\le r_v^-(F)\quad(F\subseteq\delta^-(v)),\qquad
x(F)\le r_v^+(F)\quad(F\subseteq\delta^+(v)).
\]
Retain nonnegativity and conservation unchanged. Output the resulting polymatroidal flow system; its feasible arc vectors are identical to those of the input system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace each local independence-polytope membership constraint by its complete family of submodular subset capacity inequalities.
assumptions_latex: Each \(r_v^-\) and \(r_v^+\) is a polymatroid rank function.
The graph and local ground sets are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{ind}}=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{poly}}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conversion is a valid finite constraint expansion, but no source establishes it as the intended named conversion. The record also does not characterize that explicit expansion may contain exponentially many inequalities.

children.title: Polymatroidal-to-Independent Conversion
children.top_down_role: Structural translation from polymatroidal flows to independent flows.

knowledge_statements.title: Polymatroidal-to-Independent Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compression of complete subset capacities into local independence-polytope membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a polymatroidal flow system whose local constraints are \(x(F)\le r_v^-(F)\) for every \(F\subseteq\delta^-(v)\) and \(x(F)\le r_v^+(F)\) for every \(F\subseteq\delta^+(v)\). For each vertex \(v\), initialize the polytopes \(P(r_v^-)\) and \(P(r_v^+)\), remove the expanded subset inequalities, and impose
\[
x|_{\delta^-(v)}\in P(r_v^-),\qquad x|_{\delta^+(v)}\in P(r_v^+).
\]
Retain nonnegativity and conservation unchanged. Output the independent representation, interpreted through rank oracles when the inequality families are implicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compress every complete family of local polymatroid inequalities into membership in the corresponding independence polytope.
assumptions_latex: The supplied subset inequalities use polymatroid rank functions.
Each complete local subset family is represented explicitly or by a rank oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{poly}}=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{ind}}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Compression into polytope-membership notation is formally equivalent when the complete subset families come from the stated rank functions, but neither the named conversion nor the rank-oracle interpretation is sourced.

children.title: Polymatroidal Flow Representation
children.top_down_role: The polymatroidal-boundary side of the equivalence.

assumptions_latex: For each \(v\in V\), normalized nondecreasing submodular functions \(\rho_v^-\) and \(\rho_v^+\) are given on the arcs entering and leaving \(v\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible vectors are precisely the nonnegative flows satisfying all local polymatroid inequalities.

notation.meaning: Set of arcs entering or leaving vertex v
Sum of flow over an arc set F
Local incoming and outgoing polymatroid rank functions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local-capacity polymatroidal flow model; equivalence to submodular flow is treated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A polymatroidal flow representation consists of a vector \(x\in\mathbb{R}_+^A\) satisfying flow conservation \(x(\delta^-(v))=x(\delta^+(v))\) at every designated transshipment vertex and the local inequalities
\[
x(F)\leq \rho_v^-(F)\quad(F\subseteq\delta^-(v)),\qquad x(F)\leq \rho_v^+(F)\quad(F\subseteq\delta^+(v)).
\]
Each function is normalized by \(\rho_v^\pm(\varnothing)=0\), nondecreasing, and submodular. Terminals may instead have prescribed net imbalance. Thus each incident flow vector lies in a polymatroid, while conservation couples the local polymatroids through the arcs of \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polymatroidal flow obeys conservation while every subset of arcs incident to a vertex satisfies a capacity inequality supplied by a local submodular rank function.
knowledge_statements.title: Polymatroidal Flow Representation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the leaf, and the formulation is plausible, but no citation supports the precise local-polymatroid model, terminal treatment, or terminology.

children.title: Submodular Flow Representation
children.top_down_role: The submodular-system side of the equivalence.

assumptions_latex: Arc bounds satisfy \(\ell(a)\leq u(a)\) for every \(a\in A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility is represented by \(\ell\leq x\leq u\) and \(\partial x\in B(f)\).

notation.meaning: Sum of vector coordinates indexed by X

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Base-polyhedron formulation of bounded submodular flows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the base polyhedron
\[
B(f)=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^V:y(X)\leq f(X)\text{ for every }X\subseteq V,\ y(V)=f(V)\}.
\]
A submodular flow is an arc vector \(x\in\mathbb{R}^A\) such that
\[
\ell(a)\leq x(a)\leq u(a)\quad(a\in A),\qquad \partial x\in B(f).
\]
Equivalently, its net-inflow vector satisfies \((\partial x)(X)\leq f(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq V\), together with \((\partial x)(V)=0\). Linear-cost submodular flow additionally minimizes \(\sum_{a\in A}c(a)x(a)\) over this feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded submodular flow is an arc vector whose net-inflow vector belongs to the base polyhedron of a submodular set function.
knowledge_statements.title: Submodular Flow Representation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits and the base-polyhedron formulation is standard in appearance, but the record has no authoritative source for its sign convention, normalization, and exact definition.

children.title: Polymatroidal-to-Submodular Conversion
children.top_down_role: Structural translation from polymatroidal flows to submodular flows.

assumptions_latex: A finite polymatroidal flow instance has rational local rank functions accessible through value oracles.
The representation permits auxiliary vertices and arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constructed submodular-flow instance preserves feasibility and projected arc flows.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary-network conversion preserving the original arc-flow projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A polymatroidal-to-submodular conversion replaces each local incoming or outgoing polymatroid constraint by an auxiliary vertex block and defines a submodular function \(f_{\mathcal P}\) on the enlarged vertex set so that
\[
x\text{ is feasible for }\mathcal P
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists z\text{ feasible for }\mathcal S(\mathcal P)\text{ with }\pi(z)=x.
\]
The construction retains the original arc variables, imposes ordinary bounds on auxiliary arcs, and encodes every local inequality \(x(F)\leq\rho_v^\pm(F)\) as a base-polyhedron inequality for \(f_{\mathcal P}\). For linear objectives placed on original arcs, the extension assigns zero cost to auxiliary arcs, so corresponding feasible solutions have equal objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local polymatroid capacities can be encoded by auxiliary network elements and one submodular base constraint while preserving projected flows and linear costs.
knowledge_statements.title: Polymatroidal-to-Submodular Conversion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source or explicit construction establishes that arbitrary local polymatroid constraints admit the asserted single-base-polyhedron realization while preserving projections and costs. The exact construction is also needed to decide whether this leaf should contain a representation or an algorithm.

children.title: Submodular-to-Polymatroidal Conversion
children.top_down_role: Structural translation from submodular flows to polymatroidal flows.

assumptions_latex: A finite rational submodular-flow instance is given through a value oracle for its defining function.
The representation permits auxiliary vertices, arcs, and local polymatroid constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constructed polymatroidal instance preserves feasibility and projected arc flows.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary-network realization of a global base-polyhedron constraint by local polymatroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A submodular-to-polymatroidal conversion constructs local rank functions on an enlarged directed network such that
\[
x\text{ is feasible for }\mathcal S
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists z\text{ feasible for }\mathcal P(\mathcal S)\text{ with }\pi(z)=x.
\]
The auxiliary variables route the net-inflow vector of the original arcs through local polymatroid constraints whose projection is the base polyhedron \(B(f)\). Original lower and upper bounds remain ordinary arc constraints. When the original objective is linear, original arcs retain their costs and auxiliary arcs receive zero cost; hence projection and extension preserve objective values and optimal solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global submodular base constraint can be realized through auxiliary flows and local polymatroid capacities, preserving original flows and linear objective values.
knowledge_statements.title: Submodular-to-Polymatroidal Conversion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The claimed realization of an arbitrary global base-polyhedron constraint by local polymatroids is specialized and unsupported. A cited construction is required to validate feasibility, projection, objective preservation, and the selected knowledge kind.

assumptions_latex: The arc bounds \(\ell,u\) are finite and satisfy \(\ell\leq u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible submodular flow exists exactly when every displayed cut inequality holds.

notation.meaning: Sum of bound values over an arc set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite bounded base-polyhedron feasibility criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exists \(x\in\mathbb{R}^A\) satisfying \(\ell\leq x\leq u\) and \(\partial x\in B(f)\) if and only if
\[
\ell(\delta^-(X))-u(\delta^+(X))\leq f(X)
\qquad\text{for every }X\subseteq V.
\]
Necessity follows from the bound-implied inequality \((\partial x)(X)\geq\ell(\delta^-(X))-u(\delta^+(X))\) and the base inequality \((\partial x)(X)\leq f(X)\). The reverse implication is the submodular-flow feasibility min–max assertion under the stated finite submodular hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded submodular flow exists exactly when each cut's forced minimum net inflow does not exceed the submodular allowance for that vertex set.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Min–Max Framework

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits the framework leaf, and the displayed cut condition is plausible under the stated net-inflow convention, but the sufficiency theorem has no source. The statement also contains proof-style justification, which must be removed in any sourced revision.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Min–Max Criterion for Disjoint Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility criterion for choosing one base from each of several matroids with all chosen bases pairwise disjoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathbf M_i=(E,\mathcal I_i) have rank function \rho_i for i=1,\ldots,k. Pairwise disjoint bases B_i of \mathbf M_i exist if and only if \[\sum_{i=1}^k\rho_i(E)=\min_{X\subseteq E}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^k\rho_i(X)+|E\setminus X|\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One can choose pairwise disjoint bases, one from each of k matroids on E, exactly when the sum of their full-ground-set ranks equals the stated minimum over all subsets of E.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\exists\text{ pairwise disjoint bases }B_i\text{ of }\mathbf M_i)\iff \sum_{i=1}^k\rho_i(E)=\min_{X\subseteq E}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^k\rho_i(X)+|E\setminus X|\right\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directed subgraph degree-bound feasibility criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes directed subgraphs satisfying simultaneous vertexwise indegree and outdegree intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G=[N;A] be directed, with integer bounds \(0\leq a(x)\leq a'(x)\) and \(0\leq b(x)\leq b'(x)\) for every x\in N. There exists a subgraph H with \(a(x)\leq i_H(x)\leq a'(x)\) and \(b(x)\leq e_H(x)\leq b'(x)\) for all x if and only if, for every X\subseteq N, \[a(X)\leq\sum_{y\in A(X)}\min\{b'(y),|(X,y)|\},\qquad b(X)\leq\sum_{y\in B(X)}\min\{a'(y),|(y,X)|\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directed graph has a spanning subgraph meeting all prescribed indegree and outdegree intervals exactly when both displayed cut-capacity inequalities hold for every vertex subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists H\subseteq G:\ a\leq i_H\leq a',\ b\leq e_H\leq b'\iff\forall X\subseteq N\text{ both displayed inequalities hold}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid Partition Number Formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-density characterization under the necessary exclusion of selfloops.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathbf M=(E,\mathcal I) have rank function \rho and no selfloops, so \rho(\{e\})>0 for every e\in E. The minimum integer k for which E can be partitioned into k pairwise disjoint independent sets is \[\max_{\varnothing\ne X\subseteq E}\left\lceil\frac{|X|}{\rho(X)}\right\rceil.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a matroid without selfloops, the fewest independent sets that partition its ground set equals the maximum, over nonempty subsets, of the ceiling of cardinality divided by rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\{k:E\text{ is partitionable into }k\text{ pairwise disjoint independent sets}\}=\max_{\varnothing\ne X\subseteq E}\left\lceil\frac{|X|}{\rho(X)}\right\rceil

children.title: Cut Certificates
children.top_down_role: Feasibility or obstruction witnesses expressed through network cuts.

assumptions_latex: The data \(D,f,\ell,u\) satisfy the finite bounded submodular-flow hypotheses.
A subset \(X\subseteq V\) is explicitly supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A strict cut violation certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infeasibility witness for bounded submodular flow.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(X\subseteq V\), define
\[
d(X)=\ell(\delta^-(X))-u(\delta^+(X))-f(X).
\]
If \(d(X)>0\), then \(X\) is a cut certificate of infeasibility. Indeed, every vector satisfying the arc bounds has
\[
(\partial x)(X)\geq\ell(\delta^-(X))-u(\delta^+(X))>f(X),
\]
whereas membership of \(\partial x\) in \(B(f)\) requires \((\partial x)(X)\leq f(X)\). The certificate is checked by evaluating one submodular-function value and summing the lower and upper bounds on the two directed sides of the cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vertex set certifies infeasibility when its forced minimum net inflow exceeds its submodular allowance; checking the witness requires one cut calculation.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits, and a positive displayed deficit is a plausible infeasibility witness, but its governing feasibility framework is uncited. The statement includes proof text that should be removed when a sourced record is supplied.

children.title: Tight-Set Certificates
children.top_down_role: Witnesses expressed through saturated submodular constraints.

assumptions_latex: The vector \(y\) belongs to the base polyhedron \(B(f)\).
The subset \(X\subseteq V\) is explicitly supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equality \(y(X)=f(X)\) certifies that the base inequality indexed by \(X\) is active.

notation.meaning: Slack of the base inequality indexed by X

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set witness inside a submodular base polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A set \(X\subseteq V\) is tight for \(y\in B(f)\) when
\[
s_y(X)=f(X)-y(X)=0.
\]
Thus \(X\) certifies an active base-polyhedron inequality by the verifiable equality \(y(X)=f(X)\). Moreover, submodularity implies that the tight-set family
\[
\mathcal T_y=\{X\subseteq V:y(X)=f(X)\}
\]
is closed under union and intersection: if \(X,Y\in\mathcal T_y\), then \(X\cup Y\in\mathcal T_y\) and \(X\cap Y\in\mathcal T_y\). Consequently, unions and intersections of supplied tight witnesses remain valid certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tight-set certificate is a subset whose base-polyhedron inequality holds with equality; tight sets are closed under union and intersection.
knowledge_statements.title: Tight-Set Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits and the active-inequality definition is precise, but no source supports the asserted lattice closure of tight sets in this exact base-polyhedron setting.

children.title: Cut–Tight-Set Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural relations between network cuts and tight constraint families.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Zero exchange capacity is equivalent to the existence of a tight set containing \(u\) and excluding \(v\).

notation.meaning: Maximum feasible transfer from v to u in the base polyhedron
Slack of the inequality indexed by X

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Base-polyhedron exchange obstruction expressed by a separating tight set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the exchange capacity
\[
\kappa_y(u,v)=\sup\{\alpha\geq0:y+\alpha(\chi_u-\chi_v)\in B(f)\}.
\]
Then
\[
\kappa_y(u,v)=\min\{f(X)-y(X):u\in X,\ v\notin X\}.
\]
Accordingly, \(\kappa_y(u,v)=0\) if and only if some tight set \(X\) satisfies \(u\in X\) and \(v\notin X\). Such a set is simultaneously a cut separating the proposed exchange endpoints and a tight base constraint blocking every positive transfer in that direction. Positive minimum slack permits an exchange of any size not exceeding that slack.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proposed base-polyhedron exchange is blocked exactly when a tight set separates its receiving vertex from its giving vertex.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut–Tight-Set Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind is reasonable for the correspondence leaf, but the exchange direction and minimum-slack formula require an authoritative locator. No cited evidence confirms the orientation or zero-capacity equivalence.

assumptions_latex: The vector \(x\) is feasible for a finite linear-cost submodular-flow instance.
The residual structure includes bound-residual arcs and admissible base-polyhedron exchange arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible potential satisfying all reduced-cost inequalities certifies global optimality of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost certificate for linear-cost submodular flow.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A potential \(p:V\to\mathbb{R}\) is an optimality certificate for \(x\) when every residual arc \(e=(u,v)\) in \(R_x\) satisfies
\[
c_x(e)+p(u)-p(v)\geq0.
\]
The residual arcs comprise forward and reverse adjustments allowed by the arc bounds together with directed exchanges allowed by positive base-polyhedron exchange capacity. Because potential terms sum to zero around every directed cycle, the displayed inequalities imply that every residual directed cycle has nonnegative total cost. Under the residual-cycle optimality theorem for linear-cost submodular flow, this certifies that no feasible adjustment decreases the objective and hence that \(x\) is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vertex potential certifies optimality when all ordinary residual and submodular-exchange arcs have nonnegative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Potential Optimality Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits, but the residual exchange arcs and their costs are not defined precisely enough to validate the reduced-cost inequalities. The global-optimality implication depends on an uncited specialized theorem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Potential criterion for continuous M-convex submodular flows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality characterization and fixed-potential description of all optimal flows for the continuous problem MSFP_3.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_a\in\mathcal C[\mathbf R\to\mathbf R]\) for every \(a\in A\), and let \(f\in\mathcal M[\mathbf R\to\mathbf R]\). A feasible flow \(\xi:A\to\mathbf R\) is optimal if and only if there exists \(p:V\to\mathbf R\) such that \(\xi(a)\in\arg\min f_a[\delta p(a)]\) for every \(a\in A\) and \(\partial\xi\in\arg\min f[-p]\). If a potential \(p\) satisfies these conditions for an optimal flow \(\xi\), then a feasible flow \(\xi'\) is optimal if and only if \(\xi'(a)\in\arg\min f_a[\delta p(a)]\) for every \(a\in A\) and \(\partial\xi'\in\arg\min f[-p]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible continuous M-convex submodular flow is optimal exactly when a potential satisfies the arcwise and boundary minimization conditions. A potential certifying one optimum characterizes every other feasible optimum by those same conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\xi\text{ is optimal}\iff\exists p:V\to\mathbf R:\ [\forall a\in A,\ \xi(a)\in\arg\min f_a[\delta p(a)]]\land[\partial\xi\in\arg\min f[-p]]\), and any fixed \(p\) satisfying these conditions for one optimum characterizes all other feasible optima.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Potential criterion and optimal-set structure for integer M-convex submodular flows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Potential optimality certificate, fixed-potential characterization, optimal-boundary geometry, and integer-potential conclusion for the integer problem MSFP_3.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_a\in\mathcal C[\mathbf Z\to\mathbf R]\) for every \(a\in A\), and let \(f\in\mathcal M[\mathbf Z\to\mathbf R]\). A feasible integer flow \(\xi:A\to\mathbf Z\) is optimal if and only if there exists \(p:V\to\mathbf R\) such that \(\xi(a)\in\arg\min f_a[\delta p(a)]\) for every \(a\in A\) and \(\partial\xi\in\arg\min f[-p]\). If such a potential \(p\) certifies an optimal integer flow, then it characterizes every other feasible optimal integer flow by the same conditions. Moreover, \(\partial\Xi^*=\{\partial\xi\mid\xi\text{ is an optimal integer flow}\}\) is an \(M_2\)-convex set. If additionally \(f_a\in\mathcal C[\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z]\) for every \(a\) and \(f\in\mathcal M[\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z]\), then an integer-valued certifying potential exists and the set \(\Pi^*\) of integer-valued optimal potentials is L-convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible integer M-convex submodular flow is optimal exactly when a real potential satisfies the arcwise and boundary minimization conditions. A potential certifying one optimum characterizes all feasible integer optima. Their boundaries form an M2-convex set, and integer-valued costs guarantee an integer optimal potential whose optimal-potential set is L-convex.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi:A\to\mathbf Z\text{ is a feasible integer flow}\)
\(f_a\in\mathcal C[\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z]\quad(a\in A),\ f\in\mathcal M[\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z]\) for the integer-potential and L-convexity conclusions
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\xi\text{ is optimal}\iff\exists p:V\to\mathbf R:\ [\forall a\in A,\ \xi(a)\in\arg\min f_a[\delta p(a)]]\land[\partial\xi\in\arg\min f[-p]]\); also \(\partial\Xi^*\) is \(M_2\)-convex, while integer-valued costs imply an integer certifying potential and an L-convex set \(\Pi^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometry and integrality of continuous M-convex submodular-flow optima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-boundary and dual-potential structure when the continuous problem MSFP_3 attains an optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume that the M-convex submodular-flow problem has an optimal solution, with \(f_a\in\mathcal C[\mathbf R\to\mathbf R]\) for every \(a\in A\) and \(f\in\mathcal M[\mathbf R\to\mathbf R]\). Then \(\partial\Xi^*=\{\partial\xi\mid\xi\text{ is an optimal flow}\}\) is an \(M_2\)-convex polyhedron, and \(\Pi^*=\{p\mid p\text{ is an optimal potential}\}\) is an L-convex polyhedron. If \(f_a\in\mathcal C[\mathbf Z\mid\mathbf R\to\mathbf R]\) for every \(a\) and \(f\in\mathcal M[\mathbf Z\mid\mathbf R\to\mathbf R]\), then \(\partial\Xi^*\) is integral and an integer-valued optimal flow exists. If \(f_a\in\mathcal C[\mathbf R\to\mathbf R\mid\mathbf Z]\) for every \(a\) and \(f\in\mathcal M[\mathbf R\to\mathbf R\mid\mathbf Z]\), then \(\Pi^*\) is integral and an integer-valued optimal potential exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When an optimum exists, the boundaries of optimal continuous flows form an M2-convex polyhedron and the optimal potentials form an L-convex polyhedron. The respective primal and dual integral-data conditions make these polyhedra integral and guarantee an integer optimal flow or integer optimal potential.
assumptions_latex: \(f_a\in\mathcal C[\mathbf Z\mid\mathbf R\to\mathbf R],\ f\in\mathcal M[\mathbf Z\mid\mathbf R\to\mathbf R]\) for the primal-integrality conclusion
\(f_a\in\mathcal C[\mathbf R\to\mathbf R\mid\mathbf Z],\ f\in\mathcal M[\mathbf R\to\mathbf R\mid\mathbf Z]\) for the dual-integrality conclusion
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial\Xi^*\text{ is an }M_2\text{-convex polyhedron and }\Pi^*\text{ is an L-convex polyhedron}\), with primal and dual integrality only under their respective stated hypotheses.

assumptions_latex: The vector \(x\) is feasible for a finite linear-cost submodular-flow instance.
The residual graph represents every bound-feasible and base-feasible elementary adjustment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The flow \(x\) is optimal if and only if its residual graph contains no negative-cost directed cycle.

notation.meaning: Total residual cost of a directed cycle

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-cycle characterization for linear-cost submodular flow.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a directed cycle \(C\) of the residual graph \(R_x\), let
\[
c_x(C)=\sum_{e\in C}c_x(e).
\]
If \(c_x(C)<0\), augmenting by any positive amount not exceeding every ordinary residual capacity and every exchange capacity used by \(C\) produces a feasible flow of strictly smaller cost; thus \(C\) certifies nonoptimality. Conversely, if \(R_x\) has no negative-cost directed cycle, then the residual-cycle optimality theorem implies that \(x\) is optimal. A shortest-path potential witnessing nonnegative reduced costs gives an independently checkable certificate of the latter condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative residual cycle certifies an improving feasible augmentation; absence of every such cycle characterizes optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Cycle Optimality Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A negative cycle can serve as a nonoptimality certificate, but the record principally asserts an if-and-only-if optimality theorem. The residual construction, simultaneous augmentation claim, and exact knowledge kind require authoritative support.

assumptions_latex: The directed graph, arc bounds, and submodular function are integral.
The submodular function is normalized by \(f(\varnothing)=f(V)=0\).
The bounded submodular-flow system is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible system contains an integral flow; an integral linear objective has an integral optimum when its minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integral finite bounded submodular-flow system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{Z}\) be submodular, and let \(\ell,u\in\mathbb{Z}^A\) satisfy \(\ell\leq u\). If
\[
\{x\in\mathbb{R}^A:\ell\leq x\leq u,\ \partial x\in B(f)\}
\]
is nonempty, then it contains a vector \(x\in\mathbb{Z}^A\). More strongly, the bounded submodular-flow polyhedron is integral: every nonempty face contains an integral point. Consequently, for every integral cost vector \(c\in\mathbb{Z}^A\), if the minimum of \(c^\mathsf{T}x\) over this polyhedron is attained, some optimal solution is integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integral bounds and an integer-valued submodular function yield integral feasible and optimal submodular flows whenever the relevant system is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.title: Submodular-Flow Integrality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits the integrality leaf, but no source supports the full integral-polyhedron assertion, especially the stronger claim that every nonempty face contains an integral point under exactly these hypotheses.

children.title: Augmenting Methods
children.top_down_role: Flow methods organized around feasible augmentations.

assumptions_latex: A finite submodular-flow instance and a current rational pseudoflow \(x\) are given.
Residual capacities and base-polyhedron exchange capacities can be computed.
An augmentation target or improving residual walk is specified by the algorithmic variant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each update preserves the enforced constraints and either reduces infeasibility or strictly improves the objective.

notation.meaning: Residual structure at the current vector
Incidence adjustment induced by a residual walk or cycle P

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic residual augmentation template; exact feasibility and optimization variants require separate sourcing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize with the prescribed feasible flow or bound-feasible pseudoflow \(x\). Construct \(R_x\) from ordinary forward and reverse residual arcs and from exchange arcs having positive base-polyhedron exchange capacity. Select an admissible residual path or cycle \(P\) according to the variant: a path joins a current excess to a deficit, while a negative-cost cycle improves a feasible solution. Set
\[
\varepsilon_P=\min\{\text{all ordinary residual capacities and exchange capacities used by }P\},
\qquad x\leftarrow x+\varepsilon_P\chi_P.
\]
Recompute the residual structure and repeat. Stop when all imbalances vanish in the feasibility variant, or when no negative-cost residual cycle exists in the optimization variant; output \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly augment along a residual path to remove imbalance or along a negative residual cycle to reduce cost, respecting every ordinary and exchange capacity.

children.title: Exchange Methods

assumptions_latex: \(E\) is finite and \(f:2^E\to\mathbb Z\) is normalized, submodular, and has nonempty integral base set \(B_{\mathbb Z}(f)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in B_{\mathbb Z}(f)\) and distinct \(i,j\in E\), define \(\gamma_x(i,j)=\max\{\alpha\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}:x+\alpha(e_j-e_i)\in B_{\mathbb Z}(f)\}\). Starting from \(x^0\), repeatedly choose \(i,j\) with \(c_j<c_i\) and \(\gamma_x(i,j)\ge 1\), and replace \(x\) by \(x+e_j-e_i\). Stop when no such pair exists. Because the integral base set is finite and every update strictly decreases \(c^\top x\), the process terminates; the exchange optimality criterion then yields \(c^\top x=\min\{c^\top y:y\in B_{\mathbb Z}(f)\}\).

children.title: Augmentation-Exchange Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Connections between residual augmentations and boundary exchanges.

assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a directed residual network, \(P\) is a directed \(s\)-to-\(t\) path, and every arc of \(P\) has residual capacity at least \(\delta>0\).
The boundary vector is defined by \(\partial\varphi(v)=\varphi(\delta^-(v))-\varphi(\delta^+(v))\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A path augmentation changes the boundary vector by exactly the endpoint exchange \(\delta(e_t-e_s)\).

notation.meaning: Boundary or net-inflow vector of a flow.
Incidence vector of the directed path.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic correspondence between residual path augmentation and boundary exchange.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi'=\varphi+\delta\chi_P\), interpreting reversed residual arcs as decreases on their underlying arcs. At each internal vertex of \(P\), the added inflow and outflow cancel. At \(s\), net outflow increases by \(\delta\), while at \(t\), net inflow increases by \(\delta\). Consequently, \[\partial\varphi'=\partial\varphi+\delta(e_t-e_s).\] Thus augmentation along a residual path realizes an exchange between two boundary coordinates. Conversely, any boundary exchange realized by a feasible residual \(s\)-to-\(t\) flow decomposes into path augmentations, possibly together with circulations that leave the boundary unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Augmenting along a residual path is exactly an exchange between its endpoint boundary coordinates; internal changes cancel.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The boundary identity has the correct sign under the stated net-inflow convention, and property is an appropriate content kind for this correspondence. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut characterization and integrality of maximum independent flows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If the maximum independent-flow problem $P_{MI}$ is feasible, then
\[
\max\left\{\partial\varphi(S^+):\varphi\text{ is an independent flow satisfying (5.98b)--(5.98e)}\right\}
=
\min_{U\subseteq V}\left\{f^+(S^+\setminus U)+\bar c(\Delta^+U)-\underline c(\Delta^-U)+f^-(S^-\cap U)\right\},
\]
where $f^+(X)=+\infty$ when $X\notin\mathcal D^+$ and $f^-(Y)=+\infty$ when $Y\notin\mathcal D^-$. Moreover, if $\bar c,\underline c,f^+,f^-$ are integer-valued, an integral maximum independent flow exists.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximum-Submodular-Flow Min-Cut Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut formula and conditional integrality for maximum submodular flow with a reference arc.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the maximum submodular-flow problem $P_{MS}$ described by (5.133),
\[
\max\left\{\varphi(a_0):\varphi\text{ is feasible in }\mathcal N_S\right\}
=
\min\left\{\bar c(a_0),\min_{\substack{X\in\mathcal D\\a_0\in\Delta^+X}}\left[\bar c(\Delta^-X)-\underline c(\Delta^+X\setminus\{a_0\})+f(X)\right]\right\}.
\]
Moreover, if $\underline c,\bar c,f$ are integer-valued and a maximum submodular flow exists, then an integral maximum submodular flow exists in $\mathcal N_S$.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lexicographic Augmenting-Cycle Maximum Submodular-Flow Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm, unboundedness boundary, and augmentation bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from a feasible submodular flow $\varphi$ with reference arc $a_0$ and vertex numbering $\pi$, repeatedly choose a minimum-arc $\partial^-a_0$--$\partial^+a_0$ path whose internal-vertex numbering sequence is lexicographically least in $\mathcal N_\varphi$. Form the cycle $Q$ with $a_0$, set $\alpha=\min\{c_\varphi(a):a\in Q\}$, and augment $\varphi$ by $\alpha$ along the oriented residual arcs of $Q$. Stop when $\varphi(a_0)=\bar c(a_0)$ or no such path exists; if $\alpha=+\infty$, the flow value is unbounded. Otherwise the resulting flow is maximum, and at most $O(|V|^3)$ augmentations are performed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a feasible flow, repeatedly augment around the cycle formed by the reference arc and the lexicographically shortest minimum-arc auxiliary path. The method returns a maximum submodular flow, detects an arbitrarily large value when the augmentation capacity is infinite, and performs O(|V|^3) augmentations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The algorithm returns a maximum submodular flow or detects unbounded flow value, using }O(|V|^3)\text{ augmentations.}

knowledge_statements.title: Independence–Submodularity Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matroid independence represented through the submodular rank function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a matroid \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\), its rank function \(r(S)=\max\{|I|:I\subseteq S,\ I\in\mathcal I\}\) is normalized, nondecreasing, integer-valued, and submodular. Moreover, \(I\subseteq E\) is independent exactly when its incidence vector satisfies \(\chi_I(S)\le r(S)\) for every \(S\subseteq E\). The integer points of \(B(r)=\{x\in\mathbb R_{ge0}^E:x(S)\le r(S),\ x(E)=r(E)\}\) are precisely the incidence vectors of bases of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid’s independent sets and bases are encoded by inequalities of its submodular rank function; integral base-polytope points are exactly bases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[I\in\mathcal I\iff \chi_I(S)\le r(S)\quad(\forall S\subseteq E),\qquad B(r)\cap\mathbb Z^E=\{\chi_B:B\text{ is a base of }M\}.\]

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role and the matroid-rank correspondence are mathematically standard, but the record has no inspectable citation. In addition, \mathbb R_{ge0} is not the intended nonnegative orthant notation; it should be \mathbb R_{\ge 0}. An authoritative matroid-polytope source is required before the record can be accepted.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility characterization and integrality for submodular flows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility criterion for crossing-submodular demands, its intersecting-submodular specialization, and the integer-valued regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(b\) be crossing submodular with \(b(V)=0\). A feasible subflow exists if and only if, for every \(Z\subseteq V\) and every tree-composition \(\mathcal F\) of \(Z\), \[\varrho_f(Z)-\delta_g(Z)\le \sum_{X\in\mathcal F} b(X).\] If \(b\) is intersecting submodular, it suffices to test partitions \(\mathcal F\) of \(Z\). Moreover, if \(f,g,b\) are integer-valued and a feasible subflow exists, then an integer-valued feasible subflow exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For crossing-submodular b with b(V)=0, feasibility is equivalent to the stated inequality for every subset Z and every tree-composition of Z. For intersecting-submodular b, only partitions need be tested. With integer-valued f, g, and b, feasibility implies integer feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ a feasible subflow}\iff \forall Z\subseteq V\ \forall\mathcal F\in\operatorname{TreeComp}(Z),\ \varrho_f(Z)-\delta_g(Z)\le\sum_{X\in\mathcal F}b(X);\quad b\text{ intersecting submodular}\Rightarrow\mathcal F\text{ may be restricted to partitions};\quad f,g,b\in\mathbb Z\text{-valued and feasible}\Rightarrow\exists\text{ an integer-valued feasible subflow}.

For a submodular \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) with \(f(\varnothing)=f(V)=0\), a separable convex-cost neoflow minimizes \(\sum_{a\in A}\phi_a(x_a)\) over flows satisfying \(l\le x\le u\) and \(\partial x\in B(f)\). In the discrete version, the variables and effective domains are integral and each \(\phi_a\) is discrete convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each arc has its own convex cost, while capacities and a submodular boundary constraint couple the feasible flow globally.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\phi_a\) is proper convex on its arc domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname*{minimize}_{l\le x\le u,\ \partial x\in B(f)}\ \sum_{a\in A}\phi_a(x_a).\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent Arc Fixings and Exchange Exclusions from an Approximate Optimal Potential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequences for every original optimal submodular flow inferred from an optimal potential of an approximate-cost network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\gamma'\) be an \(\alpha\)-approximation of \(\gamma\), and let \(p'\) be an optimal potential in \(\mathcal N'=(G=(V,A),\underline c,\bar c,\gamma',(\mathcal D,f))\). Then every optimal submodular flow \(\varphi\) in \(\mathcal N=(G=(V,A),\underline c,\bar c,\gamma,(\mathcal D,f))\) satisfies: \[\forall a\in A:\quad \gamma_{p'}(a)>\alpha|V|\Longrightarrow\varphi(a)=\underline c(a),\] \[\forall a\in A:\quad \gamma_{p'}(a)<-\alpha|V|\Longrightarrow\varphi(a)=\bar c(a),\] and \[\forall u,v\in V:\quad p'(u)-p'(v)>\alpha|V|\Longrightarrow v\notin\operatorname{dep}(\partial\varphi,u).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every optimum of the original network, a sufficiently positive reduced cost fixes an arc at its lower capacity, a sufficiently negative reduced cost fixes it at its upper capacity, and a sufficiently large potential difference excludes the stated exchange dependency.
assumptions_latex: p'\text{ is an optimal potential in }\mathcal N'
\varphi\text{ is any optimal submodular flow in }\mathcal N
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall a\in A:\ [\gamma_{p'}(a)>\alpha|V|\Rightarrow\varphi(a)=\underline c(a)]\wedge[\gamma_{p'}(a)<-\alpha|V|\Rightarrow\varphi(a)=\bar c(a)];\quad \forall u,v\in V:\ p'(u)-p'(v)>\alpha|V|\Rightarrow v\notin\operatorname{dep}(\partial\varphi,u)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fundamental-Cycle Reduction Procedure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One reduction cycle for a submodular-flow network with a direct-sum submodular system and a strongly connected auxiliary graph on each component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given capacities \(\underline c,\bar c\), a partition \(\mathcal W=\{W^i\mid i\in I\}\), a direct-sum representation \(\mathbf S=\bigoplus_{i\in I}(\mathcal D^i,f^i)\), strongly connected component graphs \(H^i=(W^i,E^i)\), and the tight-arc set \(A^0=\{a\in A\mid\underline c(a)=\bar c(a)\}\), the Fundamental-Cycle procedure: (i) contracts the sets \(W^i\), deletes \(A^0\), chooses a spanning forest, and constructs a potential \(p\) whose reduced costs vanish on the forest; (ii) sets \(M=\max\{|\gamma_p(a)|:a\in A\setminus A^0\}\), stopping if \(M=0\); (iii) otherwise scales costs by \(|V|^2/M\), rounds them to the nearest integers, and solves the resulting approximate submodular-flow problem for an optimal flow and potential \(p'\); (iv) fixes an arc at its upper capacity when its scaled reduced cost under \(p'\) is less than \(-|V|/2\), fixes it at its lower capacity when that reduced cost exceeds \(|V|/2\), deletes every auxiliary arc \((u,v)\) with \(p'(v)-p'(u)>|V|/2\), and decomposes each \(H^i\) into strongly connected components using a maximal chain of upper ideals and the corresponding submodular minors. If \(M=0\), the current feasible submodular flows are exactly the original optimal flows. If \(M\ne0\), the updated data preserve the required input structure and either \(A^0\) strictly increases or the auxiliary arc set \(D\) strictly decreases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The procedure constructs a tree-normalized potential, scales and rounds the remaining reduced costs, solves the approximate submodular-flow problem, then uses the approximate optimal potential to fix persistent arc bounds and split exchange components. A zero scale certifies that every current feasible flow is originally optimal; otherwise the tight-arc set grows or the auxiliary graph loses an arc while the maintained structure is preserved.
assumptions_latex: \underline c,\bar c\text{ are lower and upper capacities}
\mathbf S=\bigoplus_{i\in I}(\mathcal D^i,f^i)\text{ with each summand supported on }W^i
H^i=(W^i,E^i)\text{ is strongly connected for every }i\in I
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M=0\Rightarrow\{\text{current submodular flows}\}=\{\text{original optimal submodular flows}\};\quad M\ne0\Rightarrow\bigl(A^0\text{ strictly enlarges}\ \lor\ D\text{ strictly shrinks}\bigr)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Auxiliary-network algorithm for the neoflow intersection problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative bottleneck augmentation from an initially feasible neoflow.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a feasible flow \varphi in \mathcal{N}, repeatedly construct the auxiliary network \mathcal{N}_{\varphi}. If no directed s^+\!\text{-}s^- path exists, terminate with the current \varphi as a maximum flow. Otherwise choose a shortest directed path P, set \alpha=\min\{c_{\varphi}(a):a\in P\}, augment \varphi by \alpha along forward original arcs of P and decrease it by \alpha along original arcs traversed in reverse, and reconstruct the auxiliary network.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a feasible flow, repeatedly augment by the bottleneck capacity of a shortest source-to-sink path in the auxiliary network. Absence of such a path is the stopping certificate that the current flow is maximum.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal{N}_{\varphi}\text{ is the auxiliary network associated with the current flow}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s^+\not\leadsto s^-\text{ in }\mathcal{N}_{\varphi}\ \Longrightarrow\ \varphi\text{ is a maximum flow in }\mathcal{N}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal–Dual Shortest-Path Algorithm for Independent Assignment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of a prescribed-cardinality independent matching, including its explicit infeasibility stopping condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize M\leftarrow\varnothing. While |M|<k, find in the auxiliary network \mathcal N_M a shortest directed path P from s^+ to s^- relative to w_M, choosing among shortest paths one with the minimum number of arcs. If no such directed path exists, stop and report that no k-independent matching exists. Otherwise update M\leftarrow M\triangle A(P), where A(P) consists of original arcs on P together with matching arcs whose reversals lie on P. Continue until |M|=k.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start with the empty matching. Until its size is k, choose a minimum-arc shortest auxiliary path from the positive source to the negative source and augment by symmetric difference. If no such path exists, report that no k-independent matching exists.
assumptions_latex: k\text{ is the required independent-matching cardinality}
\mathcal N_M\text{ and }w_M\text{ are the auxiliary network and length function associated with }M
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |M|=k\quad\text{or the procedure stops with the conclusion that no }k\text{-independent matching exists}

knowledge_statements.title: M-Convex Submodular Flows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete flow optimization with an M-convex boundary penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(l,u\in\mathbb Z^A\), let \(\phi_a:\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be discrete convex, and let \(g:\mathbb Z^V\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be M-convex. An M-convex submodular-flow problem minimizes \(g(\partial x)+\sum_{a\in A}\phi_a(x_a)\) over \(x\in\mathbb Z^A\) with \(l\le x\le u\). Taking \(g\) as the indicator of the integral points of an integral base polyhedron recovers a submodular boundary constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integral flow pays separable discrete convex arc costs and an M-convex cost on its boundary vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname*{minimize}_{x\in\mathbb Z^A,\ l\le x\le u}\left\{g(\partial x)+\sum_{a\in A}\phi_a(x_a)\right\}.\]

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the M-convex submodular-flow container, but no source supports the precise objective, domain conventions, terminology, or the claim that an indicator of integral base-polyhedron points recovers the stated submodular boundary model.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unit cancellation along a shortest-arc negative cycle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the candidate unit-flow update for the integer M-convex submodular-flow cycle-cancellation method; feasibility and improvement are separate conclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the integer assumptions, let \(\xi\) be feasible and let \(Q\subseteq A_\xi\) be the arc set of a negative cycle having the smallest number of arcs. Define \(\bar\xi:A\to\mathbf Z\) by \(\bar\xi(a)=\xi(a)+1\) if \(a\in Q\cap A_\xi^*\), \(\bar\xi(a)=\xi(a)-1\) if \(\bar a\in Q\cap B_\xi^*\), and \(\bar\xi(a)=\xi(a)\) otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a negative auxiliary-network cycle with the fewest arcs. Increase the original flow by one on each forward residual arc of the cycle, decrease it by one where the cycle uses a reversed arc, and leave all other arc flows unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar c:A\to\mathbf Z\cup\{+\infty\}\), \(\underline c:A\to\mathbf Z\cup\{-\infty\}\), and \(f\in\mathcal M[\mathbf Z\to\mathbf R]\).
\(Q\) is a negative cycle of \((G_\xi,\ell_\xi)\) having the smallest number of arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar\xi=\xi+\chi_{Q\cap A_\xi^*}-\chi_{\{a\in A:\bar a\in Q\cap B_\xi^*\}}\) is the unit cycle-cancellation update.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimality and Integrality for M-Convex Submodular Flows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes optimal feasible flows by reduced arc costs and an M-convex boundary minimization condition, with primal and dual integrality conclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A feasible flow \(\varphi\) for (MSF) is optimal if and only if there exists \(p\in(\mathbb R^V)^*\) such that, for every \(a\in A\),
\[\gamma_p(a)>0\Rightarrow\varphi(a)=\underline c(a),\qquad \gamma_p(a)<0\Rightarrow\varphi(a)=\bar c(a),\]
\[\partial\varphi\in\operatorname{argmin}(g-p),\qquad \gamma_p(a)=\gamma(a)+p(\partial^+a)-p(\partial^-a).\]
Moreover, if \(\underline c\) and \(\bar c\) are integer-valued, \(g\) is domain-integral, and an optimal flow exists, then an integral optimal flow exists. If additionally \(g\) is co-domain-integral and \(\gamma\) is integer-valued, then \(p\) may be chosen integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible M-convex submodular flow is optimal exactly when a vertex potential makes every positive-reduced-cost arc attain its lower capacity, every negative-reduced-cost arc attain its upper capacity, and the flow boundary minimize the potential-tilted M-convex function. Integral capacities and domain-integrality yield an integral optimum when an optimum exists; co-domain-integrality and integral costs also allow an integral potential.
assumptions_latex: \text{For primal integrality: }\underline c,\bar c\text{ are integer-valued, }g\text{ is domain-integral, and an optimum exists}
\text{For integral }p:\ g\text{ is co-domain-integral and }\gamma\text{ is integer-valued}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-Dual Algorithm for MSFP2 with Dual Integrality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded primal-dual scheme using the source-defined feasibility conditions, deficit sets, maxSFP subproblem, and minimum-cut potential update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize $(\xi,p)\in\mathbb R^A\times\mathbb Z^V$ satisfying (10.54) and (10.59). If $D_\xi(v)=\varnothing$ for every $v\in V$, return $(\xi,p)$ as optimal. knowledge_statements.statement_title: M-Convex Submodular Flow Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a capacitated flow model with linear arc costs and an M-convex objective term applied to the flow boundary vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,A)\), let \(\underline c:A\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) and \(\bar c:A\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be lower and upper capacity functions, let \(\gamma:A\to\mathbb R\), and let \(g\) be an M-convex function on \(\mathbb R^V\). The M-convex submodular flow problem is
\[
\min_{\varphi}\left\{\sum_{a\in A}\gamma(a)\varphi(a)+g(\partial\varphi):\underline c(a)\leq\varphi(a)\leq\bar c(a)\ \text{for every }a\in A\right\}.
\]
This problem generalizes the submodular-flow problem and hence the neoflow problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An M-convex submodular flow minimizes linear arc costs plus an M-convex function of the flow boundary, subject to lower and upper arc capacities. It generalizes submodular flow and neoflow.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{(MSF)}:\quad\min_{\underline c\leq\varphi\leq\bar c}\left\{\sum_{a\in A}\gamma(a)\varphi(a)+g(\partial\varphi)\right\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Auxiliary network for a real-valued M-convex submodular flow
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines residual-capacity arcs, feasible boundary-exchange arcs, their lengths, and negative cycles for the real-valued problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible flow \(\xi:A\to\mathbf R\) in \(\mathrm{MSFP}_2\), with \(f\in\mathcal M[\mathbf R\to\mathbf R]\), define \(G_\xi=(V,A_\xi)\), where \(A_\xi=A_\xi^*\mathbin{\dot\cup}B_\xi^*\mathbin{\dot\cup}C_\xi\), \(A_\xi^*=\{a\in A\mid \xi(a)<\bar c(a)\}\), \(B_\xi^*=\{\bar a\mid a\in A,\ \underline c(a)<\xi(a)\}\), and \(C_\xi=\{(u,v)\mid u\ne v,\ \exists\alpha>0:\partial\xi-\alpha(\chi_u-\chi_v)\in\operatorname{dom}_{\mathbf R}f\}\). Set \(\ell_\xi(a)=\gamma(a)\) on \(A_\xi^*\), \(\ell_\xi(\bar a)=-\gamma(a)\) for reverse arcs associated with \(a\in A\), and \(\ell_\xi(u,v)=f'(\partial\xi;-\chi_u+\chi_v)\) on \(C_\xi\). The pair \((G_\xi,\ell_\xi)\) is the auxiliary network, and a directed cycle of negative total length is a negative cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The auxiliary network of a feasible real-valued M-convex submodular flow contains forward and reverse residual-capacity arcs and feasible boundary-exchange arcs. Their lengths are the signed linear arc costs and the appropriate directional derivatives of the boundary cost. A negative cycle has negative total length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((G_\xi,\ell_\xi)\) and its negative cycles are defined by the stated residual-capacity and boundary-exchange construction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate scaling algorithm for MSFP2 with dual integrality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Problem-specific scaling algorithm for M-convex submodular flow, using bounded integer-potential minimization and a primal-dual solver at each scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Start with a feasible flow $\xi_0\in\mathbf{R}^A$ and an integer-valued potential $p_0\in\mathbf{Z}^V$ satisfying (10.59); define $\widetilde\gamma,\widetilde f,\widetilde g$, and set $p^*:=\mathbf0$, $K:=\max_{a\in A}|\widetilde\gamma(a)|$, and $\alpha:=2^{\lceil\log_2K\rceil}$. While $\alpha\ge1$, find $p\in\mathbf{Z}^V$ minimizing $\widetilde g^\alpha(p)-\langle p,\partial\xi\rangle$ subject to $2p^*\le p\le2p^*+(n-1)\mathbf1$; solve $\operatorname{MSFP}_2$ for $(\gamma,f)=(\lceil\widetilde\gamma/\alpha\rceil,\widetilde f^{\langle\alpha\rangle})$ by the primal-dual algorithm initialized with $(\xi,p)$ to obtain an optimal $(\xi^*,p^*)\in\mathbf{R}^A\times\mathbf{Z}^V$; then set $\xi:=\xi^*$ and $\alpha:=\alpha/2$. If $\alpha<1$, stop and return $(\xi,p_0+p^*)$, which is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize from a feasible flow and an integer potential satisfying condition (10.59), with a power-of-two scale determined by the largest transformed arc magnitude. At each scale, minimize the stated scaled objective over the prescribed integer box, solve the scaled MSFP2 instance with the primal-dual algorithm, update the flow, and halve the scale. When the scale is below one, the returned flow and shifted potential are optimal.
assumptions_latex: \text{The MSFP}_2\text{ instance has the stated dual-integrality setting}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha<1\implies (\xi,p_0+p^*)\text{ is optimal}.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Integrality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonintegral boundary data can destroy integral-flow feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the one-arc digraph \(s\to t\) with \(0\le x_a\le1\) and require \(\partial x=(-1/2,1/2)\). The unique feasible flow is \(x_a=1/2\), so the feasible polyhedron contains no integral flow despite integral arc bounds. Thus an integrality theorem for submodular flows cannot generally survive replacement of an integral base-polyhedron boundary by arbitrary nonintegral boundary data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integral capacities do not guarantee an integral flow when the prescribed boundary or its defining polyhedron is nonintegral.
assumptions_latex: The boundary convention is net inflow.
The boundary requirement is the singleton \(\{(-1/2,1/2)\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\{x\in[0,1]:\partial x=(-1/2,1/2)\}=\{1/2\},\qquad \{1/2\}\cap\mathbb Z=\varnothing.\]

Net inflow boundary vector ordered as s,t.

knowledge_statements.title: Incompatible Boundary Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous boundary requirements may make a flow model infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=\{s,t\}\) and impose simultaneously \(\partial x\in B_1\) and \(\partial x\in B_2\), where \(B_1=\{(-1,1)\}\) and \(B_2=\{(1,-1)\}\). Each boundary system is individually feasible on a suitably oriented unit arc, but \(B_1\cap B_2=\varnothing\). Consequently no flow on any common network can satisfy both boundary requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two individually meaningful boundary systems can be mutually inconsistent because their feasible boundary sets have empty intersection.
assumptions_latex: Both boundary constraints apply to the same boundary vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[B_1\cap B_2=\varnothing\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \{x:\partial x\in B_1,\ \partial x\in B_2\}=\varnothing.\]

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The empty-intersection implication is directly correct and the failure_boundary kind fits, but the record has no evidence for treating these singleton sets as the relevant boundary systems in the local neoflow model. A source defining or analyzing simultaneous boundary systems is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonseparable-Cost Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cross-arc interactions cannot generally be encoded by unary arc costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On two binary arc variables, let \(C(x_1,x_2)=x_1x_2\). If \(C\) admitted a separable representation \(C(x_1,x_2)=\phi_1(x_1)+\phi_2(x_2)\), its rectangular mixed difference would vanish. Instead, \(C(1,1)-C(1,0)-C(0,1)+C(0,0)=1\). Hence this interaction cost cannot be represented by separable arc costs without auxiliary variables or an enlarged state space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A genuine interaction between arc variables defeats a sum of unary arc costs unless the formulation is enlarged.
assumptions_latex: A separable representation uses only one unary function per variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[C(x_1,x_2)=x_1x_2\ne\phi_1(x_1)+\phi_2(x_2)\quad\text{for all choices of }\phi_1,\phi_2.\]

notation.meaning: Joint cost of the two arc variables.
Hypothetical unary cost for variable i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mixed-difference calculation correctly rules out a sum of two unary costs for the displayed binary interaction, and failure_boundary is the proper kind. No source is supplied for the broader modeling conclusion concerning auxiliary variables or enlarged state spaces.

children.title: Value-Oracle Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Limitations arising from oracle-based access to flow-model data.

knowledge_statements.title: Value-Oracle Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete recovery from a value oracle has exponential query cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be accessible only through a value oracle returning \(f(S)\) for a queried \(S\subseteq V\). Any procedure required to output the complete value table of an otherwise unrestricted member of a full-dimensional submodular family must query every unqueried coordinate in the worst case. Thus complete explicit recovery requires \(2^{|V|}\) oracle calls, although particular optimization tasks may require far fewer calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A value oracle avoids storing an exponential table, but reconstructing the entire submodular function still requires exponentially many queries.
assumptions_latex: The oracle returns one exact set value per call.
The required output is the complete table.
The admissible submodular family has freely perturbable coordinates locally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Q_{\mathrm{table}}(|V|)\ge 2^{|V|}.\]

notation.meaning: Worst-case oracle queries needed to recover the complete table.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A complexity bound is appropriate for this container, but the exact 2^{|V|} lower bound depends on a formally specified oracle, algorithmic, and admissible-family model. The phrase freely perturbable coordinates locally does not by itself establish the adversarial indistinguishability claim, and no source is cited.

children.title: Explicit Representation Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Limitations arising from explicit descriptions of feasible structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Representation Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tabular representation grows exponentially with the ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An explicit value-table representation of \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) stores one entry for each subset of \(V\). Therefore it contains exactly \(2^{|V|}\) entries. If every value is represented with \(b\) bits, the table occupies \(2^{|V|}b\) bits, before indexing overhead. Submodularity inequalities restrict admissible tables but do not change the number of coordinates in this representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Listing every value of a set function uses exponentially many entries, even when the function is submodular.
assumptions_latex: The representation lists every subset value explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{size}_{\mathrm{table}}(f)=2^{|V|}b\ \text{ bits}.\]

notation.meaning: Bits used for one stored function value.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counting statement is correct for the explicitly stipulated full value table, and complexity_bound fits the terminal container. However, there is no citation or explicit standard-field rationale record supporting the representation-complexity claim; the review flag alone is not an inspectable rationale.

children.title: Succinct Encoding Limits
children.top_down_role: Failure boundaries associated with compressed input descriptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Succinct Encoding Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Succinct encodings necessarily cover only structured subfamilies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n=|V|\), a code of length at most \(p(n)\) bits has at most \(2^{p(n)+1}-1\) distinct codewords. Consequently, if a finite class \(\mathcal F_n\) of exactly represented submodular functions satisfies \(|\mathcal F_n|>2^{p(n)+1}-1\), no injective encoding of all members can use at most \(p(n)\) bits. Polynomial-size formulas therefore require structural restrictions and cannot encode every sufficiently large finite submodular class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial-bit format has too few codewords to represent every member of a sufficiently large submodular family exactly.
assumptions_latex: Exact representation requires distinct functions to have distinct decodings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[|\mathcal F_n|>2^{p(n)+1}-1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\max_{f\in\mathcal F_n}\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{enc}(f))>p(n).\]

notation.meaning: Finite class of submodular functions on an n-element ground set.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-codeword counting implication is valid for injective exact binary encodings, and failure_boundary fits the container. The claimed consequence for submodular functions remains conditional because no sufficiently large submodular family is instantiated or sourced, and the meaning of formula encoding is not formalized.

children.title: Generalized Submodular Domains
children.top_down_role: Classical extensions of set-function submodularity to restricted families, lattices, signed domains, and multilabel domains, including their polyhedral and optimization interfaces.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strongly Polynomial Optimization over Two Crossing-Submodular Extended Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the prescribed total-coordinate sum and linear objective stated in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C_1,\mathcal C_2\) be crossing families of subsets of \(S\), let \(f_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathbb Q\) be crossing submodular for \(i=1,2\), and let \(k\in\mathbb Q\) and \(w\in\mathbb Q^S\). A vector \(x\in EP_{f_1}\cap EP_{f_2}\) satisfying \(x(S)=k\) and maximizing \(w^\top x\) can be found in strongly polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two rational crossing-submodular functions on crossing families, a maximum-weight point in the intersection of their extended polyhedra with prescribed total coordinate sum can be found in strongly polynomial time.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C_1,\mathcal C_2\) are crossing families of subsets of \(S\).
\(f_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathbb Q\) is crossing submodular for \(i=1,2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A maximizing \(x\in EP_{f_1}\cap EP_{f_2}\) with \(x(S)=k\) can be found in strongly polynomial time.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partition characterization for two intersecting supermodular requirements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient pointwise bounds for partition classes to meet every specified set with the required multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C_1\) and \(\mathcal C_2\) be intersecting families of subsets of \(S\), let \(g_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathbb Z\) be intersecting supermodular for \(i=1,2\), and let \(k\in\mathbb Z_+\) with \(k\ge 1\). Then \(S\) can be partitioned into classes \(L_1,\ldots,L_k\) satisfying \(g_i(U)\leq |\{j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}:L_j\cap U\neq\varnothing\}|\) for every \(i\in\{1,2\}\) and \(U\in\mathcal C_i\) if and only if \(g_i(U)\leq\min\{k,|U|\}\) for every such \(i\) and \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partition of S into k classes satisfying both intersecting-supermodular coverage systems exists exactly when each requirement is no greater than k and no greater than the cardinality of its set.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal C_1,\mathcal C_2\text{ are intersecting families of subsets of }S
g_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathbb Z\text{ is intersecting supermodular for }i=1,2
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\exists\text{ a partition of }S\text{ into }L_1,\ldots,L_k:\ \forall i\in\{1,2\},\ \forall U\in\mathcal C_i,\ g_i(U)\leq |\{j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}:L_j\cap U\neq\varnothing\}|\bigr]\iff\bigl[\forall i\in\{1,2\},\ \forall U\in\mathcal C_i,\ g_i(U)\leq\min\{k,|U|\}\bigr]

knowledge_statements.title: Intersecting-Submodular Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Submodularity restricted to pairs having nonempty intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite and let \(\mathcal F\subseteq2^V\) satisfy \(X\cap Y,X\cup Y\in\mathcal F\) whenever \(X,Y\in\mathcal F\) and \(X\cap Y\ne\varnothing\). A function \(f:\mathcal F\to\mathbb R\) is intersecting-submodular if, for every such intersecting pair, \(f(X)+f(Y)\ge f(X\cap Y)+f(X\cup Y)\). No inequality is required by this definition for disjoint pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting submodularity imposes the usual submodular inequality only on domain pairs with nonempty intersection.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\) is closed under union and intersection of intersecting pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[X,Y\in\mathcal F,\ X\cap Y\ne\varnothing\quad\Longrightarrow\quad f(X)+f(Y)\ge f(X\cap Y)+f(X\cup Y).\]

notation.meaning: Intersecting family forming the function domain.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the terminal container and the displayed inequality is internally consistent. Because conventions differ between functions on all of 2^V and functions on intersecting families with closure assumptions, an authoritative source with a precise definition locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Crossing-Submodular Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-family formulation with closure required only for crossing pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite. Two sets \(X,Y\subseteq V\) cross if \(X\cap Y\), \(X\setminus Y\), \(Y\setminus X\), and \(V\setminus(X\cup Y)\) are all nonempty. A pair \((\mathcal F,f)\), where \(\mathcal F\subseteq 2^V\) and \(f:\mathcal F\to\mathbb R\), is a crossing-submodular system if, whenever \(X,Y\in\mathcal F\) cross, both \(X\cap Y,X\cup Y\in\mathcal F\) and \[f(X)+f(Y)\ge f(X\cap Y)+f(X\cup Y).\] No inequality or closure condition is imposed on noncrossing pairs by this definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A crossing-submodular system is closed under union and intersection of crossing members, and its function satisfies the submodular inequality on exactly those pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X,Y\in\mathcal F\) crossing implies \(X\cap Y,X\cup Y\in\mathcal F\) and \(f(X)+f(Y)\ge f(X\cap Y)+f(X\cup Y)\).

notation.meaning: restricted family of subsets of the ground set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no citation establishes the intended crossing convention or the combined closure-and-inequality terminology.
